spell-amphisbaena-call-greater: This spell is identical to lesser amphisbaena call, but can be used to enhance summon monster or summon nature's ally I-IX. The amphisbaena snakes stay one additional round for each caster level.
spell-amphisbaena-call-lesser: While this spell is in effect, the caster can give the amphisbaena serpent template to any snakes he then summons using the summon monster or summon nature's ally I-V spells. It also extends the duration the summoned amphisbaena snakes can stay by 1 round per two caster levels.
spell-aura-of-venom: This spell surrounds you with a translucent, writhing aura of purple and red. Any living creature that comes within 5 ft. of you must save or become poisoned. The poison inflicts 1d4 damage to a random ability (Strength, Dexterity, etc.), with no secondary damage. Creatures that successfully save are immune to the aura's poison for the duration of the spell. All snakes and creatures that are immune to poison are unaffected by the spell.
spell-balor-wings: This spell is similar to fly, except that the caster grows bat-wings made of fire that he may use to attack when not flying, and maximum flying speed is 30 ft. with no penalty for carrying a heavy load. Attacks with both wings count as a single melee touch attack with a 10 ft. reach and a +1 bonus to hit. The wings cause a total of 1d8 points of fire damage +1 point per two caster levels (maximum +15). Since the wings are immaterial, your Strength modifier does not apply to the damage.
spell-black-swords:
This spell summons a trio of black, eldritch longswords. Each sword occupies a 5 ft. square (though other creatures can move through their space without penalty), and each sword must always be adjacent with at least one other sword. The swords strike at any opponents within range, as you desire, starting in the round that they appear. Each sword attacks its designated target once each round on your turn. Its attack bonus is equal to your base attack bonus with an additional +2 enhancement bonus. Each sword is considered a magic, cold iron weapon and deals 1d8+2 points of slashing damage, with a threat range of 20 and a critical multiplier of ×2.

The swords always strike from your direction. They get no flanking bonuses and cannot help a combatant get one. If any of the swords go beyond the spell range from you, go out of your sight, or you are not directing them, all three return to you and hover.

Each round after the first, you can use a standard action to switch one of the swords to a new target. If you do not, each sword continues to attack the previous round's target.

Each sword's AC is 12 (10, +0 size bonus for Medium object, +2 deflection bonus), has a hardness of 10 and has 5 hit points.

If an attacked creature has spell resistance, the resistance is checked the first time one of the swords strikes it. If the sword is successfully resisted, that sword is dispelled. If not, the sword has its normal full effect on that creature for the duration of the spell.
spell-bleeding-wounds:
This spell causes all creatures who fail their save to become susceptible to bleeding. For the duration of the spell, if the targets suffer any physical wounds or have any existing physical wounds, they bleed for 1d4 damage per round. Targets suffer only 1d4 bleed damage per round, regardless of how many wounds they have. However, if the target is suffering from an additional bleed effect (such as from a monster's bleed ability or a bleeding critical hit), the bleed damage from this spell stacks with the bleed damage from the other effect. Multiple castings of this spell on the same targets do not stack.

The bleeding can be stopped by a successful DC 17 Heal skill check. A remove curse or heal spell will also stop the spell's bleeding damage, as will healing the affected creature back up to its maximum hit points.

Once the spell ends, the bleeding damage from the spell ends.
spell-bleeding-wounds-3pp-rite-publishin: This spell accelerates injuries with small amounts of negative energy. By infecting the target with a minute amount of negative energy, this spell accelerates injuries to living tissue and makes wounds more serious. Even a small knife wound can be made to bleed more heavily, the flesh around it turning septic as the spell works its dark magic. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack to strike your target. A creature struck by this ray takes an additional 1d6 damage every time it takes damage from any weapon or non-energy damage source (so not from spells that deal energy damage, or breath weapons) for the duration of the spell. This spell has no effect on undead, constructs, plants or oozes.
spell-brilliant-energy-weapon: This spell transforms an existing melee weapon into a brilliant energy weapon. This spell cannot be cast on a natural weapon, such as an unarmed strike.
spell-chariot-of-the-warlord: This spell summons a light chariot pulled by a single war trained horse that can only be used by you. The chariot has all the normal qualities of a light chariot. Use the light chariot rules. You are considered proficient to drive the chariot and count as having 5 ranks in the Handle Animal skill, unless you already have more ranks in a chariot driving skill. The chariot and horse appear together where you designate but cannot act without a chariot rider. The chariot and horse cannot be summoned into an environment that cannot support them. The horse cannot be unhitched from the chariot. The chariot and horse radiate an aura of magic, but otherwise function as normal objects and creatures.
spell-chill-grasp: This spell functions like chill touch, inflicting 1d6 points of damage from negative energy and 1d2 points of Strength damage. In addition, for every 2 points of Strength damage inflicted, the caster gains a +1 enhancement bonus to a random physical ability score (Str, Dex, or Con). This bonus lasts for 1 round per two levels (10 rounds maximum). A touched undead creature takes no damage of either sort, but it must make a successful Will saving throw or flee as if panicked for 1d4 rounds + 1 round per caster level.
spell-clutch-of-stone:
The caster conjures clutching stone arms with clawed hands out of the ground, which must be made of earth or stone. This spell only affects Tiny, Small, Medium or Large targets that are in contact with the ground or are no more than 3 ft. above it. Every creature within the area of the spell is the target of a combat maneuver check made to grapple each round at the beginning of your turn, including the round that the spell is cast. Creatures that enter the area of effect are also automatically attacked. The claws do not provoke attacks of opportunity. The claws have a BAB of +5, a Strength of 16, CMB +8, and CMD 18. Roll only once for the entire spell effect each round and apply the result to all creatures in the area of effect. The claws do not inflict damage but always attempt to maintain their grapple. If the claws succeed in grappling a foe, that foe gains the grappled condition. Each round thereafter, the claws attempt to maintain their grapple. The claws cannot initiate grapple maneuvers such as move, damage, pin, etc., as their only purpose is to hinder foes by giving them the grappled condition. If a target escapes the claws' grapple, it is immune to further grapple attempts from the claws for the duration of the spell.

This spell is countered by move earth, soften earth and stone, and transmute rock to mud.
spell-cone-of-venom: This spell causes venom to spew from your mouth and extend outward in a cone. The poison deals 1d6 points of temporary Constitution damage immediately and another 1d4 points of temporary Constitution damage 1 minute later. Each instance of damage can be negated by a Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 your caster level + your Int or Wis modifier).
spell-cone-of-vitriol: This spell creates a spray of incredibly corrosive acid, originating at your hand and extending outward in a cone. The acid deals 1d4 points of damage per caster level (maximum 20d4). In addition, up to 1d4 of those who fail their save must make a second save or they are affected as if by a rusting grasp spell. The caster determines one object or item carried by each target to be affected by the rusting grasp.
spell-corruption-of-entropy:
This spell conjures a squirming mass of incorporeal purple tentacles which appear to writhe around everything within the area of effect. The tentacles remain for 1 minute per level of the caster. Those within the area of effect must make a Will save each round they are within it or suffer from temporary physical mutation and/or insanity. All physical mutations caused by the spell (and their benefits and penalties) disappear when the victim leaves the area of effect or when the spell ends. Insane victims act randomly each round, even if they somehow leave the area, as indicated by the following table:

d10

Mutation/Insanity Effect

1-2 Run from the mass of tentacles for 1d4 rounds

3-4 Sprout two 5 ft. long, feebly waving tentacles from neck or shoulder (no effect other than visual), and Despair for 1 round as the crushing despair spell

5 Skin wrinkles and withers, and suffer fatigue for 1d4 rounds

6 Sprout extra eyes all over body (gain All-Around Sight) and do nothing for 1 round

7 Sprout an extra arm/leg* (gain +1 on CMD) and attack the nearest creature (friend or foe) for 1 round. *If wearing Medium or heavy armor, the extra limb magically grows through the armor without damaging it.

8 Sprout an extra eye (gain +1 on visual Perception checks) and laugh uncontrollably for 1 round, as the hideous laughter spell

9 Attack self for 1 round

10 Sprout horns* (gain natural gore attack for 1d4 damage), become enraged (as the rage spell) and attack the nearest creature (friend or foe) for 3 rounds, but still suffer fatigue for three rounds after.

*If wearing a helm, the horns magically grow through the helm without damaging it.

Once a victim makes a successful save, he cannot be affected by the tentacles again, unless by a new casting of the spell. When the spell expires, the tentacles vanish and all victims are restored to normal.
spell-create-vampiric-serpent:
This spell allows you to create a vampiric serpent from the corpse of any corporeal snake or snake-like creature. Examples of snake-like creatures might include a couatl, marilith demon, naga, xocouatl, or any creature whose anatomy includes a snake's head or body. Merely having tentacles, slit eyes, scales or a forked tongue is not enough to qualify a creature as snake-like.

Vampiric serpents are not automatically under the control of their animator. If you are capable of commanding undead, you may attempt to command the vampiric serpent as it forms. This spell must be cast at night.

Material Component: A clay pot filled with grave dirt and another filled with brackish water. This spell must be cast on a dead snake's body. You must place a black onyx gem worth at least 50 gp per HD of the undead to be created into the mouth or eye socket of the corpse. The magic of the spell turns the gem into a worthless shell.
spell-curse-of-the-epidemic: This spell causes a single living creature to become a carrier of diseases, poison, and curses. A creature under this curse may pass along any disease, poison, or curse they suffer from or contract while this spell is in effect. Any living creature that comes within 5 ft. of the carrier of curse of the epidemic must make a save vs. each of the carrier's current diseases, poisons, or curses, although they get a +2 bonus on each save. A creature can only contract one of the bearer's diseases, poisons or curses. If they fail to save vs. more than one, roll randomly to determine which one they actually contract. The effects passed on by the carrier take effect immediately. A maximum of three living creatures may be affected by the carrier. It is not possible for the carrier to pass along curse of the epidemic itself. A dispel magic or remove curse spell will remove the effects passed on by the carrier, even if they normally cannot be removed by those means. Unlike bestow curse, curse of the epidemic can be removed from the carrier with dispel magic as well as remove curse.
spell-curse-of-the-mandrake: This spell can only be cast in wilderness areas and areas with an earth or unworked stone floor, and causes dozens of thrashing, shrieking mandrake roots to erupt from the ground or partially wriggle and crawl out of cracks or underneath stones. The mandrakes emit a constant shriek that deafens all those within the area (and for 1d4 rounds after leaving it) unless they succeed on a Fortitude save. Non-deafened creatures must save each round they are within the area. In addition, each round a creature moves more than 5 ft. through the area of the thrashing mandrakes, it is subject to a trip attack by the mandrakes (CMB equal to your caster level +2). The mandrakes do not provoke attacks of opportunity. Only one trip attack may be made against each target per round. The mandrakes can make no other attacks. The mandrakes created by this spell cannot be damaged, but they can be dispelled as normal. In addition, the following spells will affect them: control plants, command plants, diminish plants, or antiplant shell will silence and immobilize them for the duration of the spell being cast. Any one of these spells may also serve as a counter to curse of the mandrake. A silence spell silences the mandrakes but does not prevent them from making trip attacks.
spell-dagger-swarm-greater: This spell functions the same as lesser dagger swarm, but the swarm's fly speed is 35 ft., its swarm attack inflicts 2d6 damage, and its wound effect causes 1d4 damage.
spell-dagger-swarm-lesser: You summon a 10 ft. swarm of floating, diminutive, magic daggers (treated as a swarm of bats with construct traits, a fly speed of 30 ft., and a swarm attack of 1d6 with wounding), which attacks all creatures within its area. (You may summon the swarm so that it shares the area of other creatures.) Each round you may spend a standard action to direct the swarm to move up to 25 ft., otherwise it pursues the nearest target.
spell-dagger-swarm-minor: You summon a small 5 ft. x 5 ft. swarm of floating, diminutive, magic daggers (treated as a small swarm of bats with a fly speed of 20 ft. and a swarm attack that inflicts 1d4 damage, but with no 128 bat swarm wounding effect), which attacks all creatures within its area. (You may summon the swarm so that it shares the area of other creatures.) If no targets are within its area, the swarm attacks or pursues the nearest creature as best it can. The caster has no control over its target or direction of travel.
spell-dancing-weapon: This arcane spell is identical to spiritual weapon, but the caster's Intelligence or Charisma modifier (whichever is higher) is used instead of Wisdom. The caster must choose a weapon appropriate for his alignment.
spell-dancing-weapon-3pp-orphaned-bookwo:
The touched weapon hovers around you and attacks nearby enemies. Once per round as a free action, the weapon can attack an adjacent creature you designate.

The weapon's attack roll is equal to your caster level + your spellcasting ability modifier. The damage dealt by the weapon is its base damage plus your spellcasting ability modifier. Any enhancement bonuses or effects the weapon has apply to attack and damage as well.

This weapon cannot make attacks of opportunity and remains in your square. Like spiritual ally, this weapon does not gain any additional bonuses to attack or damage from positioning, your feats, class abilities, or actions.
spell-deadly-nightshade:
This spell causes areas of normal vegetation (grasses, briars, bushes, creepers, thistles, vines, and so on) within close range (25 feet + 5 feet per caster level) to sprout poisonous deadly nightshade plants. At your option, the area can be a 10-foot-radius circle, a 15-foot-radius semicircle, or a 20-foot-radius quarter circle. The plants are 3 ft. high, and the entire area provides partial concealment for anything within it.

The plants seem possessed by an evil sentient spirit and lean hungrily toward any living thing entering their area, feebly entwining their poisonous stems and leafs around them. This does not entangle opponents, but the plants' touch inflicts deadly necromantic poison that deals 1d2 Constitution damage per round for 5 rounds. A successful Fortitude save negates. Poisoned creatures can make a Fortitude save each round to negate the damage and end the affliction. Creatures that make their save become immune to the plants' poison for the duration of the spell. The nightshade plants are not undead, but if a consecrate or positive energy burst is used in their area they will die within three rounds.

Diminish plants or antiplant shell counter this spell.

If a living creature of 3HD or less dies within the area of effect while the nightshade exists, the plants immediately infest it, and there is 25% chance it rises in 1d4 rounds as an uncontrolled zombie. However, only one such zombie may be created by the spell. When the spell ends, or as soon as a zombie is created, all nightshade plants in the area of effect wither and crumble into harmless dust.
spell-deathly-familiar:
This spell temporarily turns an undead creature of 4 hit dice or less that is currently under your control (via the animate dead, control undead or command undead spells or the Command Undead feat) into your familiar. This works even if your class cannot normally have a familiar. Only one undead creature can be your familiar at a time. This spell has no effect if you already have a familiar of any kind.

For the duration of the spell, the undead familiar gains the following benefits:
spell-devouring-cloud:
This spell functions like fog cloud, except the cloud roils with morphing images of large, cloudy, monstrous or skeletal maws. These maws can extend out to grab any creature of size Large or smaller within 5 ft. of the exterior edge of the cloud and instantly drag them into one of the center squares of the cloud (Reflex negates). Once in the center of the cloud, the maws let go and the creature is free to act on its next turn, but it is still subject to the vision impairing effects of the cloud. Targets that have been previously grabbed are immune to further grab attempts by the cloud. Likewise, once a target successfully saves, it is immune to further dragging attempts by the cloud. The cloud can only attempt to drag one creature per round. If more than one creature is within range of the cloud maws, randomly determine which one the cloud maws attempt to grab. The caster is not immune to dragging attempts by the cloud. Creatures with spell resistance who resist the spell are immune to its vision impairing effects as well as its grab attempts.

A moderate wind (11+ mph) disperses the cloud in 4 rounds; a strong wind (21+ mph) disperses the cloud in 1 round.

This spell does not function underwater.
spell-divine-light-weapon: This spell functions like brilliant energy weapon, but the weapon is also endowed with divine light that that gives it an additional +2 to hit and damage. Unlike a normal brilliant energy weapon, weapons endowed with this spell can also affect undead, constructs, and objects, but only inflict half damage against them. This spell cannot be cast on a natural weapon, such as an unarmed strike.
spell-dread-cyclone: This spell is identical to the whirlwind spell, but for the following: a dread cyclone can affect creatures up to size Huge; if the dread cyclone exceeds the spell's range, it moves randomly for 1d6 rounds; those who fail their save and are suspended by the winds suffer 1d10 damage per round.
spell-drowning: Drowning causes water to fill the target's mouth and nose, causing it to slowly suffocate. See the drowning rules in the core rulebook, but the target suffers a –4 penalty to its Constitution for determining how long it can hold its breath. Also, spellcasters must make a Concentration check (DC 22) each round in order to cast spells. A dispel magic, water breathing or a spell that negates the need to breathe cast on the target will negate drowning. Drowning has no effect on creatures that do not need to breathe, such as constructs, elementals, oozes, plants, and undead.
spell-elemental-hands: This spell is identical to burning hands, but produces a fan of electricity (air), magma (earth) fire (fire) or ice (water), depending on the caster's elemental specialty. Storm knights may use either electricity or ice, and earth lords use magma. winter warlocks use ice. Fire and magma can cause flammable materials to burn similar to burning hands, and electricity and ice cause those who fail to save to suffer –1 to attack rolls and skill checks for 1 round.
spell-explosive-meteor: This spell is similar to a fireball, but instead of a ball of fire it is a tiny meteor that detonates, showering the area with chunks of rock that inflict 1d6 bludgeoning damage per level (max 8d6). The meteor has no heat and will not set fire to combustibles or melt metals as a fireball would.
spell-eye-of-the-storm:
This spell creates a 20 ft. diameter, 10 ft. high cylinder of hurricane winds (75-174 mph) centered on the caster, rotating in a clockwise or counterclockwise direction (caster's choice). The caster is immune to the wind.

The area of wind moves with the caster, but only if he moves no more than 5 ft. per round. If he moves faster than this, the spell immediately ends as soon as he begins his movement.

The hurricane-strength winds extinguish all flames in the area and may fell small trees. Eye of the storm can do anything a blast of hurricane force would be expected to do. It can create a lashing spray of sand, dust, or water, extinguish a large fire, break windows and shutters, rip off awnings, hangings or light wooden roofs, keel over small and even some Medium-sized boats, and blow gases or vapors to the edge of the range.
spell-fire-gems: This spell is identical to fire seeds, except that 25 gp topazes are substituted for acorn grenades, and 50 gp rubies are substituted for holly berry bombs.
spell-fire-shield-greater:
This spell is identical to fire shield, except the maximum damage is +20. In addition, the caster may also release two flaming spheres from the flames surrounding him. The flaming spheres inflict either fire or cold damage, depending on the type of fire shield used. Each sphere must be used against different targets, all of which must be within 30 ft. of each other. Directing both spheres requires concentration.

Arcane Material Component: A bit of phosphorus for the warm shield; a live firefly or glowworm or the tail portions of four dead ones for the chill shield. A bit of tallow, a pinch of brimstone, and a dusting of powdered iron for the flaming spheres.
spell-flame-wave: This spell causes a sudden burst of fire to emanate from the caster, dealing 1d8 damage for every two caster levels (5d8 at level 10, 6d8 at level 12, 7d8 at level 14, etc., to a maximum of 10d8) to everything within range. The caster is immune.
spell-flaming-weapon:
This spell temporarily transforms an existing melee weapon into a flaming weapon.

This spell cannot be cast on a natural weapon, such as an unarmed strike or bite.
spell-freezing-doom:
This spell encases the target in supernaturally cold ice, up to 1 inch thick per caster level. The target is completely immobilized and suffers 3d6 points of cold damage each round. Each round, the target may make a Strength check vs. DC 20 + 1 per three caster levels to break out of the ice. However, if the target breaks free, it is severely numbed and frostbitten and suffers 1d6 points of Strength and Dexterity damage that lasts for 1 round per two caster levels.

If the ice takes 50 points of fire damage or more in 1 round, it melts.
spell-freezing-wall:
This spell creates an anchored wall of ice that emanates a deep, freezing cold. The wall cannot be formed in an area occupied by creatures or objects. The wall is 1 inch thick per caster level. One side of the wall emanates bone-chilling cold, dealing 2d6 points of cold damage to creatures within 10 feet and 1d6 points of cold damage to those past 10 feet but within 20 feet. The wall deals this damage when it appears and on your turn each round to all creatures in the area. In addition, the wall deals 2d6 points of cold damage +1 point of cold damage per caster level (maximum +20) to any creature touching it. Each 10-foot length of wall has 5 hit points per inch of thickness. Creatures can hit the wall automatically. A section of wall whose hit points drop to 0 is breached. If a creature tries to break through the wall with a single attack, the DC for the Strength check is 15 + caster level.

Even when the ice has been broken through, a sheet of frigid air remains. Any creature stepping through it (including the one who broke through the wall) takes 1d6 points of cold damage +1 point per caster level (no save).

If any 10-foot length of wall takes 25 points of fire damage or more in 1 round, that length melts. (Do not divide fire damage by 4, as normal for objects.) Freezing wall can be made permanent with a permanency spell. A permanent freezing wall that is extinguished by fire damage becomes inactive for 10 minutes, then reforms at normal strength.
spell-ghost-serpent-greater: This spell is identical to lesser ghost serpent, except the snake or snake-like creature affected by the spell remains incorporeal when it attacks, and its incorporeal bite also inflicts poison. It may also use its constriction ability, if it has one. All the creature's bite and constriction attacks are incorporeal touch attacks.
spell-ghost-serpent-lesser: This spell was created to allow snakes to serve as assassins that can easily penetrate a target's lair. This spell temporarily 132 gives any snake or snake-like creature the incorporeal subtype, allowing it to move through walls and objects. However, the creature may not use any poison or constriction abilities when in ghost serpent form. The creature immediately becomes corporeal when it attacks, ending the spell.
spell-ice-blade: This arcane spell is similar to flame blade, but creates a cold, blue flame that causes cold damage. It cannot ignite objects, but it can freeze up to 1 cubic foot of water per caster level. Using the blade to freeze water requires a standard action. Creatures made of water are immune to the freezing effect.
spell-incendiary-cloud-greater: This spell is similar to incendiary cloud, but also causes heat metal on targets within the cloud. Targets must make Reflex saves to reduce the amount of fire damage caused by the cloud (as stated under the incendiary cloud spell description) and must also make Will saves to escape the heat metal effect. The number of targets that may be affected by the heat metal is one creature per two levels, no two of which can be more than 30 ft. apart; or 25 lb. of metal/level, all of which must be within a 30-ft. circle. If a target successfully saves against the heat metal, it may not be affected by it again, even if it re-enters the incendiary cloud (though it could still suffer fire damage).
spell-infernal-pillar-of-fire: This spell is similar to levitate, except the caster levitates just above a 5 ft. wide pillar of fire. The caster may levitate to a maximum height of 20 ft. The pillar inflicts 2d6 damage to anything touching it or passing through it (Reflex save for half).
spell-lightning-shield: This spell is identical to fire shield but produces and protects against lightning, instead of fire and the damage it deals is electrical (shock).
spell-luminous-retribution: This spell functions identically to the daylight spell. Additionally, all evil creatures and those associated with darkness suffer a –1 penalty to attacks, saves, and ability checks while within the illuminated area. Qualifying evil creatures of darkness include shadows, shadow demons, evil creatures with light sensitivity, light blindness, light vulnerability, evil creatures that can see in darkness, and any creatures that possess an innate spell-like or supernatural ability that creates darkness (such as a black dragon's or babau demon's darkness ability).
spell-luminous-wrath:
This spell functions identically to the luminous retribution spell. Additionally, if this spell is used in an area occupied by magic darkness, it acts as a dispel magic against it.

If it successfully dispels the darkness, it also causes 1d4 damage per level of the caster (max 10d4), no save (although spell resistance applies), to the creature that created the darkness, provided the creature is within 100 ft. of the object radiating this spell. Only one dispel attempt is allowed per casting of this spell.
spell-magma-spray: A cone of magma and molten rocks shoots from your fingertips. Any creature in the area of the takes 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 12d6), half of which is fire damage and half of which is bludgeoning. A successful Reflex saves halves the damage. Flammable materials ignite if the magma touches them, as if hit by burning oil. A character can extinguish burning items as a full-round action.
spell-magma-wave: A cone of thick, heavy magma and molten rock shoots from your fingertips. Any creature in the area of the takes 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 15d6), half of which is fire damage and half of which is bludgeoning. A successful Reflex saves halves the damage. Size Medium or smaller victims who fail their save and are touching the ground must make a second save or be knocked down and trapped under a 4 ft. high carpet of cooling magma and are unable to act until the magma vanishes one round later. Flammable materials ignite if the magma touches them, as if hit by alchemist's fire. A character can 134 extinguish burning items as a full-round action, provided he is able to act.
spell-major-tremor:
This spell has the same effects as the earthquake spell but with the following differences: Concentration checks to cast spells are made vs. DC 17 + spell level.

Cave, Cavern, or Tunnel: This spell causes chunks of rock to fall from the roof, dealing 5d6 damage to any creature caught under the partial cave-in (Reflex half DC 15). Cliffs: Vertical slabs of rock crumble from the cliffside, causing a minor landslide that travels horizontally as far as it fell vertically. Any creature in the path sustains 5d6 points of damage (Reflex half DC 15). Open Ground: Fissures created by the spell are 10 ft. deep. Reflex DC 18 to avoid falling into one. Victims falling into fissures are not killed when they grind shut, but suffer 2d6 points of damage each round until they are freed. Victims can attempt to drag themselves out of shut fissures by making a DC 18 Strength check each round. Structure: Most structures standing on open ground sustain major damage and have a 50% chance of partially collapsing each round, dealing 5d6 points of damage to those caught within or beneath the rubble (Reflex half DC 15). River, Lake, or Marsh: Fissures drain the depth of the water down to half, but otherwise have no effect. At the end of the spell rest of the body of water rushes in and restores the area to its original depth.
spell-malific-meteor: The caster summons a small meteor and sends it hurtling toward a single foe. The meteor travels in a straight line and the caster must have line of sight to the target. On impact, the target suffers 1d6 bludgeoning damage per two levels of the caster (max 8d6), Reflex save for half. Targets who fail their save are knocked back 10 feet away from the caster and fall prone. If an obstacle prevents the target from getting knocked back, the target and the obstacle each take 1d6 points of damage, and the target stops in the space adjacent to the obstacle. Flying targets are knocked back but do not fall.
spell-minor-tremor: This spell has the same effects as the earthquake spell but with the following differences: Concentration checks to cast spells are made vs. DC 14 + spell level.
spell-mummification-of-nine: This spell inflicts 1d6 negative levels on a single, living humanoid creature of at least 8 hit dice. A creature slain by the spell rises as a mummy after nine days. Mummies created in this way must serve the caster for a period of nine days (as if they were affected by a command undead spell), after which they crumble to dust. The caster is immune to the despair ability of his mummies as long as they are under his control. The caster may never have more than twice his level in hit dice of mummies under his control. Thus, a 14th level caster could control up to twenty-eight hit dice of mummies at one time. If the caster exceeds this limit, all the mummies under his control are instantly freed, seek to slay him, and will not stop until nine days have passed or he is slain.
spell-numbing-wind-greater: As lesser numbing wind, but the maximum nonlethal damage is 12d4. Dexterity loss is 1d6+1 additional point per two caster levels (maximum 1d6+8).
spell-numbing-wind-lesser: This spell creates a numbingly cold wind that originates from you, affecting all creatures in its path. Creatures within the path must save or suffer 6d4 points of cold nonlethal damage. Those who fail to save also take a penalty to Dexterity equal to 1d4+1 additional point per two caster levels (maximum 1d4+5). The subject's Dexterity score cannot drop below 1. This Dexterity loss lasts for 1 round per caster level.
spell-phantom-draught-horse:
This spell functions like phantom steed, but conjures a strong, stocky work horse that is not easily hindered and can also be used in battle, though it is not as fast or mobile as a phantom steed, and does not last as long. The mount is war trained and will attack if ordered to do so by its rider. Animals normally shun it, but may still attack it. Only the caster may ride the phantom draught horse, and he gains +2 bonus on Ride checks while doing so.

Spd 40; AC 17, touch 13, flat-footed 13 (+4 Dex, –1 size, +4 natural); hp 25 + 3 per caster level (2d8+12), BAB +4*; Atk: 2 hooves +3 (1d6+2), bite +3 (1d4+2); Fort +9, Ref +7, Will +5; Init +4; Senses low-light vision; Str 20, Dex 18, Con 22, Int 2, Wis 17, Cha 11; Base Atk +4; CMB +7; CMD 21 (25 vs. trip); Feats: Endurance, Improved Sunder, Iron Will, Power Attack, Run; Tricks: Combat Training, Heavy Labor, Down, Heel, Stay

*The mount's base attack bonus increases by +1 for every three caster levels after level six (e.g., +5 at caster level nine, +6 at caster level twelve, etc.).

If it loses all its hit points, the phantom draught horse disappears. It can bear its rider's weight plus up to 20 pounds per caster level.

These mounts gain certain powers according to caster level. A mount's abilities include those of mounts of lower caster levels.
spell-phantom-warhorse:
This spell functions like phantom steed, but conjures a fierce destrier trained for battle, though it is not as fast or mobile as a phantom steed, and does not last as long.

The mount is war trained and will attack if ordered to do so by its rider. Animals normally shun it, but may still attack it. Only the caster may ride the phantom warhorse, and he gains +2 bonus on Ride checks while doing so. The caster gains the ability to use the Mounted Combat and Ride-by Attack feats while riding the warhorse.

Spd 50; AC 18, touch 14, flat-footed 13 (+5 Dex, –1 size, +4 natural); hp 25 + 3 per caster level (2d8+10), BAB +5*; Atk: 2 hooves +4 (1d6+2), bite +4 (1d4+2); Fort +8, Ref +8, Will +3; Init +4; Senses low-light vision; Str 20, Dex 20, Con 21, Int 2, Wis 17, Cha 11; Base Atk +5; CMB +7; CMD 21 (25 vs. trip); Feats: Endurance, Improved Sunder, Power Attack, Run; Tricks: Combat Training, Down, Heel, Stay

*The mount's base attack bonus increases by +1 for every three caster levels after level six (e.g., +6 at caster level nine, +7 at caster level twelve, etc.). If it loses all its hit points, the phantom warhorse disappears. It can bear its rider's weight plus up to 10 pounds per caster level.

These mounts gain certain powers according to caster level. A mount's abilities include those of mounts of lower caster levels.
spell-plague-scythe-of-entropy: Plague scythe of Entropy summons a magical +2, two-handed scythe of serrated black bone infused with disease. The scythe is usable only by the caster, who is considered to be proficient with the weapon. The scythe deals damage as a greatsword and struck targets must make a DC 17 Fortitude save or be affected by a contagion spell. The disease is determined randomly and lasts for 1d6 rounds. Victims can only be affected by one disease at a time – multiple hits do not inflict multiple diseases.
spell-plague-whip: This dreaded spell allows the caster to draw forth a shadowy, plague-infested whip from the essence of the netherworld that shudders and writhes as if it were a living thing. The caster is considered proficient with the whip, which functions exactly like a normal whip, providing reach and the ability to perform disarm and trip maneuvers. The caster gains a +1 competence bonus on attack roll and damage rolls with the whip per two caster levels (max +5). Despite being made of shadowy essence, the whip can be damaged or destroyed like a normal whip. A target struck by the whip must make a Fortitude save or suffer 1d2 points of ability damage to a random ability. Targets who fail their save also appear to be disfigured by a horrible pox, bulging tumors, and infected welts and give off a repulsive smell. Even targets with a high armor bonus that are normally immune to whip damage must save or suffer the effects. A target that successfully saves is immune to further ability damage from the whip, for the duration of the spell. The whip vanishes if the caster drops it. Only the caster can use the whip.
spell-plague-wind: This spell creates a strong force of wind with the same effects as a gust of wind, accompanied by images of flying, moaning spectral skeletons and diseased corpses wrapped in tattered funeral shrouds. Targets that fail their save are not only affected by the force of the wind, but are also infected with one of the following random diseases: 1) cackle fever, 2) filth fever, 3) mindfire, 4) red ache, 5) shakes, or 6) slimy doom. The disease is contracted immediately (the onset period does not apply). Use the disease's listed frequency and save DC to determine further effects.
spell-pyre-of-flames: Pyre of flames immolates the target in a pyre-like wreath of flames and smoke, dealing 10d6 points of damage on the first round, 5d6 on the second round, 3d6 on the third round, and 2d6 on the fourth round. The target only makes one save. If it fails, it takes full damage each round as the pyre of flames moves with it. Additionally, the flames produce thick, oily, eye-stinging black smoke that reduces the target's visibility to 20 ft. on the first round, 40 ft. on the second round, 60 ft. on the third round, and 80 ft on the fourth round. True seeing or a spell that allows the target to see through smoke will negate the reduced visibility.
spell-quicksand: This spell temporarily transforms an existing area of earth, mud, clay or sand (but not stone) into a magical quicksand pit. Creatures in the area are allowed a Reflex save to escape before the area is turned into quicksand. For details about the effects of quicksand, see the core rules. The quicksand created by the spell is thicker and harder to spot, so all the Swim and Strength DCs required to escape from it are increased by 3. When the spell ends, the area returns to normal.
spell-rain-of-sparks: Rain of Sparks You are adept at making sparking torches that spew forth unbelievable amounts of sparks. Prerequisite(s): Pyro sparking torch special torch attack class feature, base attack bonus +5. Benefit(s): Your sparking torch special torch attack ability inflicts 1d6 point of damage per two levels, instead of 1d4, and the radius increases to 10 ft.
spell-ravenous-fire: Ravenous fire is identical to chain lightning, except it deals fire damage instead of electrical damage.
spell-ray-of-ice: A ray of frigid air and ice shoots from your pointing finger. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack with the ray to deal damage to a target. The ray deals 1d6 points of cold damage per caster level (maximum 10d6).
spell-scaly-skin: The creature appears to be covered with patterned scales and gains resistance to blows, cuts, stabs, and slashes. This spell is otherwise identical to stoneskin, except that the damage reduction is only 5/adamantine and it prevents a total of 5 points of damage per level (maximum 70 points) before the spell is discharged.
spell-screaming-gate:
This spell creates an otherworldly, screaming, horrific gateway.

The ghostly gate is a 10 ft. wide by 10 ft. high, incorporeal, four-sided Gothic arch adorned with rusted spikes and chains, its stained surface studded with staring, twitching, and bloodshot eyeballs. Inside the gate is a shifting scene alternating between swirling blackness and nightmarish, alien landscapes. The gate itself trembles and sways and periodically emits blood-chilling screams of terror. The gate grants concealment (20% miss chance) to those behind it but does not impede movement through it.

Even though the gate is incorporeal, it must be created in a 10 ft. space with enough room to contain it. It may not be created in a space already occupied by creatures.

A maximum of one creature may be affected by the screaming gate each round. Any creature (including the caster) of size large or smaller within 10 ft. of the screaming gate gets sucked in (Fort DC negates) and instantly dimension doored in a random direction, 30 ft. away from the gate. A creature that successfully resists getting sucked into the gate is immune to all its effects for the duration of the spell, and can see through the gate as if it were not there. If dimension doored creatures arrive in a place that is already occupied by a solid body, they take no damage and are shunted to a random open space on a suitable surface within 30 ft. of the gate. If no such space is available, they are returned to their original space.

Creatures that are dimension doored must also make a Will save or suffer one of the following insanity effects for 1d4 rounds after reappearing (roll 1d4): 1- Minor amnesia: A victim suffering from minor amnesia cannot remember his name or past, suffers a -4 penalty on all skill checks, and has a 30% chance of spell failure.

2- Minor phobia: The victim suffers from fear of doors, gates, dimension door, teleportation, and creatures from other planes. If the victim is within 30 ft. of any of these things, he must make a Will save or become frightened. 3- Psychosis: The victim suffers from psychotic urges. The GM selects one random creature (friend or foe) within 30 ft. of the victim. The victim will attack that target to the best of his ability. 4- Paranoia: The victim is convinced the world is out to get him and receives a -2 penalty on all saves, and will resist all advice, suggestions, assistance, healing, or beneficial spells used on him by anyone. He will also refuse to enter combat, but will attack those who attack him.

Creatures get a new save each round to throw off the insanity effects. Each time an insane creature is sucked again into the gate and fails to resist the insanity effect, re-roll on the insanity table and roll the new insanity duration. A creature that successfully makes its insanity Will save is immune to further insanity effects from the gate for the duration of the spell. Mindless creatures and creatures immune to fear and mind-affecting magic are immune to the insanity effects, though they may still be dimension doored.
spell-sentient-serpent: Sentient serpent transforms a normal snake into a sentient serpent (see Chapter 8: Creature Templates). A sentient serpent cannot serve as an animal companion, familiar, or special mount.
spell-serpent-coils: This spell causes three black and purple snakes to shoot from your hand and coil about a single target, biting and constricting. You must make a ranged touch attack for each snake. Each snake that misses vanishes into smoke. Each snake that hits automatically bites for 1d6 damage per round and coils around the target, interfering with its movement. The target must make a Will save each round or be affected as if they were entangled. The target only makes one save regardless of how many snakes are coiled around it.
spell-serpent-sneak-attack: This spell endows the recipient with the stealth and precision of a stalking serpent, giving him or her a +2 bonus to confirm critical hits. The recipient also gains a rogue's sneak attack ability, causing an additional +2d6 points of damage. Only one sneak attack can be made while the spell lasts, though the bonus to confirm critical hits remains for the duration. At caster level 7, the bonus sneak attack damage increases to +3d6. At caster level 10, the damage is +4d6. If the recipient already has the sneak attack ability, the damage bonuses from this spell don't stack with it.
spell-serpent-strike: This spell gives the recipient the attack speed and ferocity of a striking snake when attacking with a melee weapon. The recipient gains a +4 enhancement bonus to initiative and may ignore dodge bonuses of targets within melee range. In addition, such is the snake-like ferocity of the recipient's attacks that his opponents must make a Will save or become shaken for 1 round each time they are struck. Victims who are immune to fear are not shaken.
spell-serpents-wrath: This spell fills the recipient with the cold rage of an angry serpent. This rage is similar to a barbarian's, but the recipient gains only a +1 morale bonus to Strength and Constitution and a +1 morale bonus on Will saves, while suffering a –1 penalty to AC. These bonuses do not stack with bonuses gained from other raging abilities. Furthermore, the recipient's eyes take on the light of a cold, methodical killer, and any opponent within 5 ft. of him must make a Will save or become shaken for 1 round. Creatures immune to fear are not shaken. Creatures that make their save are immune to the shaken effect for the spell duration. Like the barbarian, enraged creatures cannot use skills, feats or abilities that require patience and concentration, such as moving silently or casting spells. At the end of the rage, the recipient is fatigued for a number of rounds equal to the number of rounds spent in the rage.
spell-serpentine-reflexes:
The transmuted creature gains the defensive reflexes of a serpent, giving them a +1 dodge bonus to AC and Reflex saves. The creature also gains the evasion ability of a rogue, but this secondary benefit can only be used once while the spell is in effect. After evasion is used, the spell immediately ends.

Multiple serpentine reflexes don't stack. Serpentine reflexes dispels and counters slow.
spell-serpentine-weapon:
This spell has two uses: it can enhance a poisoned weapon or it can enhance the poison DC of a creature with a natural poison attack. When cast on a weapon already coated with poison, the spell doubles the length of time the weapon stays coated. Thus, poison coated on a weapon is effective for two hits rather than one. This spell affects only one light slashing or piercing melee weapon already coated with poison. In addition, the wielder gains a +1 bonus to initiative the first time he strikes with the poisoned weapon.

If used on any snake or snake-like creature that has a natural poison attack, the save DC of the creature's poison is increased by 2.
spell-serpentine-whip-greater: This spell is identical to lesser serpentine whip, but the whip can extend up to 30 ft and may deliver up to two poison bites, each of which inflicts 1d8 Con/1d8 Str damage. It may deliver touch spells up to the 6th level.
spell-serpentine-whip-lesser: This spell creates a whip with a fanged snake's head, which you are considered to be proficient with. You may use the whip as a weapon or to deliver 5th-level or lower melee touch spells. When using the whip as a weapon, it functions as a normal whip, but always inflicts lethal damage. Once per casting of the spell, the whip's snake head may also deliver a poisonous bite (Fort DC 10 + 1/2 your caster level + your Int or Cha modifier, 1d6 Con/1d6 Str, duration: 1 round). This requires a successful touch attack. For as long as the spell lasts, any touch range spell of 5th level or lower that you cast can be delivered by the serpent whip, although the whip itself inflicts no damage when used for this purpose. The whip gives you a +1 bonus on your melee touch attack roll when delivering a touch spell, and attacking with the whip counts normally as an attack. The whip may not make a bite attack in the same round that it is used to deliver a touch spell.
spell-shield-of-arcane-imperviousness: This spell gives a shield the ability to deflect ranged touch spells. When the bearer of the shield is hit by such a spell, the attacker must re-roll his attack roll. If he hits again, the shield fails to protect its bearer and the attacker's spell takes effect normally. If the re-rolled attack misses, the shield protects the bearer from all effects of the spell, and the bearer may choose 142 to deflect the spell onto any target within 30 ft. of him that he can see. The bearer must make his own ranged touch attack roll to hit the new target. If the target is hit, it suffers all the effects of the spell just as if the original caster had hit them, saves applicable (if any).
spell-skill-of-the-rogue:
You become skillful, nimble, faster, and sneakier. However, you can no longer cast spells, even from magic items.

You gain a +2 enhancement bonus to Dexterity. You use the rogue's BAB or your own, whichever is higher. For example, a 5th-level sorcerer would have the BAB of a 5th level rogue.

You gain the rogue's evasion and sneak attack (+1d6) abilities. If you already have sneak attack, the bonus damage does not stack.

You gain +4 ranks in each of the following skills: acrobatics, climb, disable device, escape artist, perception, and sleight of hand. If you already have ranks in these skills, the bonus ranks stack, but cannot take you above the normal rank limit.

You lose your spellcasting ability, including your ability to use spell activation or spell completion magic items, just as if the spells were no longer on your class list.
spell-sonic-boom:
This spell generates a spark that detonates with an incredibly loud boom. This spell causes 2 points of sonic damage per caster level (maximum 20 points) to all those within its radius that fail to save. Additionally, those that fail to save are stunned for 1 round and deafened for 1d4 minutes.

You face the palm of your hand in the desired direction and determine the range (distance and height) at which the sonic boom is to burst. A tiny, translucent ball of air streaks from your hand and erupts into a sonic boom at that point. If the ball impacts a body or solid object before arriving at the set range, it detonates at that point. If you attempt to send the ball through a narrow passage, such as through an arrow slit, you must "hit" the opening with a ranged touch attack, or else the ball strikes the barrier and detonates prematurely.
spell-speed-of-the-mamba: This spell has the same effects as haste, but works only on snakes and snake-like creatures. Examples of snake-like creatures include a couatl, marilith demon, naga, or any creature whose anatomy includes a snake's head or body. Merely having tentacles, slit eyes, scales or a forked tongue is not enough to qualify a creature as snake-like.
spell-suffocating-earth: This spell causes any existing earth, mud, or sand the target is standing on to rise up, entangling the target and filling their mouth and nose, causing it to slowly suffocate. Targets that fail their save are entangled and begin to suffocate. See the rules for holding your breath in the core rulebook, but the target suffers a –4 penalty to its Constitution check to determine how long it can hold its breath. Also, spellcasters must make a Concentration check (DC 22) each round in order to cast spells. Suffocation of earth has no effect on creatures that do not need to breathe, such as constructs, elementals, oozes, plants, and undead.
spell-summon-slime-and-fungi: This spell works like summon monster, but summons a random ooze, slime, mold or fungus from the list below, depending on the caster's level. If the caster does not meet the minimum required caster level for the creature, roll again. The caster must specify where the random creature will appear before rolling to see which creature is actually summoned.
spell-summon-snake-swarm: This spell functions like summon swarm, but can only be used to summon a snake swarm (Bestiary 3).
spell-summon-venomous-snake-swarm: This spell functions like summon swarm, but can only be used to summon a venomous snake swarm.
spell-superheating-flames: This spell immolates the target in a burst of incredibly hot fire, dealing 10d4 points of damage per caster level (maximum 20d4), Reflex for half. Additionally, if the target fails its Reflex save, it must make a Will save or become affected by a heat metal spell.
spell-sweet-water: You draw forth some of your own soul essence to conjure sparkling clear diamond dust water which you sprinkle over the recipient, miraculously curing their ailment and healing minor wounds. This spell functions like lesser restoration, and also heals 1d6 points of damage. You suffer 2d6 points of damage from the loss of your own essence.
spell-transmute-rock-to-mud-greater: This spell is similar to transmute rock to mud, but will also affect cut or worked stone. When the spell duration ends, affected objects return to stone. Creatures in the mud get a Reflex save to avoid getting stuck when the mud returns to stone.
spell-trident-of-seafury: A large, two-handed magic trident of steel-hard ice appears in your hand, which only you can use. You are considered proficient with the weapon. The trident counts as a magic, cold iron reach weapon with a +2 enhancement bonus per three caster levels (max +6), inflicts 1d10 damage, and critical on an 18-20/x2. Half the damage is piercing and half is cold damage. The trident can also be used to coat an opponent that was just hit with a layer of ice. Activating this effect is a swift action. This ice slows the target (Reflex save negates, spell resistance applicable) for one round per two caster levels, but the trident immediately shatters if the ice attack is successful. Cold type creatures are immune to this effect.
spell-trident-of-the-helldukes: A two-handed, barbed, magic trident of steel-hard, reddish brass appears in your hand, which only you can use. You are considered proficient with the weapon. The trident counts as a magic reach weapon with a +2 enhancement bonus, inflicts 1d8 damage, and criticals on a 20/x2. On a critical hit, the painful barbs sink into the target, hampering it as it tries to free itself and reducing its movement by 10 ft. for one round.
spell-vampire-sword:
A 3-foot-long, serrated black sword with a howling vampire face on the hilt appears in your hand. You wield this as if it were a longsword and are considered proficient with it. Attacks with the vampire sword are melee touch attacks. The blade deals 1d8 points of slashing damage + 1 point per two caster levels (maximum +10). Since the blade is immaterial, your Strength modifier does not apply to the damage. In addition, you gain temporary hit points equal to the damage you deal. You can't gain more than the subject's current hit points + the subject's Constitution score (which is enough to kill the subject). Regardless of how many creatures you attack, the maximum amount of temporary hit points that can be gained is equal to your normal maximum hit points. For example, a caster with a normal maximum of 32 hit points could never gain more than 32 additional temporary hit points from this spell. All temporary hit points gained from this spell disappear 30 minutes later.

There is a 50% chance that humanoids slain by this spell temporarily rise as zombies. However, the sword wielder cannot control these zombies unless he has some ability that allows him to control undead. The maximum number of hit dice worth of zombies that can be created in a single day is equal to your caster level. All zombies created by the sword crumble to dust one day later.
spell-vein-of-magma: This spell causes a vein of glowing hot, sulfurous magma to ooze out of the ground, dealing 3d6 damage per round to anyone standing on it, Reflex save for half damage. The magma creates illumination equal to a candle in each square, and automatically ignites flammable materials that contact it, as if they had been hit by alchemist's fire. Furthermore, the sulfurous fumes emanating from the magma sicken all those standing on the vein (Fort negates). The sickening effect lasts only as long as the victim is on or within 5 ft. of the vein of magma.
spell-viper-rod: The caster summons a rod of the viper that he may use without restriction, regardless of his alignment, for the duration of the spell. The caster is considered proficient with the rod, and the rod will not work for anyone else. Unlike the actual magic item, victims struck by a summoned rod of the viper become immune to its poison once they make a successful save. The rod disappears when the spell ends.
spell-virulent-venom:
This spell increases the potency of the venom possessed by serpents and snake-like creatures. Any such creature that possesses a natural bite attack that inflicts poison can be affected. The creature's poison inflicts +1 points of ability damage for the duration of the spell. For example, a snake whose poison normally inflicts 1d4 Con damage now inflicts 1d4+1 Con.

Furthermore, the venom resists delay poison spells, reducing the spell's duration by half (minimum 1 round).
spell-volcanic-eruption: This spell causes a small, localized area of earth or stone to erupt, spewing molten rock, lava, hot gas and dark smoke over the area. Those within the area of the spell suffer 3d8 damage (half bludgeoning, half fire) each round from the flying rocks, superheated toxic gas and streams of lava (Reflex save for half) and are ignited for an additional 1d6 points of damage per round if they fail their save. A character can extinguish burning items as a full-round action. Creatures immune to fire are not affected by the heat or lava, but still suffer half or quarter damage from flying rocks. In addition, the toxic gases cause nausea identical to a stinking cloud spell (Fort negates). Last, the dark, billowing smoke within the area reduces vision to 20 ft.
spell-vultures-of-death:
This spell summons three ominous black vultures with white, milky eyes, considered magical beasts. These vultures have the same statistics as a normal small eagle, though they are slower flyers (40 fly speed). Each vulture has one-third the caster's total hit points (not including temporary hit points), rounded down, regardless of its actual Hit Dice, and has a +1 natural armor adjustment per two caster levels. Each vulture also has an empathic link with the caster (1,000 ft. range), and an intelligence of 4.

The vultures have a continuous short range deathwatch ability (20 ft. cone), making them aware of the physical condition of creatures near them. They empathically relay an emotion of eagerness to the caster when they detect a creature within range is dead, fragile or fighting off death, as described in the deathwatch spell. However, they are not able to communicate the target creature's exact condition.

Each vulture must remain within 20 ft. of the other vultures at all times. If a vulture is somehow separated from the others, it must spend a full action each round to get within range, or do nothing.

The vultures will attack opponents to the best of their ability. The caster can also direct them not to attack, to attack particular enemies, or to perform other actions.

If a living creature within 30 ft. of one of the vultures falls to 4 or less hit points, the vultures immediately move on their next turn and attack that creature or its body, regardless of what the caster commands. If more than one such severely wounded target is available, roll randomly for each vulture to determine which one it attacks. The vultures continue to attack such targets and cannot be commanded by the caster for a full round. If one of the vultures kills the target, each vulture gains 1d8 temporary hit points and a +2 enhancement bonus to Strength, similar to a death knell spell. These bonuses last until the spell ends.

When within the area of a desecrate spell, the vultures gain improved evasion, suffering no damage when successfully saving vs. an attack that normally allows a Reflex saving throw, and suffering only half damage even if the saving throw fails.
spell-wall-of-crashing-waves:
This spell creates a wall of dark water churning with violently crashing waves. The wall cannot be formed in an area occupied by creatures or objects. The wall is 2 inches thick per caster level. The churning dark water obscures vision through it so that creatures can only see up to 10 feet past it. Both sides of the wall emit a cold, stinging spray of water and the sound of loud, crashing waves that is very distracting. Spellcasters must make Concentration checks (DC 13) when within 5 ft. of the wall.

Creatures attempting to pass through the wall suffer 2d4 points of bludgeoning damage and must make an opposed Strength roll vs. the wall, which has a Strength of 20 + 1 per two caster levels. The wall violently ejects those who fail back the way they came, throwing them back 5 ft. per two caster levels. If the creature impacts a solid object as a result of being ejected, it suffers damage as if it had fallen the same distance. If the wall is ring-shaped, it only ejects creatures attempting to pass through it from the outside.

Each 10-foot length of wall has 3 hit points per inch of thickness. The wall has damage reduction 5/bludgeoning. Creatures can hit the wall automatically. A section of wall whose hit points drop to 0 is breached. If a creature tries to break through the wall with a single attack, the DC for the Strength check is 15 + caster level.

If any 10-foot length of wall takes 30 points of fire damage or more in 1 round, that length evaporates. (Do not divide fire damage by 4, as normal for objects.)

Wall of crashing waves can be made permanent with a permanency spell. A permanent wall of crashing waves that is extinguished by fire damage becomes inactive for 10 minutes, then reforms at normal strength.
spell-wall-of-hurricane-winds:
This spell creates a wall of hurricane-force wind. The wall cannot be formed in an area occupied by creatures or objects. One side of the wall (your choice) emits the hurricane-force winds, the other side is calm. The windy side of the wall has all the effects of a hurricane to everything within 10 feet of it.

This spell can be made permanent with a permanency spell.
spell-wall-of-living-fire: This spell is identical to wall of fire, but the caster can change the location, orientation and form of the wall once per round, up to a maximum of three times per casting of the spell. The caster must concentrate to change the wall.
spell-wall-of-serpents:
This spell creates an anchored plane of stone, one side of which is dotted with hundreds of irregularly shaped holes. Hiding within the holes are hundreds of small vipers, which extend to attack any creature coming within 5 ft. of the wall. Targets must make a Reflex save to avoid being bitten. Those who fail suffer a total of 1d6 points of damage from the collective bites and must make a Fortitude save or be poisoned. The vipers' poison inflicts 1d4 initial points of Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution damage (caster's choice). The poison has no secondary damage. Even though it appears that targets may have been bitten by multiple heads, they need only make one Reflex and/or Fortitude save each round that they are within 5 ft. of the wall. The vipers within the wall are immune to all attacks and magic.

The thickness, hit points, and hardness of a wall of serpents are identical to a wall of stone.
spell-wave-of-doom:
This spell creates a massive, rapidly moving wave of violent water. Anything in the path suffers 1d4 points of damage per caster level (maximum 20d4) In addition, those who fail to save are knocked down, pushed back 2 ft. per caster level, and begin choking from the inhaled water in their lungs. Choking victims suffer a –2 penalty on attack rolls, damage rolls, ability checks, and saving throws for 1d4 rounds. Choking spellcasters must make a Concentration check (DC 18) in order to cast spells with verbal components.

This spell extinguishes all normal flames and has a 75% chance of dispelling magic fire effects, such as a wall of fire or fire shield.

This spell has a chance of overturning ships (80% for small ships, 55% for Medium ships, and 30% for large ships). Standing structures hit by the wave are affected as if by an earthquake spell.
spell-zombie-form:
You take on the appearance of a horrific, rotting zombie and gain some undead immunities and resistances, at the cost of being slow and suffering some undead vulnerabilities.

When the spell is cast, you gain two of the undead-like immunities or resistances of your choice listed below. Once selected, they cannot be changed for the duration of the spell.

While in zombie form, you also gain the following abilities and hindrances: DR 5/slashing. Once the spell has prevented a total of 5 points of damage per caster level (maximum 25 points), the spell is discharged and all its benefits and hindrances end.

Each round you are in zombie form, you must make a DC 13 Will save at the start of your turn or become 149 staggered for one round and can only perform a single move action or standard action. While under the effect of the spell, you are vulnerable to effects that damage, hinder or detect undead, such as channeled positive energy, chill touch, command undead, detect undead, disrupt undead, holy water, etc. Positive energy and healing spells no longer heal you, but negative channeled energy heals you for half the normal amount. You gain no benefit from spells and magic that bolster undead.

This spell does not fool undead into thinking the caster is undead.
spell-absolute-zero:
When you cast this spell, the temperature within the affected area plummets to absolute zero (0° Kelvin, –470° Fahrenheit, –273° Celsius). All gaseous and liquid molecules instantaneously freeze and become solid, granting concealment and total cover to creatures within the area. If creatures are within the area when you first cast the spell, they may avoid being caught in the area with a successful Reflex save, appearing in the closest unoccupied square adjacent to the area. If there are no unoccupied squares adjacent to the spell's area, the creature may remain in its original location or move to any unoccupied square of the creature's choice within the affected area.

Creatures and objects within the area take 10d6 points of cold damage at the beginning of your turn, including the round when absolute zero is cast. If the damage would be sufficient to kill the creature, it lapses into cryogenic stasis instead and no longer takes cold damage from this spell. In this state, its hit points are a negative amount equal to one higher than its Constitution score (for instance, –12 for a creature with a Constitution score of 13), which renders it unconscious, but still alive. (However, damage other than cold damage dealt to the creature from another source, such as a successful melee attack, can still kill the creature while in cryogenic stasis.) Its bodily functions completely cease, and it is frozen solid. The creature cannot heal naturally and most magical healing also fails. Only a heal, limited wish, miracle, or wish can affect a creature in cryogenic stasis. The creature's cryogenic stasis ends when the spell's duration expires or the creature is removed from the affected area. When this occurs, the creature must succeed on a Fortitude save with a penalty equal to the number of rounds the creature spent in cryogenic stasis. If the creature succeeds, it stabilizes. On a failed save, the creature immediately dies.

Creatures who survive the damage are not frozen solid, but they must hold their breath or risk suffocating and are also trapped in place by the solidified gases and liquids encasing them. Despite being solidified, creatures can force their way through the formerly gaseous material by making a Strength check as a full-round action. For every 5 points by which the check exceeds 10, a creature moves 5 feet (up to a maximum distance equal to its normal land speed), though it can move only through areas occupied by solidified gases or liquids and not permanent, fixed objects. Creatures attempting to enter the area from the outside must do the same in addition to taking cold damage when they enter the affected area. Nonmagical objects within the area become brittle, reducing their hardness to 0.

Ethereal creatures can move through the area without hindrance.

At the end of the duration, gases and liquids solidified by the extreme cold return to their natural state as the temperature also reverts to what it was before you cast the spell. If you cast this spell within a vacuum, creatures may move freely through the affected area without making Strength checks.
spell-belly-of-the-beast: You instantly teleport the creature touched inside the belly of another creature you can see as if the creature swallowed the target whole. The target may be of any size and always arrives in the exact spot desired, but the creature you teleport the subject into must have the swallow whole special attack and be large enough to accommodate a creature of the target's size. If the creature does not satisfy the preceding requirements, the spell fails. Only the target receives a Will save to negate this spell. However, if you attempt to teleport the target into a creature with spell resistance, you must overcome that creature's spell resistance to teleport the target into the creature, otherwise the spell fails.
spell-brain-freeze: This spell causes fleeting yet intense pain in the subject's brain triggered by a false sensory response to extreme cold. On a failed save, the subject takes 1d6 points of nonlethal damage + 1 point per caster level (maximum +5), and is staggered and distracted. Although this spell deals no cold damage, creatures immune to cold damage are also immune to this spell.
spell-campfire:
You conjure an image of a roaring, seemingly abandoned campfire with burning logs surrounded by a ring of stones. The spell can alter the appearance of terrain, flora, or objects within the spread (or it can add them where none are present). Nonetheless, it cannot disguise, hide, or add creatures (though creatures within the spread might use the illusory surroundings to hide their presence just as they would in a real location). The illusion duplicates the sights, smells, sounds, tactile feelings, and thermal effects of a real campfire. The flames emit light and periodically crackle, the odor of charred wood fills the air, the stones feel solid and hot to the touch, and most importantly the blaze radiates heat.

Although the campfire creates the illusion of generating heat, the weather conditions around the campfire remain unchanged. Creatures within the affected area believe they are warm, dry, and sheltered from the wind when the exact opposite may be true.

When a creature experiences the effects of external weather conditions, such as suffering a penalty to a ranged attack attributable to high winds, or has sufficient reasons for suspicion about the illusion's veracity, such as seeing snow fall around the area except for the campfire's immediate vicinity without a plausible explanation, the creature gains another saving throw with a +2 bonus. When a creature takes nonlethal or lethal damage, regardless of the source, the creature also gains another saving with a bonus equal to the damage.
spell-cold-day-in-hell: This spell evokes a vertical column of cold infused with positive energy. The spell deals 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 15d6). Half the damage is cold damage, but the other half is positive energy dealing damage to evil outsiders only, though the positive energy damage is not subject to being reduced by resistance to cold-based attacks. The positive energy does not deal damage to any other creature type, nor does it heal living creatures.
spell-crevasse:
This spell causes the sand, earth, dirt, rock, stone, snow, or ice just in front of your feet to split open, leaving a 5-foot-wide crevasse in its wake. Creatures standing atop the crevasse must succeed on a Reflex save to avoid falling into the newly formed chasm by stepping into an adjacent square. Creatures that are forcibly pushed, moved, or thrown into the crevasse do not receive a Reflex save to avoid falling into it, but they may catch themselves while falling by succeeding on a DC 40 Climb check (DC 45 if the walls are covered in ice). Large-size creatures and bigger cannot fall into the crevasse.

Any creature that fails its saving throw falls into the crack and plummets to the bottom, which is up to 10 feet deep per caster level (maximum 100 ft.). Creatures falling into the crevasse take falling damage as normal.

The crevasse's walls have a Climb DC of 20 (DC 25 if covered in ice). The fracture is too narrowly focused to damage large stone structures. Smaller structures such as cottages and homes still supported by two or more solid and diametrically opposed points also emerge unscathed. Crevasse has no effect on surfaces made from wood, worked stone, or metal.
spell-endless-night:
The subject believes he is surrounded by supernatural darkness. The target first gets a Will save to recognize that the darkness is unreal. The subject takes a –4 penalty on this save if he does not have low-light vision or darkvision and has not seen the sun within the last twenty-four hours. Subjects with low-light vision gain a +2 bonus on this save while those with darkvision gain a +4 bonus on this save. If the save fails, the darkness seems impenetrable, even to creatures with darkvision.

Because the creature believes the darkness to be real, he has no reason to communicate this fact to others and may be inclined to use his available resources to improve the prevailing lighting conditions. Allies notice the subject's strange behavior and surmise the reason, such as fumbling around in the imaginary darkness, with a successful DC 20 Sense Motive check. If they communicate the darkness's unreal nature to the subject, he may immediately attempt another Will save against the spell with a +4 bonus. If the subject casts a spell or effect that would normally counter or dispel darkness, the subject gains a new saving throw against this spell instead. Blind creatures as well as those relying upon other senses such as blindsight to discern their surroundings are immune to this spell.
spell-false-north:
This spell distorts the true location of the planet's magnetic poles as well as bending light to distort the actual position of stars and other heavenly bodies in the sky, making it impossible to accurately navigate within the spell's area of effect. At the time of casting, you must designate the cardinal direction of the false magnetic pole. If you alter the false magnetic pole's direction by more than thirty degrees from true magnetic pole, all creatures receive a Will save to disbelieve the illusion upon first entering the area.

Creatures very familiar with the area or those using an accurate map of the area relying upon geographical landmarks gain a +4 bonus on the preceding Will save. Divination spells such as know direction also grant the caster a Will save to disbelieve this spell. On a failed save, the spell points toward the false magnetic pole.

Multiple castings of the same spell by the same caster do not grant the creature a new Will save and yield the same results as the initial attempt.

If the actual magnetic pole is anywhere within the spell's area of effect, all creatures take a –4 penalty on their saving throws against this illusion. Otherwise, all Survival checks made within the area of effect to avoid getting lost automatically fail. Nonmagical compasses and other navigational devices relying upon the location of the magnetic pole or the positions of heavenly bodies also provide false information, leading the user astray.
spell-fire-and-ice: A spherical globule of viscous, gelatinous material springs from your hand and races to its target. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack to hit your target. The globule deals 1d6 points of cold damage per caster level (maximum 5d6). At the beginning of your next turn, the chilly substance rapidly warms, dealing 1d6 points of fire damage, unless the target uses a full-round action to remove the gooey material with at least a gallon of water. For every three caster levels you possess beyond 3rd level, the viscous material lasts for another round (to a maximum of 6 additional rounds at 18th level), dealing another 1d6 points of fire damage in each round.
spell-flame-foe: You gain spell resistance equal to 10 + your caster level against spells with the fire descriptor.
spell-fortress-of-frigid-solitude:
You transform existing ice and snow into a fortress, 60 feet square at its base and 40 feet high with two-foot-thick walls. If there is an insufficient quantity of ice and snow on hand to satisfy the preceding dimensions, the spell fails. The fortress has arrow slits on all sides and a small door crafted from two-foot-thick ice serving as its only entrance. Only you can command the door to open. The spell even foils magical attempts to open the portal, including the use of a knock spell.

The fortress appears in just 1 round, though it cannot be conjured so it occupies the same space as a creature or another object. You can create any floor plan you wish to the limit of the spell's effect, but the only building materials you may use are ice and snow.

Likewise, you may also furnish the fortress as you desire, once again using only ice and snow to create functional beds, tables, chairs, and other objects.

Regardless of the weather conditions outside the fortress, the internal temperature remains a constant 60° Fahrenheit (15° Celsius) with a fresh, moderately chilly breeze circulating throughout the fortress.

Despite the internal temperature, the ice and snow within the fortress remains frozen.

The fortress provides its occupants with life-sustaining nourishment, eliminating living creatures' need to eat and drink within its protective confines. The occupant's mental acuity also increases while within the fortress.

Living creatures need a meager 2 hours of sleep per day to gain the benefit of 8 hours of sleep, though spellcasters still cannot prepare spells more than once per day. In addition, living creatures heal ability score damage to their Charisma, Intelligence, and Wisdom at a rate of 1d4 points each per day, though damage to physical ability scores, Constitution, Dexterity, and Strength, still heals at the normal rate of 1 point each day.
