The fortress's icy walls have 72 hit points and hardness 0. However, if the outside temperature is at or below the freezing point (32° Fahrenheit, 0° Celsius), the fortress automatically repairs itself, restoring damage each round at a rate of 2 hit points per caster level.

Nonetheless, if a 10-foot section of the wall is reduced to 0 hit points, the wall is breached. Even in the wall's absence, the fortress's efforts to repair the damage, when applicable, generate a continuous blast of frigid air dealing 1d6 points of cold damage + 1 point of cold damage per caster level (no save) to any creature stepping through the breach.
spell-frozen-acid:
You hurl a fist-sized snowball made from frozen acid.

You must succeed on a ranged touch attack to hit your target. On a successful hit, you deal 1d6 points of cold damage per two caster levels (maximum 5d6). At the beginning of your next turn, the ball of frozen acid melts, dealing 1d4 points of acid damage per two caster levels (maximum 5d4). The target may spend a full-round washing off the acid with at least a gallon of water. If the target does so prior to the beginning of your next turn, the subject takes no acid damage from the melted acid.
spell-geomagnetic-storm: Dazzling multicolored lights taking on a multitude of unique shapes fill the area, though the illumination sheds only dim light in the area. Sparks of electricity continuously surge through the area, dealing 1d6 points of electricity damage + 1 point of electricity damage per two caster levels (maximum +10) to creatures and objects within the storm. The storm deals this damage when it appears, and to all creatures in the area on your turn each round. The magnetism created by the storm is too weak to affect most metallic objects, but any ranged attack made with small metallic projectiles including arrows, bolts, and bullets passing through the storm suffers a 50% miss chance.
spell-glissade: The subject gains a +10 enhancement bonus on Acrobatics checks made when moving across snow-covered or icy terrain. The enhancement bonus increases to +20 at 5th caster level, and to +30 (the maximum) at 9th caster level.
spell-hot-cocoa:
This spell conjures a warm, tasty beverage made from water and cocoa beans. The drink retains its magical properties for 1 hour before becoming non-magical.

Every creature who drinks the hot cocoa within 1 hour of its creation gains temporary hit points equal to your caster level (to a maximum of 5 temporary hit points at caster level 5) that last for 1 hour after consuming the beverage. Drinking the hot cocoa is a standard action provoking attacks of opportunity. Unlike normal temporary hit points, you may lose these temporary hit points only when you sustain cold damage. As long as you have 1 temporary hit point remaining, you suffer no harm from being in a cold environment until the temperature drops below –51° Fahrenheit (–46° Celsius).
spell-hypothermia:
You can attempt to freeze one living creature to death.

When you cast this spell, frigid air swirls around your hand. You must succeed on a melee touch attack to touch the target. The target can attempt to resist the spell's effect with a Fortitude save. If he succeeds, the target takes 2d6 points of nonlethal damage +1 point per caster level from the flash freezing, but suffers no further effects. If the target fails, the subject's blood, organs, and tissue rapidly freeze. On the target's next turn, he is paralyzed and takes 4d6 points of cold damage +1 point of cold damage per caster level. One round later, the target takes 8d6 points of cold damage +1 point of cold damage per level and lapses into unconsciousness. One round after that, the target dies from hypothermia, regardless of its hit point total.

Each round, the target can delay that round's effects from affecting him with a successful Fortitude save, but the spell continues for 3 rounds, and each failed Fortitude save moves the subject one step further along the track to freezing to death. Living creatures immune to cold damage and those with the cold subtype are immune to this spell.
spell-ice-bridge:
You create a bridge made from ice. The ice bridge is 1 foot thick, 5 feet wide and up to 10 feet long per caster level. It may be a flat span, or it may have an arch at its center. The arch's apex may be up to 1 foot high per caster level. Each end of the ice bridge must be anchored on a solid surface such as earth, stone, wood, or even ice otherwise the ice bridge immediately collapses and shatters into tiny pieces. Each 5-foot square of the ice bridge has a hardness of 0 and 36 hit points. A section of bridge whose hit points drops to 0 shatters, causing the entire bridge to fail.

You may move across the ice bridge without penalty.

Other creatures unable to move across ice without hindrance move at half their normal speed with a successful DC 10 Acrobatics check. Failure by 4 or less means the creature failed to move that round and must succeed at a Reflex save to avoid falling prone.

Failure by 5 or more means it cannot move that round and automatically falls prone. Creatures opting not to move on their turn do not need to make the preceding check.

The ice is an instantaneous effect, but persists as non-magical ice. As long as the temperature remains at or below freezing (32° Fahrenheit, 0° Celsius), the ice bridge lasts indefinitely. Each minute of exposure to temperatures above the freezing point deals 1 point of damage to every 5-foot section of the ice bridge. This damage increases by +1 for every nine degrees Fahrenheit (five degrees Celsius) or fraction thereof that the temperature exceeds the freezing point. Thus, a bridge conjured in a tropical forest where the temperature reaches a balmy 80° Fahrenheit (26° Celsius) would take 6 points of damage every minute from the warm conditions.
spell-iceberg:
You conjure into existence up to three small icebergs.

An iceberg cannot be conjured so it occupies the same space as a creature or another object. The iceberg's entire surface must rest upon either solid ground or a liquid, although you may place each of the three icebergs atop a different surface from the others. When cast on solid ground such as earth, stone, snow, or ice, the iceberg merges with the surrounding surface, including another iceberg, and becomes an immovable object, even when cast on a slippery, vertical surface.

When cast on water or any other liquid, the entire iceberg floats atop the surface in the same manner as a piece of driftwood or any other entirely buoyant object.

No portion of the iceberg extends beneath the water's surface. Unlike an iceberg conjured onto solid ground, the prevailing current or winds may move the iceberg.

When an iceberg collides with another object or another object crashes into it, the iceberg deals 32d8 points of damage as described in the "Iceberg" section in Chapter 3 of this sourcebook. On the other hand, creatures take only 1d6 points of damage when an iceberg strikes them or they strike an iceberg. Of course, creatures falling onto an iceberg would still take the appropriate amount of falling damage, as would a creature forcibly hurled against the iceberg.

The iceberg has a hardness of 0 and 1,800 hp. Creatures can hit an iceberg automatically, and the iceberg takes double damage from fire-based spells and effects. When an iceberg's hit points drop to 0, the iceberg instantly vanishes into nothingness.
spell-icicle-shower:
Icicles fall to the ground dealing 1d6 points of piercing damage and 1d4 points of cold damage to every creature in the area. The icicles embed themselves into the ground unless the surface is too hard to hold footprints, such as bare rock, solid ice, or a stone floor, in which case, the icicles shatter upon impact and have no further effect. Otherwise, each creature moving through the area at greater than half speed runs the risk of stepping onto an embedded icicle. Make an attack roll for the icicles. The icicles use your caster level as their base attack bonus. Roll only once for the entire spell effect each round and apply the result to all creatures in the area of effect. For this attack, the creature's shield, armor, and deflection bonuses do not count, though a creature wearing shoes or other footwear gets a +4 armor bonus to AC.

If the attack succeeds, the creature has stepped onto an icicle. The icicle deals 1 point of piercing damage and 1 point of cold damage. Any creature taking damage from stepping on an icicle must also succeed on a Reflex save or suffer a wound to its feet that slows its land speed by half. This speed penalty lasts for 24 hours or until the injured creature receives a cure spell (which also restores lost hit points). Another creature can remove the penalty by taking 10 minutes to dress the injuries and succeeding on a Heal check against the spell's save DC. Creatures of Tiny size and smaller automatically move through the area with no chance of stepping onto an icicle, though they treat the area as difficult terrain. Creatures of Huge size and larger as well as creatures lacking feet take no damage and suffer no ill effect from stepping onto the icicles.
spell-icy-future:
You receive a brief glimpse into your future. Whenever an opponent targets you with a spell with the cold descriptor or makes an attack against you that deals cold damage, you may take a standard, move, swift, or free action of your choice, including an attempt to counterspell your opponent's spell, as if you readied the action, treating the casting of the spell or the attack as the readied action's trigger. If the action you chose makes it impossible for your opponent to legally target you or another creature with that action, the opponent's action is lost. For instance, if your opponent announced its intention to make a melee attack against you with its +1 frost longsword, but you teleported out of the battle, the opponent may still attack one of your allies if they are legal targets. However, if there are no remaining legal targets when you teleported away, your opponent's attack action would be wasted.

Unlike a normal readied action, your initiative count remains unchanged, though the readied action you took counts toward the number and type of actions you can take on your turn that round. Therefore, if you used a standard for your readied action, you cannot take another standard action on your initiative count that round. Using the readied action in the preceding manner discharges and ends the spell.
spell-icy-past:
When you cast this spell and touch your hand against the surface of a glacier, a 1-inch-radius core sample of compressed ice or snow measuring up to 1 foot in length per caster level erupts from the surface. Each 1- foot-long section of glacial ice records ten years of history. Thus, a 20-foot-high ice core contains 200 years of history. The compacted snow and ice only keeps a record of general events affecting an extensive area including the glacial ice's present location, if any.

For instance, the core sample would reveal evidence of a volcanic eruption, an asteroid impact, a massive flood, an abandoned settlement, or even a pitched battle encompassing the entire region. But it would provide no information about more localized activities such as a small skirmish in the immediate vicinity or details about a local resident unless that creature occupied the area for the ice sample's entire existence.

By placing your hand onto the icy surface, the core sample reveals information about one such generalized event per two caster levels. In the case of natural occurrences, the ice reveals the event's general nature, the approximate date, its duration, its overall impact, and consequences arising from the event. For instance, the ice sample might reveal that a giant asteroid struck the area 103 years earlier. The impact incinerated all plants and animals in a twenty-mile radius around the crater and then plunged the land into a deep freeze for the next ten years. When providing details about the activities of creatures, the ice describes the general nature of its interaction with the creatures, such as battle or long-term residency, the approximate date of the event, and the creature types involved (undead, humanoids, dragons, and so on). The ice cannot confer individual names or even the creatures' races.

At the time of casting, you designate whether you want to learn about events in chronological order, either oldest to most recent or vice versa, or in order of significance and impact. Unlike the former option, the latter choice only allows you to discover the most significant events first. You also have the option of designating whether you would like to learn about natural events or humanoid activities first.
spell-internal-combustion:
Your touch increases the subject's internal body temperature. When you cast this spell, waves of heat emanate from your hand. You must succeed on a melee touch attack to hit the target.

On the first round of the spell, the target feels uncomfortably warm but takes no damage. On subsequent rounds, the effects intensify. The following table describes the spell's effects on most creatures as well as its effects on creatures with the cold subtype.

Each round's effects are not cumulative.

Any cold intense enough to damage the creature negates fire damage from the spell on a point-for-point basis, but not the distracted, sickened, nauseated, or dazed effects. An affected target must attempt a Fortitude save each round at the beginning of its turn.

A successful save negates the distracted, sickened, nauseated, or dazed effect for that round and reduces the fire damage by half. This spell has no effect on creatures with the fire subtype and those immune to fire damage.
spell-meld-into-ice:
This spell functions like meld into stone except it allows you to meld your body and possessions into a single block of ice instead of a single block of stone.

Icebergs, glaciers, and other contiguous structures formed from compacted ice and snow are treated as a single block of ice for the purposes of this spell. The effects of the spells listed in the meld into stone description do not apply to you when you meld into ice.

However, the following spells harm you if cast upon the ice you are occupying. Any fire-based spell or effect that melts the ice expels you and deals you 5d6 points of damage. Any spell or effect able to shape the snow or ice deals 3d6 points of damage but does not expel you. Thaw (see below) expels you and then slays you instantly unless you succeed on a DC 18 Fortitude save, in which case you are merely expelled. Any spell or effect allowing another creature to pass through or burrow through the ice expels you without damage.
spell-moguls: This spell alters the shape of existing ice and snow. It turns an otherwise flat surface into bumpy terrain filled with large mounds called moguls. Vehicles such as dog sleds and sleighs find it extremely difficult to negotiate the mounds. A vehicle moving at a speed greater than half but less than its normal speed increases the driver's skill check to control the vehicle by +20. This modifier decreases to +10 if the vehicle moves at up to half its normal speed. It is impossible to drive a vehicle at its normal speed or faster through the moguls without overturning the vehicle. Likewise, the moguls increase the DC of Acrobatics checks made to ski, run, or charge downhill through the area by +10, and the DC of any Climb checks made in the affected area also increases by +5. Magical ice and snow are not affected by this spell.
spell-portage:
You create a pair of sharp runners that appear on the keel, bottom, or undercarriage of the touched vehicle.

The runners are the same length as the vehicle and appear on the vehicle's starboard and port sides. At the time of casting, you may use the spell to gently lift the vehicle onto any solid surface, including ice, adjacent to any part of the vehicle. The entire vehicle then appears in the closest unoccupied squares adjacent to that point. While on a solid surface, the vehicle may be pulled overland by muscle or current, up to the vehicle's maximum speed in the case of a land vehicle or up to half the vehicle's maximum speed for a water or air vehicle. Alternatively, as long as you are within 30 feet of the vehicle, you may direct the spell to lug the vehicle in any direction of your choice, though the vehicle's maximum speed is only half your normal speed.

The runners wink out of existence when the spell duration expires. When they disappear, the vehicle falls to the surface beneath it. In the case of a vehicle outside of its normal medium, such as a water vehicle on land, the vehicle takes damage from the fall. Treat the impact as if it collided with a Colossal object (see the "Vehicles in Combat" section in Chapter 4 of the Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Ultimate Combat). In addition, if the vehicle does not normally have a flat bottom, the vehicle falls over onto a randomly determined side, which is treated as a second collision with a Colossal object.
spell-reindeer-sleigh:
You conjure an open sleigh made of material common to the area where the spell is cast and a Large, quasi-real reindeer-like creature magically tethered to the sleigh. The sleigh shares the same characteristics as the sleigh described in the "Land Vehicles" section in Chapter 4 of the Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Ultimate Combat. You or a person you designate while casting the spell must drive the sleigh, which can carry up to four people, including its driver, as well as 1,000 pounds of cargo. The driver uses Diplomacy or Intimidate checks for driving checks, treating the quasi-real reindeer as an intelligent creature. The reindeer does not fight. The reindeer and sleigh function as a single unit with an AC of 20 (–2 size, +7 natural, +5 Dex), and 20 hit points + 2 hit points per caster level (maximum 60). If the unit is reduced to 0 hit points or less, it instantly disappears, potentially subjecting its occupants and cargo to a crash (treat as wrecked).

In addition to the sleigh's normal attributes, the vehicle radiates light as the spell and continual warmth, granting the benefits of an endure elements to all creatures seated within it. You can suppress or reactivate either of the preceding abilities as a free action. Furthermore, you can command the sleigh to fly as a free action with a bonus on Fly skill checks equal to your caster level. Every minute or portion thereof spent flying reduces the spell's duration by 1 hour.
spell-slalom-skier: The subject gains a +10 enhancement bonus on Acrobatics checks made to ski. The enhancement bonus increases to +20 at caster level 5, and to +30 (the maximum) at caster level 9.
spell-snowball-fight:
This spell causes a barrage of snowballs made from compacted ice and snow to fly randomly throughout the area. Every creature within the area of the spell is the target of 1d3 ranged attacks each round at the beginning of your turn, including the round when you cast snowball fight. Creatures entering the area of effect are also automatically attacked. The snowballs use your caster level as their base attack bonus with no range increments. You must succeed on a ranged attack to hit a target.

Each snowball deals 1d6 points of cold damage on a successful hit. On a confirmed critical hit, the foe also suffers from one of the following randomly determined effects on a failed Fortitude save in addition to taking the snowball's normal damage.

Different snowball fight effects stack, but the same effect overlaps.
spell-thaw:
This spell instantly melts ice or snow including frozen earth to reduce its depth by as much as 2 feet per caster level within a square-shaped area whose sides are up to caster level x 10 feet long. The volume of water created by the spell is equal to 90 percent the volume of melted ice and snow. You may reduce one horizontal dimension by half and double the other horizontal dimension to change the overall area of effect.

Frozen earth or permafrost thawed by the spell turns the ground into a deep bog (see "Marsh Terrain"). Water created by the melted ice and snow may seep into the remaining ice and snow or the ground, especially if it is no longer frozen, but most of it washes away along the path of least resistance toward the closest nadir. The water is generally too shallow to cause a flood or deal damage to creatures and objects in its path. However, under the right conditions, such as melting the ice and snow surrounding a depression or adjacent to a mountain pass, the GM may determine the onrushing water duplicates the effects of flowing water or causes a flood (see the "Aquatic Terrain" and "Flood" sections in Chapter 13 of the Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook). Creatures standing atop thin ice are especially vulnerable to this spell. A creature who has a chance of jumping onto solid ground with an Acrobatics check may attempt a Reflex save to leap to safety and avoid falling into the chilly water beneath the suddenly melted ice. A creature who could not leap onto solid ground automatically falls into the frigid water. (See the "Thin Ice" section in Chapter 3 of this sourcebook for details regarding the effects of falling through thin ice.)

When cast on ice elementals (Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Bestiary 2) and other creatures made from ice or snow, this spell deals 3d6 points of Strength damage to such creatures (Fortitude half). The spell has no effect on other creatures. Earth and water affected by this spell refreeze when subjected to temperatures below 32° Fahrenheit, 0° Celsius.
spell-wall-of-snow:
This spell creates a vertical wall of snow that is 1 foot thick per caster level and composed of up to one 10- foot square per level. A wall of snow's maximum height cannot exceed half of its width (with a minimum height of 10 feet). The wall must sit upon a firm foundation, but it does not require anchor points.

You can double the wall's area by halving its thickness.

The wall cannot be conjured so that it occupies the same space as a creature or another object.

A wall of snow is immune to all weapon damage and any spells or effects targeting a specific number of objects, including single target spells such as disintegrate. The wall of snow takes full damage from spells and effects targeting an area (instead of the normal half damage taken by objects). The wall of snow takes half again as much damage (+50%) from spells or effects dealing fire damage. Each 10-foot square has 2 hit points per foot of thickness. If a section of wall is destroyed, the remaining snow in the wall immediately fills in any such hole created, reducing the wall's overall size by one 10-foot square but remaining a contiguous barrier.

Creatures can force their way slowly through the wall by making a Strength check as a full-round action. For every 5 points by which the check exceeds 15, a creature moves 5 feet (up to a maximum distance equal to its normal land speed). Snow fills the area immediately after the creature moves through it.

Creatures moving through the wall of snow are blinded. Any creature moving or attempting to move through the wall of snow takes 1d6 points of cold damage +1 point per two caster levels (no save) per round of contact with the wall. Creatures can also climb over the wall by succeeding on a DC 25 Climb check.

Any creature within the area of the spell when it is cast is caught inside.
spell-white-lightning:
You release a powerful stroke of frigid electrical energy that deals 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 15d6) to each creature within its area. The stroke begins at your fingertips.

Half the damage is electrical damage, and the other half is cold damage. If the damage caused to an interposing barrier shatters or breaks through it, the stroke may continue beyond the barrier if the spell's range permits; otherwise, it stops at the barrier just as any other spell effect does.
spell-winter-wonderland:
You throw an illusion over an area to give it a festive, wintry appearance as well as creating illusory humanoid inhabitants. You must set a few general guidelines when you cast the spell pertaining to the nature of the celebratory atmosphere as well as physical identifiable traits (number, race, gender) of its humanoid residents, though the illusion defines the specific details to make the scene appear realistic. For instance, if you envision a holiday dedicated to the winter solstice, the illusion would coat the ground, vegetation, and structures with snow, while adorning the settlement with colorful decorations. The inhabitants would be dressed in clothing befitting the occasion while singing hymns commemorating the holiday. Despite its ability to create illusory residents, the spell can only enhance the already existing structural features of an area. Therefore, while it can adorn trees, buildings, and streets, the illusion cannot create these objects.

Creatures viewing or interacting with the wintry illusion experience a sense of joy and tranquility at the marvelous sight. Creatures who fail their Will save cannot take violent actions (although they can defend themselves) nor do anything destructive within the spell's area. Any aggressive action against or damage dealt to a creature believing the illusion immediately ends the illusion in that creature's mind. Otherwise, every illusory creature within the area exudes an aura of infectious merriment and joviality. They are outwardly friendly, welcoming, and gregarious, though any conversation or interaction with a single individual lasting more than five minutes causes the illusory creature to make duplicative or nonsensical statements in addition to taking repetitive actions. Unless they have reason for suspicion, creatures interacting with the illusory creatures believe these individuals always tell the truth and are solely motivated by their desire to spread happiness and love to others.

If a creature is unduly suspicious of the area without a plausible reason, the illusion placates the creature's misgivings by feeding false readings into the creature's mind. For instance, if the creature attempts a Sense Motive check to determine if an illusory creature is lying, the check confirms the other creature is telling the truth and is not under the influence of an enchantment spell, regardless of the check's actual results. Likewise, when a creature uses spells and spell-like effects to discern an illusory creature's true nature, the illusion tricks its mind into believing it cast the spell or effect and determined everything is at it appears. In reality, the creature never actually used the spell or spell-like effect; it only believes it did.

The preceding conditions apply only to illusory creatures created by the spell. Similar efforts made to discern the true nature of real creatures within the spell's area function normally. Creatures with sufficient reason to disbelieve the illusion may investigate the illusion further, which grants them another saving throw as they directly interact with the illusion.

Multiple castings of this spell overlap, provided the general parameters of the interconnected illusions remain consistent with one another. If you attempt to conjoin illusions with disparate features, the entire effect collapses and disappears.
spell-winters-chill:
The subject experiences severe chills, causing him to believe he is rapidly freezing to death. If there is a source of warmth such as a smoldering hearth, open flames, or even a creature with the fire subtype in the subject's line of sight, the subject must move toward the heat source as quickly as possible by the most direct route. The subject moves through threatened areas without hesitation, though it does avoid obviously hazardous locations such as a chasm in its path. When the subject reaches the heat source, the subject takes no actions other than to shiver uncontrollably. If there are no heat sources within the subject's line of sight, the subject takes no actions while shivering uncontrollably. Despite the subject's obsession with staying warm, the subject is not helpless.

After the spell ends, the subject can act normally. On the creature's next turn, it may attempt a new saving throw to end the effect. This is a full round action that does not provoke attacks of opportunity. If this save is successful, the effect ends. If not, the creature continues to seek the closest source of warmth or remains motionless while shivering uncontrollably.

Creatures immune to cold and those with resistance to cold are immune to the effects of this spell.
spell-altar-fire:
This spell brings into being a small pillar of green or purple flame that burns without consuming the surface it emits from.

As long as they stay within the fire's 60-feet radius, the caster and his allies gain a +2 luck bonus on attack rolls, weapon damage rolls, saves, and skill checks, while each of his foes in the same area takes a -2 penalty on such rolls.

The altar-fire cannot be distinguished by normal means, but can be negated with a dispel magic spell.

Material Component: A pinch of flammable herbs.
spell-black-fist-of-ptahaana:
This spell uses weak telekinetic force to slowly rip the victim's heart out of his chest.

While the caster concentrates, the target suffers a heart attack, becoming paralyzed and freezing in place. It is aware and breathes normally but cannot take any actions, even speech. The target suffers 1d4 points of damage per round of excruciating pain.

Each round on its turn, the target may attempt a new saving throw to end the effect. (This is a full-round action that does not provoke attacks of opportunity.)

If the target is slain by the spell, the victim's still-beating heart is transported to the caster's outstretched hand.
spell-curse-of-double-death: When cast, this spell creates a permanent necromantic bond between the caster and the target. When the caster dies, whether from old age, disease or violence or by any other means, the target immediately also dies, apparently from the same cause as the caster. The reverse is not true, so if the target creature dies, the caster is unaffected. This spell can only affect a single target. If the caster attempts to casts the spell on another creature, the spell no longer affects the previous target.
spell-curse-of-green-decay: This loathsome spell slowly turns the victim's body into a quivering mass of green slime. If the target fails the saving throw, he begins to suffer 1d4 points of Constitution damage per round while his flesh is devoured. If the victim's Constitution score reaches zero, he dies. The decay can be stopped by a dispel magic or remove curse spell.
spell-drums-of-panic:
To cast drums of panic, the caster must have at least one rank in the Perform (drums) skill. All applicable targets within 30 feet of the caster must make a Will save with a DC equal to the result of a Perform (drums) check or become panicked for 1d4 rounds.

If a target successfully saves, the caster can continue to play the drums for a maximum of 1 round per level, re-rolling the Perform (drums) check and requiring a new Will save from those within the area each round.

Focus: A set of masterwork drums.
spell-fertility-charm:
For the duration of the spell, fertility charm allows any adult subject to father children (if male) or become pregnant (if female), regardless of physical condition, old age, or disease.

The spell works on any creature capable of sexual reproduction, be it humanoid, animal, or other. Though the spell makes conception possible, it does not guarantee it or a live birth.

As a side effect, the subject also gains the free use of the Endurance feat for the duration of the spell.

Focus: A small, anatomically correct carving representing the subject's species and gender.
spell-hand-of-revelations: By simply touching the covers of a closed book or a rolled up scroll, the caster of this spell can read the contents normally. The caster must still know the language used on the written material, and he reads the contents with the same speed as if reading from a normal book. The spell triggers any spells or traps placed on a book or scroll, just as if the book had been opened.
spell-incantation-of-the-broken-limb:
The target of the spell suffers 1d4 points of damage per level of the caster (maximum 5d4), and suffers from an arm or leg injury (caster's choice). If an arm injury, the target has a -2 penalty to all rolls that involve use of the arm (attack rolls, Swim checks, etc.). If a leg injury, the target has a -2 penalty to all rolls that involve use of the leg (Jump checks, Reflex saves, etc.). The penalties remain until all the damage caused by the spell is fully healed through either magical or mundane means.

A target who makes a successful Fortitude save takes only half damage, and does not suffer a limb injury.

Material Component: The arm or leg bone of a small animal.
spell-lifeleech:
This spell is frequently used by evil sorcerers and death priests to achieve a limited form of immortality. Casting the spell requires the sacrifice of a sentient creature of the same race as the spellcaster. The creature to be sacrificed must be helpless and/or bound while the spell is being cast.

At the culmination of the spell, the caster kills the victim, and the victim's life force is transferred to the caster (or another target within touch range of the caster). The target does not age naturally for 1 month per Hit Dice or level of the creature sacrificed.

A creature slain by this spell can only be restored to life through the successful casting of a resurrection, true resurrection, wish, or miracle spell. Raise dead has no effect on a creature slain by the lifeleech spell.

XP Cost: 10 XP per Hit Dice of the victim.
spell-lovers-curse: This is a reverse charm spell, causing other individuals to regard the target as a hated enemy. All Charisma checks and Charisma-based skills used by the target suffer a -10 circumstance penalty while under the influence of this spell. In addition, no NPC can have a reaction better than Indifferent toward an individual so cursed. Individuals who have a Hostile reaction usually attack the target on sight.
spell-raise-the-ancient-lizard-gods:
This mighty ritual animates the bones of a creature that has been in the earth for thousands or millions of years. The animated creature acquires the skeleton template. The creature obeys the commands of the caster.

Creatures created by this spell do not count against the number of undead you can create and control using animate dead.

Material Component: The skull and at least 20% of the bones of a prehistoric creature.

XP Cost: 2,000 XP
spell-sorcery-of-the-skull:
By means of this grisly spell, the severed head of an opponent is enchanted by peeling off the skin and sewing up the lips and eyelids to trap and paralyze the deceased's spirit within. The skull itself is discarded, while the head is simmered in an iron pot filled with juices extracted from secret herbs until it is reduced to about half its natural size.

The shrunken head is then placed on a shelf, or worn along with other trophies in the caster's belt or necklace. Up to once per day, the caster can interrogate the enchanted head as if using speak with dead. Furthermore, once per day, as a standard action, the caster can temporarily release the captured soul to do his bidding for up to 1 round per caster level. Such souls are similar to wraiths, except that they do not suffer from daylight powerlessness, and do not create spawn when killing opponents.

The enchanted head has Hardness 2 and 15 hit points. If it is destroyed, the victim's wraith-spirit is released and immediately seeks out and attacks the caster. However, a released spirit only has 10 rounds to exact its revenge before it fades and disappears to whatever hell it has been denied while being the caster's prisoner.

The spell must be cast within 3 days of the victim's death.

Material Component: The severed head of a captured enemy.

XP Cost: 1,000 XP
spell-soul-vulture:
This evil spell summons an ethereal vulture that the caster can send out to attack a humanoid target. On the physical plane, the vulture attacks with its beak attack, which ignores Armor Class except for deflection, sacred, luck, divine or ability score-based AC bonuses. The attack does no damage, but drains 1d6 Wisdom on a hit. When the target is brought down to 0 Wisdom, the victim falls into a nightmare-filled sleep, and the vulture has captured a portion of his essence.

It then returns to its master and spits the essence out in the form of a worm. If the caster swallows the worm, the victim's lost Wisdom is instantly restored, however, the caster then has established a sensory link and complete control over the individual, as if the victim were subject to a dominate person spell.

Outside of a wish or miracle spell, the only way to reverse the control established by the spell is to remove the worm from the belly of the caster (where it otherwise remains) to be fed to the essence's owner.

The vulture pursues the target for the duration of the spell.

The vulture's stats are as follows:

Ethereal Vulture: Size Medium; Type Outsider; HD 1d8+2; hp 7; Init +2 (+2 Dex); Speed 10 ft., fly 80 ft. (average); AC 14 (+1 size, +2 Dex, +1 natural); Atk +0 melee (bite, 1d4+2) and +4 melee (claws [x2], 1d3+2); Special Attacks drain 1d6 Wisdom with successful bite attack, ignore material armor; SQ incorporeal, darkvision 60 ft.; AL CE; Saving Throws Fort +3, Ref +4, Will +2; Str 14, Dex 15, Con 15, Int 5, Wis 18, Cha 4. Skills: Perception +8, Survival +5; Feats: Flyby Attack, Weapon Finesse (claw, bite).

Material Component: Powdered diamond dust (worth 2,500 gp) mixed with earth from a tomb.
spell-sticks-to-serpents:
This spell allows the caster to send the spirits of dead snakes into pieces of wood, bringing them to life. The caster can create 1 venomous snake swarm per 4 caster levels, provided sufficient material components are available. The caster can command the creatures as he wishes. The creatures act normally on the last round of the spell, and disappear at the end of their turn, leaving only a pile of twigs behind.

Material Component: One twig or small branch for each snake swarm animated.
spell-witch-fire:
A small flame springs into life in one of the sorcerer's hands. It sheds a sickly green or purple light in a 20-foot radius, and dim light for an additional 20 feet.

The sorcerer can use this light as a torch for the duration of the spell. Although the sorcerer is not burned by the flame, he cannot carry weapons or items in the same hand as the witchfire.

The caster can end the spell by hurling the flame at an opponent within 15 feet. The sorcerer hits automatically, causing 3d4 points of fire damage. The target is allowed a Reflex save for half damage.
spell-glassiron: This spell grants any ordinary, non-magical glass the strong, indestructible qualities of iron. Spells that normally affect iron do not function on objects imbued with the glassiron spell, nor do spells that affect glass (such as shatter). While only a certain amount of glass can be affected with this spell, individually imbued pieces can be fused together with a glass-related Craft check. In addition, glass-related Craft checks used in combination with this spell can result in glass armor or items that are as durable as their corresponding steel counterparts.
spell-raise-island: An island of bare stone instantly appears upon the casting of this spell. The island can only appear on saltwater. It floats on the surface for the duration of the spell, but cannot be moved.
spell-spectral-sail: If a ship has lost one of its sails, this spell can save the day by creating a shimmering sail of pure magical energy that attaches itself to the yardarm indicated by the caster. The spectral sail performs precisely like a standard sail.
spell-bind-gargoyle:
Any gargoyle that enters the affected area is unable to leave it for the spell's duration. The first time it attempts to do so it may make a single Will save, and its spell resistance is applied to the spell, if any. If it succeeds its save or resists the spell, it can leave without any particular difficulty.

Otherwise, it is trapped within the spell's area for the spell's duration. It cannot make attacks or use its abilities across the edge of the spell's area. It can still leave via teleportation, or similar effects if it has them. If anything disrupts the circle of granite dust that forms the barrier of the spell's area, the spell immediately ends, though any gargoyles trapped inside the spell's area are unable to affect the circle (treat it as just outside the spell's area).

While the gargoyle is bound in the circle, the caster can attempt to coerce it into serving as a guardian of the nearby area. This functions identically to the process used to compel a creature to perform a service with the spell lesser planar binding, except that the creature cannot be compelled to perform any service other than guarding a specified building or area (you can still attempt to bargain with the gargoyle, but it is not required to uphold its end of the bargain once released, except for any agreement to guard an area).

The area to be guarded can be defined however you like, up to a maximum radius of 1 mile per caster level.

The gargoyle can be instructed to only guard it from certain individuals or certain types of creatures, or to only allow certain individuals or types of creatures to pass unmolested.

If desired, the gargoyle can be instructed to disable intruders non-lethally.
spell-adamantine-wings:
Metal: Spells with this descriptor include those that directly create, utilize, or manipulate metal in some manner or conjure creatures composed of metal. Such spells are considered to belong to the Metal element (for geomancers) and the metal elemental school (for metal elementalists).

This spell functions as metal wings except the damage dealt is considered adamantine in both the wing attacks in the cone attack.
spell-animate-fire: You animate a fire the size of a campfire. For the duration, the animated fire has the statistics of a small fire elemental. At the end of the duration, the animated fire and the original fire are extinguished. The animated fire cannot move beyond the range of the spell from the caster.
spell-animate-wood:
Wood: Spells with this descriptor include those that directly create, utilize, or manipulate plant or wood in some manner or conjure creatures with the plant subtype or composed of wood. Such spells are considered to belong to the Wood element (for geomancers) and the Wood elemental school (for wood elementalists).

You animate a small batch of wood the size of a small creature. For the duration, the animated wood has the statistics of a small animated object with a hardness of 5. This spell cannot be cast on wood objects carried or worn by another creature. At the end of the duration, the animated wood returns to its original form in its new square. The animated wood cannot move beyond the range of the spell from the caster.
spell-antienergy-sphere: A spherical energy field comes into being that matches the element you are defending against. When casting the spell you choose between acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic. All creatures within the emanation gain immunity to the chosen damage type. Additionally, any creature with the element as a subtype is unable to enter the area unless their spell resistance makes them immune to the spell. This spell gains the descriptor of the energy type chosen when cast.
spell-aspect-of-the-storm:
You float into the air, lifted by swirling winds and electricity courses through you, crackling along your body. You gain a 40 ft. fly speed and are immune to ranged non-spell ranged attacks. You are also not affected by high winds whether mundane or magical.

Additionally, as a standard action that does not provoke an attack of opportunity, you can release a bolt of lightning. This bolt has a range of 100 feet as a ranged touch attack, and you gain a +3 circumstance bonus on this attack if the target is bearing a metal object, wearing metal armor, or made of metal. This ability allows the target to apply their spell resistance if applicable. The bolt deals 1d6 electricity damage per caster level, maximum 10d6.
spell-bears-endurance-greater: This spell functions as bear's endurance, except it grants an enhancement bonus to Constitution equal to 1/2 your caster level.
spell-bears-endurance-greater-mass: This spell functions as greater bear's endurance, except that it affects multiple creatures.
spell-beckon-the-void:
Void: Spells with this descriptor are tied with a philosophical school of magic based on a concept known as the Void. The school teaches that the Void is the nothingness from which springs forth creativity, insight, spirit, thought, and also the source of pure energy from which all elements and phenomena are derived. Channeling the power of the Void (or the Void element) allows for the manipulation of the elements in objects and creatures, among other possibilities. Spells with the void descriptor are considered to belong to the Void element (for geomancers) and the void elemental school (for void elementalists).

If a spell has the [void] descriptor, it cannot be dispelled by elements release regardless of how high is your CL.

You enter a temporary state that allows you to call upon a minute portion of the Void to flow through you.

Whenever you expend at least 1 ki point with a feat or class ability to gain a bonus to your AC or a bonus that applies to a d20 roll you make, you increase the gained bonus by +1. You can only gain this increase once per use of the class ability or feat in this way.

Alternatively, if you have an expended feat or class ability, other than spells, that has no daily uses left, you may discharge this spell as an immediate action to gain one more daily use of that feat or class ability. You cannot use this effect for feat or a class ability that has a class level or skill rank prerequisite greater than the number of rounds remaining for your casting of beckon the void when you discharged the spell.

However, channeling the Void through this spell has its own limitations. You may only have 1 casting of this spell in effect on you at any time. You can only be the recipient of this spell each week no more than once per every 4 HD you possess.
spell-beyond-the-ego:
Void: Spells with this descriptor are tied with a philosophical school of magic based on a concept known as the Void. The school teaches that the Void is the nothingness from which springs forth creativity, insight, spirit, thought, and also the source of pure energy from which all elements and phenomena are derived. Channeling the power of the Void (or the Void element) allows for the manipulation of the elements in objects and creatures, among other possibilities. Spells with the void descriptor are considered to belong to the Void element (for geomancers) and the void elemental school (for void elementalists).

If a spell has the [void] descriptor, it cannot be dispelled by elements release regardless of how high is your CL.

You target an intelligent (Int 3 or higher) creature's mind and forcefully connect them to the Void, bombarding their awareness with cosmic enlightenment. This dissolves the boundaries between their ego and the observable world, leading to a state of spiritual tranquility of oneness and nothingness.

While you maintain concentration on this spell, the target gains the paralyzed condition, unable to take even mental actions. There is no initial saving throw to resist the spell from taking effect but each round at the start of their turn, the target may attempt a Will save to end the spell. A target can expend 1 ki point as an immediate action to gain an initial Will save to prevent the spell from taking effect on them.

While this spell lasts, if the target suffers any damage, affliction, or penalty, they gain a Will save immediately to end this spell.

When the spell ends, the target does not retain any memory or comprehension of the glimpsed truths and insights imparted by the Void in this way but they may have a momentary sense of loss or déjà vu.
spell-beyond-the-ego-mass:
Void: Spells with this descriptor are tied with a philosophical school of magic based on a concept known as the Void. The school teaches that the Void is the nothingness from which springs forth creativity, insight, spirit, thought, and also the source of pure energy from which all elements and phenomena are derived. Channeling the power of the Void (or the Void element) allows for the manipulation of the elements in objects and creatures, among other possibilities. Spells with the void descriptor are considered to belong to the Void element (for geomancers) and the void elemental school (for void elementalists).

If a spell has the [void] descriptor, it cannot be dispelled by elements release regardless of how high is your CL.

This spell functions as beyond the ego, except as noted above and you no longer need to maintain concentration.
spell-brimstone-flames:
You cause the target to be engulfed in sulfurous flames.

The target takes 1d6 fire damage per caster level (maximum 15d6) and are sickened for 2d4 rounds. A successful Fortitude save halves the damage and negates the sickening.
spell-calling-wind:
You can send a message or sound on the wind to a specific set of creatures you designate. You need not know the identity of the target, but you must know some important information like position, description, or location. For example, you could send a message to any members of the druid circle that are within the forest.

The wind cannot pass through walls, but if there are windows, it will attempt to pass through. The summoning wind is only discernible as a gentle breeze by those except the recipients. The message can be a single sound for which you are familiar or a message of up to 25 words.

This spell cannot be used to speak verbal components, command words, or otherwise activate magic items or effects.
spell-cats-grace-greater: This spell functions as cat's grace, except it grants an enhancement bonus to Dexterity equal to 1/2 your caster level.
spell-cats-grace-greater-mass: This spell functions as greater cat's grace, except that it affects multiple creatures.
spell-cloak-of-stone:
You surround the target in a swirling barrier of rocks, dirt and mud. The target gains soft cover and a hardness of 8. This barrier can absorb up to 10 points of damage (maximum 150 points) per caster level through its hardness before the hardness is lost.

Additionally, any creature that attacks they target in melee while adjacent or with a natural weapon, they take 1d6 bludgeoning damage. Any creature attempting to enter the target's square, like a swarm, much smaller creature, or a creature using Acrobatics, takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage each round they are in the target's square. A creature with spell resistance can apply it to resist damage from this spell. A creature can only be damaged by this spell once per round regardless of the number of attacks made or movement.
spell-cloak-of-water:
You surround the touched creature in a sea-green glow.

While underwater the target gains the benefits of blur, freedom of movement, and water breathing.

Additionally, they do not take damage from pressure. While out of the water, the target only gains the blur effect.
spell-close-to-the-sun:
You unleash deadly beams of sunlight from the magnifying glass. The target creatures are dealt 1d6 fire damage per caster level (maximum 25d6). Undead and plants are deals 1d8/level instead of 1d6, to a maximum of 25d8. Any creature that takes damage is fatigued. A successful Fortitude save halves the damage and prevents from being fatigued. Undead are not immune to this Fortitude save but they may be immune to the fatigue.

This spell must be cast within sight of the sun.
spell-cloud-boots:
You form boots out of cloud-material around the target's feet. These clouds allow them to move up or down in the air at a speed of 30 feet, laterally with a speed of 60 feet (perfect), and hover. The target cannot get more than 90-feet off the ground.

If the spell ends or is dismissed while the target is in the air, they fall to the ground as if affected by feather fall.

The target can dismiss this spell and walk normally by shaking the cloud-material off their boots.
spell-cloud-boots-mass: This spell functions as cloud boots except is affects multiple creatures as noted above.
spell-commune-with-spirit:
You contact a local spirit inhabiting the world or objects around you. You can ask the spirit one question per two caster levels. If you do not know a specific spirit in the area, you contact a random spirit. If the spirit is unwilling, you must make a Will save against the DC of this spell before getting it to cooperate. The spirit's knowledge is limited to its immediate area and will typically answer in one-word answers. However, if the one word would be misleading or contrary to the spirit's interests, the spirit can respond with a short phrase (five words or less) instead.

If you do not know a spirit is nearby for you to contact, there is a 50% chance there is no spirit and the spell fails.

If a spirit has been subject to commune with spirit within the past week, the new spell fails.
spell-control-snow-and-ice:
This spell has two different applications, both of which control snow and ice in different ways. The first version of this spell causes snow and ice in the area to swiftly melt or compact, lowering the snow and ice's depth.

The second version causes the snow and ice to grow and expand, increasing its overall depth and possibly cascading into nearby areas.

With either version of this spell, you may reduce one horizontal dimension (length or width) by half and double the other horizontal dimension to change the overall area of effect.
spell-cosmic-integration:
Void: Spells with this descriptor are tied with a philosophical school of magic based on a concept known as the Void. The school teaches that the Void is the nothingness from which springs forth creativity, insight, spirit, thought, and also the source of pure energy from which all elements and phenomena are derived. Channeling the power of the Void (or the Void element) allows for the manipulation of the elements in objects and creatures, among other possibilities. Spells with the void descriptor are considered to belong to the Void element (for geomancers) and the void elemental school (for void elementalists).

If a spell has the [void] descriptor, it cannot be dispelled by elements release regardless of how high is your CL.

Your consciousness and form temporarily fuses with the essence of the Void in a controlled state. Wrath of the heavens consumes all affected creatures, leaving no traces of their body behind; gear and clothing are unaffected. Such consumed creatures can only be restored to life via true resurrection, a carefully worded wish spell followed by resurrection, or miracle.

Affected creatures may negate the effects of the spell on them with a successful Fortitude save. The spell can only affect a number of creatures in one of the following ways that you choose:

If an affected creature has less than 10 HD and you have irrefutable and truthful proof that creature has previously deliberately, maliciously, and unjustly harmed you or your kin (related by blood or legal), that creature does not gain a Fortitude save against this spell.
spell-earths-cold:
You cause the earth to become arctic cold. Each round on your turn, including the turn the spell is cast, all creatures in contact with stone or earth within the area take 2d6 cold damage. A creature with the earth subtype instead takes 4d6 cold damage. A Fortitude save halves the damage taken in the round.

Additionally, the temperature in the area is dropped by 2 bands for the purposes of weather and temperature effects. If the area was already cold, the damage increases by 1 per dice rolled.
spell-ring-of-lightning:
You create a constantly spinning and rotating ring of lighting to encircle you. This does not interfere with you or others' spellcasting or attacks. However, the ring grants you a resistance to electricity of 20 and any creature that begins their turn adjacent to you takes 10d6 electricity damage. A successful Reflex save halves this damage.

Additionally, as a free action on your turn, you can unleash up to two lightning bolts that deal 5d6 electricity damage each in a 120-ft. Line. Each bolt may be sent in different directions. A successful Reflex save halves the damage from the bolt of lightning.
spell-searing-light-lesser: This spell functions as searing light except the ray deals 1d4 points of damage per two caster levels, the damage to undead is 1d3 per class level (maximum 10d3), and undead particularly vulnerable to sunlight take 1d4 damage per class level (maximum 10d4). Finally, constructs and objects only take 1d3 damage per two caster levels (maximum 5d3).
spell-shadowburst:
You create an explosion of vile shadow energy pulled from the maelstroms in the shadow plane. Creatures within the area take 1d8 damage per caster level (maximum 20d8) and are sickened for 2d6 rounds. Half of the damage is negative energy damage and half cold damage.

Undead creatures and creatures native to the shadow plane are immune to this spell, in fact undead are healed by the negative energy portion of the damage. A successful Fortitude save halves the damage and negates the sickened condition.
spell-shadowy-rays:
You fire off dark inky rays of shadow from the shadow plane. You can fire one ray for every two caster levels you have, maximum seven rays. You can fire all the rays at once, or one bolt per round as a free action. You are not required to fire a ray in any one round, but if they are not used up within 1 minute, they are lost. If all rays are hurled at once, all targets must be within 60 feet of each other.

You must succeed on a ranged touch attack with the ray to deal damage to a target. On a hit the target takes 2d8 points of damage to a living creature, and the target must make a Will save or be dazed for 1 round. The dazing does not stack if hit by multiple rays. Undead creatures are not damaged but they are dazed, and constructs are unaffected altogether.
spell-shocking-grasp-greater: This spell functions as shocking grasp except it deals 1d6 points of electricity damage per caster level (maximum 10d6). The target must also make a Fortitude save or be stunned for 1d4 rounds.
spell-shocking-grasp-lesser: This spell functions as shocking grasp except it deals 1d4 points of electricity damage.
spell-shout-of-the-cold-north: You let out a powerful shout empowered by the icy-cold North. All creatures within the cone take 1d6 damage per level (maximum 15d6). Half of this damage is cold, the other is sonic. A successful Reflex save halves this damage. Additionally, any creature who fails their save must make a Fortitude save or be dazed for 1 round.
spell-slashing-blade: You throw your weapon and it spins and slashes through all enemies in the line. Each enemy must be attacked separately with a standard melee attack except you substitute your spellcasting ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls. Regardless of the number of hits or misses, the weapon returns to your hand.
spell-sprawling-chaos:
You create a shifting cloud of chaotic colors and lights that functions like the fog cloud spell. Any creatures passing through the cloud take 2d6 damage from the chaotic psychic energies and if they take damage, they must make a Will save or be confused as per the spell confusion for 1d4 rounds. Additional instances of confusion do not stack, but the duration is extended by the 1d4 rolled. The damage and confusion effect are mind-affecting effects and are subject to spell resistance.

The fog cloud effect is not subject to spell resistance.
spell-starve-the-fire: You create an area where fire is weakened. All fire-based lights decreased their bright and dim radii by 10 feet. All fire-based spells and effects decrease their DC by 1 for those affected within the aura. Additionally, all fire damage dealt within the radius is decreased by 1 per dice of fire damage dealt, or by 1 if no dice are used. Finally, any creature with the fire subtype is fatigued. If they are immune to fatigue, they instead take a -1 penalty to their attack and damage rolls.
spell-stitches-start-to-tear: You pull terrible entropic power to undo the healing those in the area have gotten. All creatures in the area must make a Fortitude save, for which undead, constructs, and objects are not immune, or take damage equal to 1/2 the damage they have healed in the last 5 rounds. On a success, they take 1 damage per instance of healing they received within the last 5 rounds. The damage dealt by this spell cannot reduce a subject creature below 0 hit points.
spell-storming-grasp:
This spell functions as shocking grasp except you can make one touch per caster level within the duration.

Each touch is a separate standard action. This touch attack can be delivered as part of spell combat and spellstrike without needing to cast the spell.
spell-storming-grasp-greater:
This spell functions as greater shocking grasp except you can make one touch per caster level within the duration. Each touch is a separate standard action.

This touch attack can be delivered as part of spell combat and spellstrike without needing to cast the spell, so long as it is active.
spell-storming-grasp-lesser:
This spell functions as lesser shocking grasp except you can make one touch per caster level within the duration. Each touch is a separate standard action.

This touch attack can be delivered as part of spell combat and spellstrike without needing to cast the spell, so long as it is active.
spell-sudden-fear: On a failed saving throw, the target becomes frightened for 1 round. On a success, they are instead shaken for 1 round.
spell-sudden-panic: You create a cone of terror that makes those within panicked for 1 round if they fail their saving throw. On a success, they are shaken for 1 round.
spell-sudden-scare: This spell functions as sudden fear except as noted above and on HD up to 6 HD.
spell-suns-glow:
You create a flash of light in the area you designate. All undead and creatures with light sensitivity or light blindness take 1d6 damage +1 point per caster level (maximum +5). A successful Reflex save halves this damage.

Additionally any creature in the area glow with light equivalent to a torch for the spell's duration. A target takes a -20 penalty to Stealth checks and it shows the location of invisible creatures, though such creatures still have concealment.
spell-sunbeam-lesser: This ability functions as sunbeam except it creates one beam per four caster levels (maximum of 5 beams at 20th level). The beam dazzles and deals 2d6 points of damage. The damage is doubled against creatures harmed by sunlight and a successful Reflex save halves the damage and negates the dazzled effect. The damage to undead is capped at 5d6 instead of 20d6.
spell-symbol-of-ecstasy: This spell functions like symbol of death, except all creatures within 60 feet of a symbol of ecstasy instead are overwhelmed with joy and pleasure. They are stunned for 1 round then staggered for 1 round per level. On a successful save, the target is staggered for 1 round.
spell-tears-of-joy:
You fill the target with such overwhelming joy that they are blinded by tears and staggered. On the creature's next turn, it may attempt a new saving throw to end the effect. This is a full round action that does not provoke attacks of opportunity. If this save is successful, the effect ends.

Creatures without eyes and aquatic creatures are not blinded, but they are still staggered. A creature with an Intelligence score of 2 or lower is not affected.
spell-tears-of-joy-mass: This spell functions as tears of joy except it affects multiple creatures.
spell-thoughteater: This spell functions as detect thoughts except you gain 2 temp hp per creature whose thoughts you read in the 3rd round of the spell. You can gain a maximum number of temp hp from this spell equal to double your class level. This temp hp last for 1 hour and stack with other sources of temp hp except from this spell.
spell-throatshards:
You summon sharp shards of glass into the throat of the target creature. At the beginning of their turn, the target must make a Fortitude save. On a failure, the target takes 2d4 magical slashing damage, 1 bleed damage, and is unable to speak or use spells or abilities that require vocal components or linguistic communication. On a failure, they only take 1d4 magical slashing damage but must make the save next round.

Creatures without throats are not affected. If the creature has multiple throats, it only prevents one throat from vocalizing.
spell-throne-of-ash:
You summon a mass of burning ash under you. You are 20 feet higher at the center, the ash pile then drops 5 feet down and then slopes down to the edges. The area is considered difficult terrain to all creatures, aside from yourself, due to the shifting ash and the angle of the hill.

Additionally, targets within the area take 1d6 fire damage and must make a Reflex save or catch fire.

Flammable, unattended objects catch fire after 1 round.

Any creature that does not move on their turn sinks down as if in quicksand.

Your movement is not impeded, in fact your speed is doubled while in the area and you can get up to the apex of the pile as if it were flat.

At the end of the duration, the ash vanishes, leaving no aftereffects (except the damage and burning objects or creatures).
spell-thunderous-cacophony:
You fill the area with roaring thunderous crashes. Each creature beginning their turn in or entering the area takes 4d6 points of sonic damage and is deafened for 2 rounds. This deafening does not stack on consecutive rounds, but it extends the duration. A successful Fortitude save halves the damage and negates the deafening.

This cacophony has the added effect of disrupting other auditory effects. Any such language-dependent, auditory, or sonic effect only has a 50% chance of being effective against a creature in the area each round.
spell-tongues-of-hell:
You touch the corpse and allow fiendish presences to speak through it. The corpse will spit out random sentences for 1 round. There is only a 10% chance the information related is useful to you, but it is difficult to distinguish whether the information is useful (the GM makes the percentile roll in secret). If you are good aligned, or if a good-aligned creature is within 10 feet of the corpse, you are unable to get any useful information through the corpse.

Useful information may include warnings about dangers deeper in a dungeon, the command word to a magic item, or even vague and spectral warnings of your or your companions' future. The GM decides what information, useful or not, is related by the fiendish presence.

Once a corpse has been subject to tongues of hell by any caster, any new attempt to cast tongues of hell on that corpse fails. You can cast this spell on a corpse that has been deceased for any amount of time, but the head of the corpse must have a mouth in order to speak at all.

This spell doesn't affect a corpse that has been turned into an undead creature.
spell-true-strike-greater:
This spell functions as true strike except you can expend it anytime during the spell's duration.

Additionally, if you have multiple attacks, you can expend this spell as part of the full attack action and spread out the total bonus provided by the spell over the multiple attacks however you want. For example, if you have three attacks, you could apply 5 of the bonus to the first attack, 5 of the bonus to the second attack, and 10 to the final one.
spell-umbral-offering: You complete the sacrifice and anoint each creature to be protected with some part of the sacrifice, typically blood or ash, leaving the rest to the denizens of the plane of shadow. For the duration the protected 33 creatures gain a +2 bonus on initiative checks and Knowledge (planes), Knowledge (religion), Perception, Stealth, and Survival skill checks while in the plane of shadow or regarding creatures with the shadow subtype, and light spells cast by affected creatures are not impeded on the plane of shadow. The effects of this spell stack with the favored terrain ability. Additionally, any creature with the shadow subtype begins with a neutral disposition and will not run from nor attack a protected creature, unless attacked first or impelled by some outside means. This spell cannot be used for urban terrain. Any intelligent creature gets a Will save to negate the effects of the impelled peace and neutrality.
spell-under-the-nails: You bring the sensation of needles being driven under the fingernails (or similar digit) of the target. The target takes 1d4 nonlethal damage per caster level (maximum 5d4) and drops any held items. A successful Fortitude save halves the damage and negates the dropping of the items.
spell-under-the-nails-mass: This spell functions as under the nails except it affects multiple creatures and the maximum damage is increased to 10d4.
spell-vitrified-earth:
This spell functions as transmute mud to rock except the resulting 'rock' is more akin to glass or obsidian and the spell can be cast upon already rocky earth. All creatures touching or within the affected earth take 1d6 fire damage per caster level (maximum 10d6) and half that damage dealt the following round. A successful Reflex save halves this damage, however creatures inside of the affected earth, like using burrow, earthglide or stuck in quicksand automatically fail their saving throw.

As a side effect, if the affected area is or becomes wet, it becomes difficult terrain because the rock is slick.
spell-void-death:
You create a localized void from between the stars around a target. The target is surrounded with a 5-foot-radius darkness as per the darkness spell and there is no air (or other gas or liquid) to breathe so the target must hold their breath. Additionally, the target takes 2d6 cold damage each round at the beginning of their turn. A successful Fortitude save at the beginning of their turn halves the cold damage taken that round. Creatures who do not breathe do not need to hold their breath. If a creature is killed by the cold damage, their body explodes into small chunks.

As an interesting side effect, non-magical fires in the space occupied by the target are snuffed out.
spell-void-song: You create a series of notes that call upon the utter cold atmosphere of the void between the stars. Any creature in the area takes 1d8 points of cold damage per caster level (maximum 5d8) and is staggered for 1 round as the air is sucked from their lungs. A successful Fortitude save halves the damage and negates the staggered condition. Creatures that do not breathe are not staggered.
spell-void-walker:
You may transform into an embodiment of the void between the stars as a standard action and instantly travel in a straight line to a distance of up to 120 feet, rematerializing in the new location as a free action.

This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity. Creatures in this line take 10d6 points of cold damage and are staggered as they catch their lost breath for 1 round (a successful Fortitude save halves the damage and negates the staggered condition, spell resistance applies, creatures who do not breathe are immune to the staggering). The area you traverse is treated as if affected by the darkness spell until the beginning of your next turn. If your path is interrupted by a barrier or otherwise deflected, you materialize short of your final destination in the nearest open space; targets in the line to that point take damage as normal. You are immune to cold while this spell lasts.
spell-wearing-hell:
You take on the form of a devil one size category larger or smaller than yourself. You cannot look like a specific devil, but otherwise you can give your devil form unique features.

The spell does not provide the abilities or mannerisms of the chosen devil, nor does it alter the perceived tactile (touch). However, the sounds created by your equipment are masked and you make any natural, or ambient, sounds of the chosen devil. You gain a +10 bonus a the Disguise check to impersonate as a devil. A creature that interacts with the glamer gets a Will save to recognize it as an illusion.

Additionally, your presence instills fear in mortals that perceive you. Any non-outsider that sees you and is within 30 feet must make a Will save or be shaken for 1 round/level. If the target is under 5 HD, they are frightened for 1d4 rounds before becoming shaken for 1 round/level. This fear portion of the spell is a mind-affecting, fear effect.
spell-white-dagger: You create a 1-foot-long beam of pure-white positive energy. This beam sheds light like a torch and may be wielded like a dagger. Attacks with the white dagger are melee touch attacks, and can be thrown as a ranged touch attack. If thrown, the white dagger reappears in your hand at the end of your turn. The dagger deals 1d4 points of positive energy damage + 1 point per two caster levels (maximum +10). If the target is undead or otherwise harmed by positive energy, the damage dice is increased to 1d8. Since the blade is immaterial, your Strength modifier does not apply to the damage.
spell-mystic-preparation:
You gain an innate sense of magic occurring in your vicinity. You become automatically aware of a spell or spell-like ability being cast within 100 feet of you, so long as you have line of effect to the caster. You gain an automatic attempt to identify the spell with a +5 bonus to your Spellcraft check.

If you succeed on this check, you can discharge this spell as an immediate action to attempt to dispel the spell you identified, if you have a spell available to counter the spell. You do not need to see the spellcaster to counterspell, so long as you have line of effect.
spell-purification-through-blood: You cut your palm and touch the target with your bloody hand. The blood then attempts to cleanse the target of impurities. This spell functions as lesser restoration, remove disease, and neutralize poison except that you take damage based on what you heal or grant a chance to thwart. You take 2d10 damage when attempting to cure a poison or disease or 1d10 damage when removing fatigue or 1d10 per ability score healed (maximum 4). You may choose to cure between 1 and 4 ability score damage when touching the target instead of rolling 1d4. You may also do all or some of the curative effects, taking the damage for each component. However, the disease and poison removal is not guaranteed as per those spells. The damage accrued when casting this spell cannot be mitigated or prevented, but can be healed normally.
spell-red-chord: You create a sound that resonates in the material and negative energy planes. All creatures within the spread take 1d4 damage per caster level. Half of the damage is sonic, the other half is negative energy. The negative energy does not heal undead, nor does it harm them.
spell-rise-again: This spell functions as lesser rise again except it can revive a creature who was killed by a death effect and prevents them from instantaneously becoming an undead if applicable.
spell-rise-again-greater: This spell functions as rise again except it returns the target to full health and condition and can affect a creature who was destroyed as per the spell resurrection.
spell-rise-again-lesser:
You instill the target with a spell that will return them to life if they die during the duration. If the target dies while the spell is active, they are returned to life and cured of 5d8 points of damage + 1 point per caster level (maximum +25). This cannot heal or revive a target killed by a death effect, turned into an undead instantly, or if their body is destroyed or not intact. This also cannot revive a creature who dies of old age. The creature must want to be revived and the spell cannot be cast on a creature who is already dead or undead.

Any ability damage or other ongoing effects continue to affect the target and can kill them, though a 0 Con is set a 1 when this spell triggers.

Once the target is revived, this spell ends.
spell-river-of-light:
You create a wavering beam of light that shoots away from you in a direction you choose. It creates a 5-ft.-diameter line of light. It remains constant in the direction it is created, but may be changed on your turn as a move action.

A creature that begins their turn in or enters the area of the river of light, the target takes 5d6 damage. If the affected creature is undead or vulnerable to sunlight, the damage is increased to 10d4. Constructs or inanimate objects only take 2d6 damage each round. A successful Fortitude save, for which undead are not immune, halves the damage taken that round.
spell-scarlet-halo: You create a blood-red halo behind your head that grants you dark power. You detect as an evil cleric equal to your caster level if you do not already, and all of your attacks are considered evil for damage reduction purposes. Additionally, you gain a +2 enhancement bonus to your Strength and Charisma.
spell-shattered-self: You turn into a swarm composed of fleshy bits that are the same size as your normal form. You gain the distract ability and swarm traits for the duration. You lose all weapon attacks but retain the ability to cast spells and a swarm attack that deals 1d4 per 4 caster levels you possess. All your other traits remain the same.
spell-sludgehammer: You create a mass of caustic sludge that you bring violently down in the area. The spell deals 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 15d6). Half the damage is acid damage and half bludgeoning an affected creature is slowed as per the spell slow for 1d4 rounds afterward. A successful Reflex save halves the damage and negates the slowing effect.
spell-sphere-of-madness:
A scintillating globe of chaotic energy rolls in whichever direction you point and impacts those it strikes. It moves 30 feet per round. As part of this movement, it can ascend or jump up to 30 feet to strike a target. If it enters a space with a creature, it stops moving for the round and deals 5d6 points of damage to that creature, though a successful Reflex save negates that damage. If a target is damaged, they also must make a Will save or be confused as per the spell confusion for 1d4 rounds.

Multiple instances of confusion do not stack but the duration is increased. A sphere of madness rolls over barriers less than 4 feet tall.

The sphere moves as long as you actively direct it (a move action for you); otherwise, it merely stays at rest.

The surface of the sphere has a spongy, yielding consistency and so does not cause damage except by the chaotic psychic energy. It cannot push aside unwilling creatures or batter down large obstacles. A sphere of madness winks out if it exceeds the spell's range.
spell-spiritual-agony: This spell functions as lesser spiritual agony except the damage is increased to 1d6 nonlethal per caster level (maximum 15d6) and the target is nauseated for 1d6 rounds, then sickened for 1 minute thereafter. A successful save halves the damage and reduces the effect to sickened for 1 minute.
