spell-spiritual-agony-greater: This spell functions as lesser spiritual agony except the damage is increased to 1d6 nonlethal per caster level (maximum 20d6) and the target is nauseated for 1 round per level, then sickened for 10 minutes thereafter. A successful save halves the damage and reduces the effect to sickened for 10 minutes.
spell-spiritual-agony-lesser:
You instill a divinely-empowered creature with pain.

The target must be a creature with class levels in a class that grants divine spellcasting or has supernatural abilities that draw their power from a divine source. It also affects aligned outsiders. The target takes 4d8 nonlethal damage and is nauseated for 1 round, then sickened for 1 minute. A successful saving throw halves the damage and reduces the condition to sickened for 1d4 rounds.
spell-ring-of-blades:
You create a ring of spinning blades within an area of 5 feet around you. This ring of blades stays with you, and at the end of your turn, any creature within the area takes 1d6 non-magical slashing damage + 1 point per caster level (maximum +10). Such creatures can make a Reflex save to halve this damage.

Additionally, when casting the spell, if you use a weapon with the corresponding damage type, the blades can be considered silver or cold iron for damage reduction purposes. However, if the damage is silver, the slashing damage is reduced by 1.
spell-abrasive-hallucinations:
This spell functions as hallucinatory terrain except the terrain is harmful to those that believe in it. Any creature that enters the area and fails the Will save takes 1d8 magical piercing or slashing damage per 10 feet they move within the area and if they enter or begin their turn within as the sharp rocks and barbed plants tear at their flesh. Each round when they would take damage, they may make another Will save to disbelieve.

On a successful Will save, any damage taken by the spell is converted to nonlethal damage as the affected creature realizes it was a hallucination.
spell-acid-coat: This spell functions like the lesser acid coat spell except the damage dealt is 1d6/level (maximum 5d6) and the duration of the reduction is 1d4 rounds.
spell-acid-coat-lesser: You envelop the target a coat of acid dealing 1d4 acid damage. This reduces the hardness of objects and DR of constructs by 1 for 1 round. A successful Reflex save halves this damage and negates the hardness/DR reduction.
spell-acid-rain: Caustic rain pours down in the area for 1 round. All creatures beginning their turn in or entering the area take 6d6 acid damage, no save. For 1 round per caster level, the ground is muddy or slick causing it to be difficult terrain. Any creature that moves more than 10 feet in the difficult terrain takes 1d4 acid damage.
spell-acrid-death: You conjure a mass of acid within the target, causing it to burst forth dealing 10 points of acid damage per caster level. If the target's Fortitude saving throw succeeds, it instead takes 3d6 points of acid damage + 1 point per caster level. The target then takes 1d4 acid damage each round for 1d6 rounds thereafter, whether they succeed on the saving throw or not.
spell-aimless-arrow-lesser: This spell functions as lesser aimless arrow except the target is subject to a 50% miss chance.
spell-alert: All targets of this spell are alerted with a mental alarm at the same, predetermined point in time. The time is chosen by the caster when the spell is cast and it must be within the duration of the spell. Once the alarm is activated, the spell ends.
spell-altar-of-flesh: You carve symbols of your dark god into a corpse. From then on, it acts as a religious site or altar for other spells or abilities such as desecrate. If the corpse is destroyed, raised as an undead creature, or returned to life, the effect is lost.
spell-animate-element: The caster animates a small section of air, earth, fire, or water. The animated element has the statistics of a Small elemental, and attacks as directed by the caster. It cannot move beyond the range of the spell.
spell-animate-element-3pp-orphaned-bookw:
Speaking to nature you coalesce a helpful elemental.

When you cast this spell you must touch the element you wish to animate. You may animate air, earth, fire, or water with this spell. Animating the element in question grants you control over a small elemental of that type. At 5th caster level you may use this spell to animate a medium elemental, at 9th caster level you may animate a large elemental and at 13th caster level you may animate a huge elemental. You must be able to touch a source of the element you wish to animate of the equivalent size. The elemental can be directed as a move action on your turn. When not given orders it will defend you and attack enemies that threaten you or your allies.

You may instead cast this spell as a ritual which takes 10 minutes and 500 gp in supplies. If you do, its duration becomes 1 day per caster level. You may only have one such casting of animate element active at a time.

This spell gains the descriptor associated with the element animated.
spell-animate-instrument: You complete the spell and your instrument hovers next to you and keeps up your tune and maintains the effects of your bardic performance, assuming it is instrument-based. While the instrument is maintaining your bardic performance, you do not suffer any possibility of failure from being deaf nor does the performance end when you are killed, paralyzed, stunned or unconscious. The spell continues to use your rounds of bardic performance unless you use an action to change or end it. If you are killed, paralyzed, stunned or unconscious, you cannot stop or change the performance and the performance active before the condition will continue until the spell expires, you run out of bardic performance rounds, or you regain the ability to change the performance.
spell-anticipate-teleportation: This spell functions as anticipate teleportation except it identifies the type of creature arriving, and if the creature is known to the target of the spell, the creature's identity. Additionally, the delay increases up to 3 rounds, as determined when cast.
spell-antimagic-burst:
Antimagic burst causes a globe of force to explode silently from a point you select. All creatures in the globe are sickened for 1d6 rounds and take 6d6 force damage. A summoned creature takes double damage. A successful Reflex save negates the sickening and reduces the damage by half.

A construct caught within the globe takes 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 25d6), or half damage if a Reflex save is successful. Constructs can't be immune to this spell even though it has spell resistance.

Any summoned creature not destroyed by the spell is subject to a dispel magic effect.
spell-antimagic-ray:
You must succeed at a ranged touch attack to affect a target. The target, if struck, functions as if inside an antimagic field if it fails its Will save.

If the spell is used on a creature, they cannot cast spells, use supernatural abilities or spell-like effects, nor can they be affected by such. The target can still use spell completion (such as scrolls) or spell trigger items (such as wands), though they must use Use Magic Device to emulate the ability to cast the spells.

If the spell is used on an object, its magic powers are suppressed, as are any spells currently active on the object (like light or darkness). It also cannot be targeted by spells, supernatural abilities or spell-like abilities.

This ray will not affect objects except the target of the ray. For example, if a creature affected by the antimagic ray, their magic items still function normally.
spell-armor-of-light: The target is covered in an armor of pure light. The target gains a +4 deflection bonus to their AC. This AC bonus increases by +1 for every three levels above 7th, to a maximum of +8 at 19th level. This armor sheds light like a torch. The target also gains an additional +2 bonus to AC and to their saves against darkness, evil, and shadow effects. If the target is living, they also gain a +4 bonus on saves vs. channel negative energy, touch of corruption, or similar abilities.
spell-armor-of-light-3pp-rite-publishing: This spell causes the creature touched to radiate light from every part of her body. She sheds bright light to a radius of 30 feet and shadowy light an additional 30 feet beyond that. Looking directly at the target creature is difficult, granting concealment to the target (20% miss chance) and dazzling anybody who looks directly at the target for 1d6 rounds (Will negates). If a creature looks at the target more than once, she will be re-dazzled. The durations of the dazzle effects do not stack but are renewed whenever the creature becomes re-dazzled. The armor of light also provides a +1 deflection bonus to AC per four caster levels (to a maximum of +5 at 20th level).
spell-armor-of-shadow:
The target is covered in armor that seems to eat light.

The target gains a +4 deflection bonus to their AC.

This AC bonus increases by +1 for every three levels above 7th, to a maximum of +8 at 19th level. This armor does not impede sight or lower light levels, but it grants the target darkvision out to 60 ft. if they do not already possess it. The target also gains an additional +2 bonus to AC and to their saves against good or light effects. If the target is undead they also gain a +4 channel resistance.
spell-arrow-of-vengeance-greater: This spell functions as arrow of vengeance except that if it hits it is automatically a critical hit and it deals extra damage equal to 1/2 your caster level in addition to your Wisdom or Charisma bonus.
spell-avalanche:
You conjure an overwhelming avalanche of ice and snow and the squares of snow must be contiguous. All creatures in an area covered by the avalanche taking 10d6 bludgeoning damage and 10d6 cold damage. The targets must make a Reflex save or be carried along, downhill or in a direction of the caster's choice on a flat surface, by 5 feet per caster level and be knocked prone.

The targets move until an obstacle prevents the movement. The avalanche also extinguishes normal fires. The snow and ice remain in the area until they melt normally.
spell-avalanche-3pp-rogue-genius-games:
An avalanche spell may be cast anywhere on the same plane as the caster. The caster must be able to see the target area, either directly, with the aid of a spyglass, or through some form of divination at least as accurate as normal sight (such as a scrying spell, or the use of a crystal ball).

The spell creates a mass of snow and ice that crashes onto the effected area. This deals 1d8 points of cold damage per two caster levels (maximum 10d8) and affects every creature and object that takes damage as if hit with a bull rush with a CMB of 10 + caster level. All creatures and objects moved by the bull rush are pushed directly away from the center of the spell.
spell-awake: You release a burst of energy that causes all creatures within the burst to be instantly awakened, regardless of the means by which they were put to sleep. This also dispels the effects of the spell lullaby or similar effects that makes the target more prone to sleep specifically.
spell-ball-shadow:
You create two globes of shadow that fly in whichever direction you indicate. For every 4 caster levels above 7th, you create an additional globe of shadow (3 globes at 11th, 4 globes at 15th, to the maximum of 5 globes at 19th). These globes fly at a rate of 20 feet per round and have perfect maneuverability. Wind does not affect a flying sphere's course.

If a globe enters a space with a creature, it stops moving for the round and deals 3d6 points of negative energy damage to that creature, though a successful Fortitude save negates the damage. Undead creatures are healed by 3d6.

Each globe moves as long as you actively direct it (it's a move action for you to direct all the spheres created by a single casting of this spell); otherwise they stay at rest.

These globes have no mass and cannot push aside unwilling creatures or move solid objects. A ball shadow globe winks out if it exceeds the spell's range.
spell-barricade:
You manipulate your gravity field and shape it into the form of a transparent barrier that surrounds you, protecting you from weapon attacks delivered by spells, firearms, and ranged weapons. The impact from such attacks on the barrier are visible in some fashion.

Any bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage dealt to you from a ranged attack or ranged spell is reduced by 1 for every 2 caster levels. While this effect is similar to DR, it does not count as DR for the purpose of how it interacts with other effects that increase or bypass DR, and it does not stack with other external effects outside of your body that reduce damage dealt from ranged attacks.

The protection provided by barricade can only reduce up to a total amount of damage equal to 20 + twice your caster level. Once the total is reached or exceeded, any reduced amount over the total is dealt normally and the barrier is overloaded and the spell ends.

Barricade does not protect against melee attacks, energy damage (such as fire or electricity), thrown improvised weapons (including items dropped on you), and environmental hazards. Subsequent castings of barricade on yourself while an on-going barricade is still active will only reset the duration of its effects, not how much damage it can absorb.
spell-barricade-greater: This spell functions as per barricade, except as above and the amount of damage it reduces is equal to your caster level. Additionally, the total amount of damage it can absorb over the course of its duration before being overloaded is equal to 50 + 5 times your caster level.
spell-battlefield-obscuring: This spell functions as obscuring mist except as noted above.
spell-beacon-of-faith: You raise the symbol of your faith high and it emits a divine light. The nature of the light depends upon your faith but it creates a light similar to a torch. Any creature within the light of the spell that shares your deity or faith, including yourself, gains a +1 bonus to damage rolls, AC, and saving throws. The bonus provided is either sacred or profane depending on the alignment of your deity or faith. While the holy symbol need not be held aloft for the spell to be maintained, it must remain visible and shedding light for the benefits to be provided.
spell-bestow-curse-lesser:
You place a curse on the subject. Choose one of the following.

You may also invent your own curses, but it should be no more powerful than those described above.

The curse bestowed by this spell cannot be dispelled, but it can be removed with a break enchantment, limited wish, miracle, remove curse, or wish spell.
spell-bestow-curse-minor:
You place a curse on the subject. Choose one of the following.

You may also invent your own curses, but it should be no more powerful than those described above.
spell-betrayed-by-light:
Targets one creature/level, no two of which can be more than 30 ft. apart

This spell functions as betrayed by light except as notated above.
spell-black-antlers:
You cast the spell and grow black antlers akin to a deer except they seem to absorb light. In actuality, they are made of void material from the dark tapestry. These antlers do not harm you but they grant you a gore attack you can make in place of your normal attack or as a secondary attack at a -5 penalty. The attack is against touch AC and deals 1d8 damage per two caster levels (maximum 5d8 damage at 10th level). Half of the damage dealt is force damage, the other half is cold. You are considered proficient with this attack.

When you cast this spell any light spell of 4th level or lower cast by you ends and you are unable to cast light spells while this spell is active.
spell-black-bridge: This spell draws from the plane of shadow to create a bridge of solid darkness. It can support 200 pounds per caster level. If the weight limit of the bridge is exceeded, the most recent creature or object to enter the area of effect falls through the bridge as though it weren't there, this process continues until the weight limit is no longer exceeded.
spell-black-mirror:
You cast the spell and spend time gazing into the dark mirror. You see events that will unfold in the future but the mirror presents indistinct images and no direct context on time the events will occur. Each day thereafter when preparing or regaining your spells, you roll a d100 and if you roll higher than a 70, you gain the benefit for the day. Each day in which you roll under a 70, the number you must exceed decreases by 5, resetting to 70 on a success. Anytime during the day you may gain one of the following benefits:

Once you have used one of the benefits, you must wait until the next successful D100 roll to be able to use it again. You gain a number of successful uses of this spell equal to your spellcasting modifier before the spell expires. Multiple castings of this spell do not add additional uses of this spell, nor can you benefit from them concurrently. If the spell is cast again before the previous one expires, the number of successful uses resets.
spell-black-sword-of-winter: A sword-shaped sheet of the blackest ice springs forth from your hand. You wield this weapon as a longsword, though you are treated as proficient, even if you are not normally proficient. Attacks with the black sword of winter are touch attacks. The blade deals 1d4 cold damage and 1d4 negative energy damage per 2 class levels per hit. This negative energy damage does not heal undead creatures. You cannot apply ability scores to this damage dealt or apply any feats that affect the weapon damage like Power Attack or Vital Strike.
spell-black-waves:
This spell functions as lesser black waves except as above and the damage dealt increases to 1d6/CL (max 10d6).

Additionally, the maximum healing to undead increases to 10.
spell-black-waves-greater:
This spell functions as lesser black waves except as above and the damage dealt increases to 1d6/CL (max 15d6).

Additionally, the maximum healing to undead increases to 15.
spell-black-waves-lesser: You release waves of black necromantic energy. Any creature in the area takes 1d4 points of negative energy damage per caster level (maximum 5d4). Undead within the area instead heal 1 damage per caster level (maximum 5).
spell-blackbraid:
You point at the creature, the braided hair disappearing from your hand and powerful braids of hair burst forth around the target, trying to entrap them. You make a CMB check against the target using your spellcasting modifier instead of your Strength modifier and no penalties or benefits for size.

If the target breaks the grapple or the grapple attempt fails, the blackbraid attempts the grapple attempt again at the beginning of the target's next turn. The blackbraid's CMD is 10 + your spellcasting ability modifier, your Dexterity modifier, and your base attack bonus.
spell-blackened-skies: You blend your current plane with the shadow plane and shade the skies around you, nearly blotting out the sun. The entire area is considered dim light, unless it is darker, and the effects of sunlight are removed altogether. Any spell that deals damage via light is halved within the radius and any additional sunlight effects from those spells are removed.
spell-blast-of-flame:
You unleash a blast of flame in the area. Each creature in the area takes 1d6 fire damage per caster level (maximum 10d6). A successful saving throw halves this damage.

Flammable materials burn if the flames touch them. A character can extinguish burning items as a full-round action.
spell-blinding-faith:
Targets one creature/level, no two of which can be more than 30 ft. apart

This spell functions as blinding faith except as noted above.
spell-blinding-nightmare-hex:
You place a curse on the target plaguing them with terrors when they are in the darkness or cannot see. If the target fails their initial Will save they are cursed. Until the duration expires or the spell is removed by any spell that can dispel a curse, the target is shaken while unable to see, or in dim light or darker. If the target enters or begins their turn in an area of dim light, they get a Will save to negate the shaken condition for 1 minute. There is no save for when the target is blinded or in darkness. Ability to see in the dark by any means does not negate the shaken condition.

Additionally, these terrors make it difficult to sleep.

Anytime the target attempts to sleep, they must make another Will save or awaken Fatigued until they get a restful night's sleep.
spell-blinding-touch:
You channel negative energy through your touch, blinding the target. You must succeed on a touch attack to strike a target. The subject is immediately blinded for the spell's duration, though they get a new save each round at the end of their turn to end the effect..

This spell has no effect on a creature that is already blind or sightless.
spell-blink-greater: This spell functions as the spell blink, except you can control the timing of the blinking between the ethereal and material planes. You have no chance of interfering with your own attack, spells or abilities and you can ready an action to blink away from an attack or effect that would normally affect you, assuming they can't affect ethereal targets (such as force effects). While moving through solid objects, you do not risk blinking into the material plane while inside unless you end your movement there. In that case it acts as normal for the blink spell.
spell-blistering-gust: This spell functions as gust of wind, creating a severe blast of air that originates from you, affecting all creatures in its path. Any creature in the area of effect takes 1d6 fire damage per two caster levels (to a maximum of 10d6 at caster level 20) and is fatigued by the rush of heat. A successful Fortitude save halves this damage and negates the fatigued condition. If you choose to maintain the effect a new save is required each round. This effect can cause a fatigued creature to become exhausted.
spell-blood-mantra: You let out a chant or series of sounds that resound that heightens the blood of you and your allies. For as long as you concentrate on the spell, you and your allies gain a +2 morale bonus on attack rolls, damage rolls, and saving throws.
spell-blood-upon-stone-lesser: This spell functions as lesser blood upon stone except you create a Huge animated object. This can also be made permanent with the permanency spell with a minimum caster level of 13th and 11,000 gp.
spell-bloodlust-contamination:
You cast the spell on a single target sending them into a blinding rage. If the target fails their Will save, they are sent into a rage gaining a +2 morale bonus to Strength and Constitution, a +1 morale bonus on Will saves, and a -2 penalty to AC. The effect is otherwise identical with a barbarian's rage including the fatigue at the end of the rage. The rage lasts for one round per caster level.

Even if the initial target succeeds on their Will save, they can still cause adjacent creatures to fly into a rage, see below.

For the duration of the spell, anytime the original target or a creature subject to the rage effect of this spell is adjacent to a creature who is not currently raging, that adjacent creature must make a Will save or be subject to the rage effect for one round per caster level. This rage effect can last longer than the duration of the original spell. The original target of the spell is not subject to making a Will save from being adjacent to itself while not raging but may be affected by others.

The rage can be triggered on a creature that is fatigued, unlike barbarian rage and any fear effect is suppressed while the creature is subject to the rage effect.
spell-bombardment:
You cause a rain of rocks to rain down and cover creatures in the area. On a failed saving throw, each creature takes 1d8 points of damage per caster level (maximum 20d8) and is buried under rubble (see avalanche rules). A successful save halves the damage and avoids the burial.

Creatures trapped in the rubble are subject to suffocation until they crawl out from the debris.
spell-bone-twister:
You must center the spell on one or more corpses that have bones. The bones are torn from the bodies within the radius, making them not considered whole for the purposes of raise dead or similar spells. The bones are then shattered and turned into deadly shards that spin in a tornado. Those within the tornado, with the exception of you if applicable, take 1d6 slashing, piercing, and bludgeoning damage per 2 caster levels.

This damage is subject to damage reduction but not spell resistance but a successful Reflex save halves the damage taken during the round.

As a move action on your round you can direct the tornado to move up to 30 feet in the direction you designate.
spell-boneblade:
The caster changes a bone into a blade of the caster's choosing. The boneblade may take the form of any weapon in the light blades or heavy blade fighter weapon groups. This weapon has a +1 enhancement bonus on attacks and damage for every five caster levels, minimum +1 and to a maximum of +4. The blade only gains enhancement bonuses and will not gain other weapon special abilities aside from the following.

This blade deals an extra + 1d6 points of damage to living targets and an additional + 1d6 points of damage to good-aligned targets.

This spell confers no proficiency with the blade, but the caster doesn't need to be the one wielding the blade for it to be effective.
spell-bottomless-pit:
Effect 10-ft.-by-10-ft. hol.

This spell functions as create pit except there is no bottom to the pit so the creatures that fall into the pit, fall until the end of the duration or they find some other means of stopping a fall.

If the creature can fly, they are immune to this spell's effects as long as they make a Fly check against the save DC of the spell. Each round such a flying creature can reattempt the Fly check to catch themselves. On their turn a falling creature can attempt to cast a spell if they have the ability, however, the creature must make a concentration check as if they took 6d6 falling damage that turn. The walls of the pit are difficult to get a hold of and falling creatures must make a DC 35 Climb check to stop their fall, and the same Climb DC to climb up its sides.

Each full round spent falling in the extradimensional pit counts as 60 feet. If the creature is able to fly or levitate, they must move the total distance they fell before they can leave the pit. If a creature moves up to the bottomless pit and fails their Reflex save, they deduct their previous movement from the 60 feet maximum fall during the turn, to a minimum of 10 feet.

Retrieving and using items is very difficult while falling in the pit. Any creature attempting to retrieve and use an item, like a potion or a scroll, must make a Reflex save or drop the item. They can attempt the same Reflex save each round on their turn to grab the item out of the air next to them. At the end of the spell's duration, falling items do not take damage.

At the end of the duration of the spell, the creatures in the pit are shunted back out of the extradimensional area taking 1d6 damage per 10 feet from the top of the pit, to a maximum of 1d6 per caster level (maximum 20d6). Effects like slow fall or feather fall do not negate this damage but such creatures only fall 30 feet per full round and only are treated as taking 3d6 damage for their concentration check.
spell-bound-by-misery:
Targets one or more creatures, no two of which can be more than 30 ft. apart

This spell functions as bound by misery except that it affects multiple creatures as noted above.
spell-bramble-spear:
You cause the weapon to sprout vicious thorns and spikes. You must cast this spell on a weapon with a wooden striking surface, including ironwood weapons.

For the duration of the spell the weapon deals bludgeoning, slashing, and piercing damage and gains a +1 enhancement bonus for every three caster levels you possess. This stacks with any existing enhancement bonus up to +5.
spell-brimstone-heart: This spell functions like lesser brimstone heart, except you gain low-light vision, darkvision 60, resistance to cold and fire 10, and DR 5/good, and you sprout dark, leathery wings allowing you to fly at a speed of 30 feet with average maneuverability. In addition, your natural weapons and any weapons you wield are considered evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.
spell-brimstone-heart-greater: This spell functions like lesser brimstone heart, except you gain low-light vision; darkvision 60 feet; DR 15/good; immunity to cold, fire, and poison; resistance to acid and electricity 10; a +4 racial bonus on saves against compulsion; a spell resistance of 11 plus your caster level, and see in darkness and telepathy out to 100 feet as supernatural abilities for the duration of the spell. Also, your wings give you a fly speed of 60 feet with good maneuverability.
spell-brimstone-heart-lesser: You take on an aspect of a fiendish being, including some of its physical characteristics. You gain low-light vision, resistance to cold 5, resistance to fire 5, and the benefits of protection from good.
spell-broken-blades:
All weapons within the radius rust, tarnish, and splinter. They gain the broken condition and their hardness is halved.

Any weapon removed from the aura loses the broken condition unless it sustained enough damage otherwise.
spell-brutalist-imperitor: This spell functions like lesser brutalist imperitor, except you gain low-light vision, a +5 resistance bonus against poison, death, disease, and sleep effects, and DR 5/chaos, and you gain regeneration 5/chaotic. In addition, your natural weapons and any weapons you wield are considered lawfully-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.
spell-brutalist-imperitor-greater:
This spell functions like lesser brutalist imperitor, except you gain low-light vision; DR 10/good; immunity to death effects, disease, mind-affecting effects, necromancy effects, paralysis, poison, sleep, and stun; a spell resistance of 11 plus your caster level, truespeech. Also, your regeneration increases to 10/chaos.

Truespeech allows you to speak with any creature that has a language, as though using the tongues spell.
spell-brutalist-imperitor-lesser: You take on an aspect of a being of axis, including some of its physical characteristics. You gain low-light vision, a +5 resistance bonus against poison and disease effects, and the benefits of protection from chaos.
spell-burdened-by-life: You focus negative energy on a number of targets in the area. Living creatures targeted by this spell are affected by the slow spell. Any undead targeted by this spell gains a bonus to their channel resistance equal to 1/2 the caster level of this spell.
spell-burial-hymn:
You play or sing a song of death and remembrance causing all undead to feel the call of their grave. All undead who fail their saving throw are staggered, mindless undead do not gain a saving throw.

Undead that are already staggered are unable to move but may still use their standard action.
spell-buried-in-light: This spell functions as the spell daylight except any creature that enters the area of light created by this spell must make a Fortitude save or treat the area as difficult terrain or worse. Areas of normal light within the 120-foot-total radius is considered difficult terrain for those that fail their Fortitude save. Areas of bright light are considered difficult terrain but cost 15 feet per 5 feet moved instead of 10 feet for those that failed their Fortitude save. Those that succeed on their saving throw ignore the difficult terrain in normal light and treat bright light as normal difficult terrain. When casting this spell, you can designate a number of creatures, including yourself, equal 1/2 your caster level, to not be subject to this spell. Spell resistance protects against the difficult terrain portion of this spell but not the light created by the spell.
spell-burning-grasp: Your successful melee touch attack deals 1d6 points of fire damage per caster level (maximum 5d6). When delivering the fire, you gain a +3 bonus on attack rolls if the opponent is wearing wood-armor (or is carrying a easily accessible flammable materials like spellbooks).
spell-burning-pit:
This spell functions as create pit, except that it places a 5-foot deep conflagration of fire at the bottom of the pit. The pit has a maximum depth of 100 feet. Creatures who fall into the pit take falling damage as normal, plus 2d4 points of fire damage per round spent in contact with the fire. In addition, exposed items carried by a creature in the pit may be set on fire.

The walls of the pit are burned to a slick sheen and have a Climb DC of 30.
spell-burning-skull: You turn the target's skull into a conflagration from the inside out. The target takes 6d6 fire damage and is blinded. They then catch on fire taking 3d6 fire each round. The target remains blinded for as long as they are on fire. A successful initial Fortitude save halves the fire damage and negates the blinding and catching on fire. Then each round they can attempt to put out the fire with a Reflex save against this spell's DC. The ongoing fire damage does not stack with other fire damage dealt from being on fire.
spell-burnt-lungs:
You cause a combustion in the target's lungs. The target must breathe air and aquatic creatures are immune to this effect. Otherwise, an affected creature takes 6d6 fire damage and is exhausted for the remainder of the duration. They also must make a caster-level check to cast spells with verbal components.

A successful Fortitude save halves this damage and reduces the effect to fatigued for 1d6 rounds.
spell-burst-of-shadows: You create a tear into the shadow plane for a brief moment. A mass of undead shadows reach out and affect those within the burst. Each creature takes 1d6 Strength damage and is dazed for 1 round. A successful Fortitude save reduces the Strength damage to 1 and negates the dazing. A creature occupying multiple squares of the burst are affected by this spell a second time, though they get a save against the second set. The dazed effect does not stack.
spell-burst-of-strength:
You speak a word that empowers you to smash most obstacles.

When you cast this spell you gain a +10 bonus to Strength checks made to break objects. At caster level 10 or higher this spell grants a +20 bonus instead.
spell-calculative-mind:
Casting this spell channels a tiny portion of a lawful-aligned plane's essence to temporarily settle into the target's mind, smoothing out emotions while providing minor assistance in logical assessments, recall, and calculations.

A creature under the effects of this spell gains a +4 resistance bonus on saving throws against charm, compulsion, and emotion effects (including hope and despair effects). If they are already affected (or later affected while this spell is in effect) by an on-going charm, compulsion, or emotion effect, they gain an immediate saving throw (with the resistance bonus from this spell) against that effect at the same DC to resist or negate it. The target can only make this additional saving throw to resist or negate against a charm, compulsion, or emotion effect once while they are under the effects of calculative mind.

The target also automatically gains a competence bonus on all Intelligence-based checks equal 1 + 1/4 your caster level. However, once the target makes a number of Intelligence-based checks equal to your caster level, this spell is discharged.

This spell has two drawbacks. First, while this spell lasts, the target must always attempt a saving throw to resist or negate any charm, compulsion, or emotion effect (assuming one is allowed) on them, even if the effects are harmless. Secondly, if the target is successfully affected by any spell with the chaotic descriptor of equal level or greater than the on-going calculative mind cast on them, that casting of calculative mind immediately ends as if it was discharged.
spell-call-minor-monster: This spell functions as summon monster V except the creatures do not disappear at the end of the spell's duration. Instead, the creature(s) become free-willed and outside the caller's control. If the creature is destroyed, it does return to its plane as normal.
spell-called-by-the-tomb: This spell functions as hold person except you manipulate negative energies powering undead creatures to target them. Mindless undead do not get a saving throw to negate this spell or end it early.
spell-called-by-the-tomb-mass: This spell functions as mass hold person except you manipulate negative energies powering undead creatures to target them. Mindless undead do not get a saving throw to negate this spell or end it early.
spell-caustic-fumes:
This spell functions as fog cloud except the mist is caustic and deals 1d6 acid damage to any creature entering or beginning their turn in its area.

Additionally, the fumes burn the eyes and impose a -5 penalty to vision-based Perception checks while in the area and for 2 rounds thereafter.
spell-caustic-sludge: Foul caustic sludge seeps up from the ground in the designated area. This sludge is deep and sticky causing the area to be difficult terrain unless the target can fly or hover over the ground. Additionally, a creature takes 1d6 acid damage for every 5 feet moved through the area. If the target ends their turn without moving while in the area, they take 1d6 acid damage.
spell-caustic-wounds: You create an aura of acid that aggravates wounds in the area. All bleed damage in the aura is converted to acid damage and increased by 1d4. Additionally, any creature that takes piercing or slashing damage takes an additional 1d8 acid damage.
spell-chains-of-ice:
This spell creates an jumping cold blast that begins as a single beam commencing from your fingertips. Like chain lightning, chains of ice strikes one object or creature initially, then arcs to other targets.

The ray deals 1d6 points of cold damage per caster level (maximum 20d6) to the primary target. After it strikes, freezing ray can arc to a number of secondary targets equal to your caster level (maximum 20). The secondary rays each strike one target and deal as much damage as the primary bolt.

Each target can attempt a Fortitude saving throw for half damage. The Reflex DC to halve the damage of the secondary rays is 2 lower than the DC to halve the damage of the primary ray. You choose secondary targets as you like, but they must all be within 30 feet of the primary target, and no target can be struck more than once. You can choose to affect fewer secondary targets than the maximum.
spell-chains-of-shadow:
You create a burst of shadow chains in a target point.

Creatures in the area that fail a Will save are dazed for 1 round and are entangled for the rest of the duration.

They can attempt to break free of the shadowy chains by making a Strength or Escape Artist check against a DC of 10 + your caster level, as a full-round action. If the target makes their Will save, or they escape the chains, they treat the area as difficult terrain.
spell-chance: This spell was developed to help nudge games of chance though it has other minor uses, as such it has no obvious tell and requires a Spellcraft check with a DC of 15 to identify that a spell has been cast. When you cast this spell you may roll twice on any check related to a game of chance in the same round. Alternatively if a percentile would be rolled to determine how an effect would affect you you may cast this spell as an immediate action to increase or decrease that percentile by 5% before the results of the roll are known.
spell-chaos-breed: This spell functions like lesser chaos breed, except your blindsense is 10 feet, resistance to acid and electricity 10, and DR 10/law, and you gain the ability to float allowing you to fly at a speed of 30 feet with average maneuverability. In addition, your natural weapons and any weapons you wield are considered chaotically-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.
spell-chaos-breed-greater:
This spell functions like lesser chaos breed, except your blindsense is 20 feet; DR 10/chaotic; immunity to acid, resistance to electricity and sonic 10; you gain the benefits of freedom of movement, and amorphous anatomy. Also, your flight gives you a fly speed of 60 feet with good maneuverability.

The amorphous anatomy gives you a 50% chance to ignore criticals and precision damage, and immunity to polymorph effects, unless you are willing.
spell-chaos-breed-lesser: You take on an aspect of a being of pure chaos, including some of its physical characteristics. You gain blindsense out to 5 feet, resistance to acid 5, resistance to electricity 5, and the benefits of protection from law.
spell-charged-armor: This spell functions as lesser charged armor except as above, the DR is increased to 10, the amount per level is increased to 10 points per level (maximum 200), and it explodes out to 10 feet to a maximum of 15d4 force damage.
spell-charged-armor-lesser: You create a field of force around the target that protects them from damage. The subject gains DR 5/-. It ignores the first 5 points of damage each time it takes damage from a weapon. Once the spell has prevented a total of 5 points of damage per caster level (maximum 50), it is discharged and explodes with force. All creatures within 5 feet of the target must make a Reflex save or take 1d4 force damage per caster level (maximum 10d4).
spell-charged-cloud:
A charged cloud spell creates a cloud of floating copper dust charged with electricity. The cloud obscures all sight as a fog cloud does. In addition, the electrical charge within the cloud deals 6d6 points of electricity damage to everything within the cloud on your turn each round. All targets can make Reflex saves each round to take half damage.

As with a cloudkill spell, the cloud moves away from you at 10 feet per round. Figure out the cloud's new spread each round based on its new point of origin, which is 10 feet farther away from where you were when you cast the spell. By concentrating, you can make the cloud move as much as 60 feet each round.

Any portion of the cloud that would extend beyond your maximum range dissipates harmlessly, reducing the remainder's spread thereafter.

As with fog cloud, wind disperses the cloud, and the spell can't be cast underwater.
spell-charnel-winds:
A blast of wind bearing the vile smell of death blasts downward, inflicting 4d6 negative energy damage +1 point per caster level to all creatures in the area and knocking them prone. A successful Fortitude save halves the negative energy damage and negates being knocked prone. Flying creatures forced into the ground by the powerful downdraft take damage as if they fell unless they make a DC 15 Fly check, in which case they remain at their original altitude.

Any creature that takes damage from a charnel wind becomes nauseated for 1 round, then sickened for 1 minute thereafter. Undead creatures in the area are healed by the amount of negative energy damage.
spell-chasm-of-immurement:
You cause a rent in the ground to open up below the target, draw them in and close around them, sealing them into a tomb of earth and stone. You trap the target in stone 1 inch thick per caster level. If the creature fails its save, it is helpless and must begin holding their breath at the end of their next turn. They will suffocate if they are not freed from the stone. If the target makes its save, it gains the entangled condition and is unable to move until they are broken free of them but can otherwise act normally and breathe. The stone has hardness 8 and 15 hit points per inch of thickness; if broken, the creature is freed. A creature can break the stone as a full-round action with a successful Strength check (DC 20 + your caster level).

Once the spell ends, the chasm reopens freeing the creature within.
spell-checkmate: With a word and a gesture, you gain an advantageous position. The caster immediately teleports up to 25 ft + 5 ft per caster level to an open square. The targeted square must be in a position that is either adjacent to an ally or allows the caster to gain a flanking bonus.
spell-chewing-glass:
You summon sharp shards of glass into the mouth of the target creature. This is immensely painful, and if the target bleeds, bloody. At the beginning of their turn, the target must make a Fortitude save. On a failure, the target takes 2d4 magical slashing damage, 1 bleed damage, and is unable to speak or use spells or abilities that require vocal components or linguistic communication. However the target can spend a standard action to spit glass out of their mouth and be able to vocalize until the beginning of their next turn.

On a successful Fortitude save, the target takes 1d4 magical slashing damage and is also unable to speak but can clear their mouth as a move action instead of a standard. In either case, the spell ends at the end of their turn if they succeeded.

Creatures without mouths are not affected. If the creature has multiple mouths, It only prevents one mouth from vocalizing.
spell-chilling-aura: You freeze the air around you, frost dancing across their features. When you cast this spell frost seems to hang in the air around you. You gain fire resistance 20 and all creatures within 10 feet of you take 4d6 cold damage and become fatigued at the beginning of their turn. A successful Fortitude save halves the damage and negates the fatigued condition.
spell-chilling-aura-3pp-orphaned-bookwor: You create an aura of frost. All creatures within the aura take a -5 penalty on saving throws against spells or effects with the cold descriptor or that deal cold damage. Additionally, all cold damage in the area is increased by 3 per cold damage dice dealt.
spell-chimerical-reality: You create a phantasm of a split in the target's reality where they see a multitude of possible realities. Each round at the beginning of their turn, the creature must make a Will save or be dazed by the overload of information. On a successful saving throw, the target is dazzled. If the target makes 3 consecutive saving throws, the spell ends.
spell-choir-invisible:
You complete the spell and an invisible ghostly chorus picks up on your performance. If you are doing an auditory bardic performance (or similar ability like skald raging song) the chorus will continue to maintain the song to the duration of the spell while you can stop maintaining it with your bardic performance rounds.

At the end of the spell the maintained performance ends and you can start a new performance. You cannot have two concurrent bardic performances with this spell.
spell-claws-of-the-bear: Bestial claws emerge from your flesh at will. This spell grants the caster the ability to manifest and dismiss claws as a free action. These claws deal 1d6 slashing damage and function as primary natural weapons. For every three caster levels the claws gain a +1 enhancement bonus on attack and damage rolls to a maximum of +5 at 15th level. If the caster makes a full attack and damages a target with both claws they may make a grapple check as a free action. If this grapple check is successful the target takes damage from one claw in addition to gaining the grappled condition.
spell-cleansing-hands: This spell functions as lesser cleansing hands except it heals 3d8 + your caster level (maximum +15) and in addition to the previous list of conditions, you can remove the blinded, dazed, deafened, diseased, exhausted, nauseated, and poisoned conditions. Instead of removing one of the conditions, you may remove all ability damage to one ability score.
spell-cleansing-hands-greater: This spell functions as cleansing hands except it heals 4d8 + your caster level (maximum +20) and in addition to the previous lists of conditions, you can remove the feebleminded and insanity conditions. Instead of removing one of the conditions, remove all ability damage to all ability scores.
spell-cleansing-hands-lesser: You touch the creature soothing their wounds and removing some debilitations. You heal the target creature 2d8 + your caster level (maximum +10) and remove the one of the following conditions: confused, dazzled, fatigued, sickened, and stunned. Instead of healing one of the listed conditions, you can reduce the exhausted condition to fatigued, the nauseated condition to sickened, or heal 1d4 temporary ability damage.
spell-clever-distraction: You cast this spell by uttering a quick phrase and throwing a polished coin past the view of your opponent, taking them off guard for just a moment. A creature that fails a Will save is flat-footed until the beginning of its next turn.
spell-cloying-shadows: With a gesture you cause nearby shadows to wrap and twist around your target's eyes. Any creature that fails its Will save can see only 5 feet and its vision is clouded as the darkness spell, granting creatures within 5 ft. of the target partial concealment.
spell-collapse: You cause the target to hit the ground and take damage as if it had fallen from a height. The target is knocked prone and takes 1d6 falling damage per caster level (maximum 15d6). A successful Fortitude save halves the damage and negates the prone condition.
spell-collapse-mass: This spell functions as collapse except it affects multiple creatures within range and the maximum falling damage dealt is 25d6.
spell-combat-competency:
You grant the creature greater insight into combat.

They gain a +1 competence bonus to their base attack bonus. If this would grant the target more iterative attacks, they gain the extra iterative attack. This cannot grant more iterative attacks after +20. This stacks with competence bonus to your attack rolls.
spell-combat-mastery: The touched target gains a combat feat of their choice for which they meet the prerequisites. This spell does not stack with other castings of the spell, but subsequent castings can extend the duration and change the feat.
spell-comet-swarm:
When you cast this spell, four 2-foot-diameter spheres spring from your outstretched hand and streak in straight lines to the spots you select. The comets leave a trail of freezing mist behind them.

If you aim a comet at a specific creature, you may make a ranged touch attack to strike the target with the meteor. Any creature struck by a sphere takes 2d6 points of bludgeoning damage (no save) and must make a Reflex save or be stunned for 1 round. This stunning effect does not stack from multiple hits. If a targeted sphere misses its target, it simply explodes at the nearest corner of the target's space. You may aim more than one sphere at the same target.

Once a comet reaches its destination, it explodes in a 40-foot-radius spread, dealing 6d6 points of cold damage to each creature in the area. A separate Reflex save halves this damage. If a creature is within the area of more than one sphere, it must save separately against each. Despite stemming from separate spheres, all of the cold damage is added together after the saves have been made, and cold resistance is applied only once.
spell-comet-swarm-3pp-rogue-genius-games: As scorching ray, but bolts deal 4d4 damage, and you get 1 bolt per 3 caster levels. As a swift action in the next round, when you cast the spell and miss, you can redirect the bolt at a new target within range.
spell-condemned-to-rot:
You infect the target with a cursed disease of wasting.

The target is not able to be healed by magical means and loses any natural healing, including fast healing or regeneration. Heal skill checks do not help.

Additionally, if they have any damage, they additionally must make a Fortitude save each time they rest overnight or take damage equal to their hit dice.
spell-cone-of-boiling-acid: This spell functions as cone of boiling acid except the cone is larger and the maximum damage is increased to 15d6.
spell-cone-of-boiling-acid-greater: This spell functions as cone of boiling acid except the cone is larger and the maximum damage is increased to 20d6 and creatures that fail their saving throw take 1d6 fire and 1d6 acid damage each round for 2d4 rounds, or 1 round on a successful one.
spell-cone-of-boiling-acid-lesser: You burst forth with a spray of boiling acid. Each creature within the cone takes 1d6 damage per caster level (maximum 10d6). Half of the damage is acid, the other half is fire.
spell-cone-of-cold-greater: This spell functions as cone of cold except the damage maximum is 20d6 cold damage and targets are affected by the slow spell for 2d4 rounds on a failed save or 1 round on a successful one.
spell-cone-of-cold-lesser: This spell functions as cone of cold except the cone is smaller and the damage is capped at 10d6 cold damage.
spell-conjure-abyssal-parasite:
With a touch you summon forth a creature from the depths of the abyssal waterways and let it loose in your target. Even on a successful save, the energies unleashed leave the target nauseated for one round.

On a failed save you deposit the summoned abyssal parasite into your target, dealing 2 damage to their Dexterity and Charisma scores as it twists and deforms a part of their body into its new permanent home. While infested, the target takes a -2 penalty on all saving throws against spells with the evil or curse descriptors as the parasite acts as a magnet for such magics. Whenever the target would be subject to a healing spell or casts a healing spell they take 1 damage to each of their Dexterity and Charisma scores. If the parasite is removed or destroyed the target's body reverts to normal, leaving no evidence of the parasite aside from any remaining ability damage.

The parasite, a pitifully weak creature, can be removed in several ways:

Lesser restoration and its more powerful versions can repair some or all of the damage caused by the parasite, but they do not remove the parasite from the host.

Spells that banish extradimensional creatures will end this spell if cast upon the host.
spell-conquering-countermand: This spell functions like dispel magic except you may add your caster level up to a maximum of +20 to the dispel check and you may only use this spell to make a targeted dispel or a counterspell. When you use this spell to make a counterspell attempt you may also make a caster level check with a DC of 25 + twice the level of the spell you are countering, if you succeed you may gain control of that spell. This means you cast the countered spell as an immediate action, treating it as though it had been cast from one of your own spell slots. Using your caster level and calculating save DC as normal for your spellcasting feature.
spell-consecrate-battlefield:
You fill the battlefield with positive energy. This spell functions as consecrate, except as above and as follows:

Any creature slain within the area cannot be turned into undead for the duration of the spell, even if removed.

This spell counters and dispels desecrate and desecrate battlefield.
spell-control-shadows:
You can shift and alter existing darkness and shadow, whether natural or magical. You can cause one of the following effects:

You can only have one effect operating at a time but you can switch between them as a free action once per round. The chosen effect covers the entire affected area.

When the spell expires all shadows and darkness reverts to their original light levels and locations.
spell-corpsethrone:
You summon a mass of corpses that piles up underneath you. You are 20 feet higher at the center, the pile of bodies then drops 5 feet down and the pile of bodies slopes down to the edges. The area is considered difficult terrain to all creatures, aside from yourself, due to the shifting bodies and the angle of the hill. Additionally, the corpses reach out and attempt to grasp all creatures aside from you. All those moving through the area must make a Reflex save or be entangled as per the spell entangle.

Your movement is not impeded, in fact your speed is doubled while in the area as the bodies propel you faster. You can get up to the apex of the pile as if it were flat. The corpses summoned in this manner cannot be used to animate dead creatures, though the area of the spell grants the benefits of the desecrate spell with the center of the corpsethrone being treated as an altar.
spell-cosmic-voice: You speak with a voice that transcends reality and shakes the mortal fabric of your enemies within the area. Each enemy within the burst of sound must make a Will save. On a failure, they suffer a condition as noted on the table below. On a success, they are treated as one HD category higher than they are on the table. If they were already greater than your CL and make the Will save, they are unaffected.
spell-crawling-sensation: You cause your target to believe that they can feel multitudess of tiny insects crawling and biting all over. The target may attempt a Will save each round to ignore the sensation for that round. A success means they may act normally. A failure means they take a -2 penalty AC and can only move at half speed for that round. In addition the creature must also make a concentration check to cast spells with DC 11 + the caster level of the crawling sensation spell or lose the spell.
spell-create-drone:
You instill power into the brass ball, turning it into a miniature attack construct. The drone attacks foes at a distance, as you direct it, dealing 1d8 force damage per hit, + 1 point per three caster levels (maximum +5 at 15th level). It strikes the opponent you designate, starting with one attack in the round the spell is cast and continuing each round thereafter on your turn. It uses your base attack bonus (possibly allowing it multiple attacks per round in subsequent rounds) plus your spellcasting ability modifier as its attack bonus. It strikes as a spell, not as a weapon, so for example, it can damage creatures that have damage reduction. As a force effect, it can strike incorporeal creatures without the reduction in damage associated with incorporeality. The drone always strikes from your direction. It does not get a flanking bonus or help a combatant get one. Your feats or combat actions do not affect the weapon. If the drone goes beyond the spell range, if it goes out of your sight, or if you are not directing it, it returns to you and hovers.

Each round after the first, you can use a move action to redirect the weapon to a new target, it can move up to 60 feet per round with a perfect fly maneuverability. If you do not, the drone continues to attack the previous round's target. On any round that the drone switches targets, it gets one attack. Subsequent rounds of attacking that target allow the drone to make multiple attacks if your base attack bonus would allow it to.

The drone can be attacked and harmed by physical attacks. It has an AC of 24, cannot be caught flat-footed, has construct traits, a hardness of 9, and hit points equal to 5 times your caster level. If destroyed, the spell ends.

If an attacked creature has Spell Resistance, you make a caster level check (1d20 + caster level) against that Spell Resistance the first time the drone strikes it. If the drone is successfully resisted, it is unable to attack it for the remainder of the duration.
spell-create-drone-assailant: This spell functions as create drone, except it grows to a Small-sized construct that appears in a space within range. Its damage is increased to 1d10 + 1 point per three caster levels (maximum +5 at 15th level), it can attack as a normal creature and can provide flanking based upon its positioning. Its AC is reduced to 18, but its HP is increased to 8 times your caster level + 10 and its hardness is 10.
spell-create-drone-defenders: This spell functions as create drone, except it creates a mass of fine brass drones that occupies a 10-foot radius area centered on the point you designate. They gain swarm traits, but otherwise retain the stats of the original spell. The swarm cannot move from the designated area. Any creature passing through its area must make a Reflex save or take 4d6 force damage. A successful save halves the damage. Once the drone defenders deal damage to a number of creatures equal to your caster level, the spell ends.
spell-create-trap-lesser: This spell functions as lesser create trap except you create one CR 4 trap with up to a 10-foot-by-10-foot triggering area, or two CR 2 traps with up to a 10-foot-by-5-foot triggering area.
spell-crimson-eclipse:
You flood the area with a crimson shade like blood.

Within the area, all light spells are treated as 1 CL lower for their effects and duration and all blood and necromancy spells are considered 1 CL higher for their effects and duration.
spell-crimson-path:
You cut your palm dealing 1 damage and touch a living creature, violently and bloodily entering their body, and exiting in a similar fashion from a nearby creature.

You teleport 10 feet when touching Small or smaller creatures and the distance teleported doubles for each size category larger than small. Medium would be 20 feet, Large 40, and so on. The touched creature and the endpoint creature must make Fortitude saves or be dealt 1d6 damage per caster level (maximum 15d6). A successful saving throw halves this damage but does not prevent the teleportation. This spell cannot use bloodless creatures as a target or end point. If there is no valid endpoint creature available, this spell fails. You cannot enter and exit the same creature.
spell-cryo-blast: You cause the temperature around the target to drop quickly freezing them solid. The target takes 1d6 points of cold damage + 1 point per caster level (maximum +10). The target must then make a Fortitude save or be paralyzed by the cold for 1 round per caster level. The target gains another Fortitude save to end the effect at the beginning of each of their rounds. If in an area of hot or summer weather, or if the creature has the fire subtype, they gain a +5 bonus on the saving throw. Additionally, they gain a +1 bonus on their saving throw for each round they have been paralyzed. While paralyzed the target cannot be subject to a coup de grace and they gain a hardness of 8.
spell-cryo-blast-greater: This functions as cryo blast, except that it affects all creatures within the area.
spell-crystal-casket:
You encase the target in a crystalline structure that is 1 inch thick per caster level. If the target fails their Reflex save, it is helpless, but held in stasis and will not age, need to eat, or breathe. A creature that succeeds on their saving throw is entangled but not held in stasis for the duration or until the crystal is broken. The crystal blocks line of effect, but not line of sight, though the creature cannot be affected by any mind-affecting effects while in the crystal. The crystal has a hardness of 2 and 5 hit points per inch of thickness. If the crystal is broken, the creature is freed. A creature can break the crystal as a full-round action with a successful Strength check (DC 15 + your caster level).

This spell can be made permanent with the permanency spell with a minimum caster level of 13th and 18,000 gp.
spell-crystal-casket-mass: This spell functions as crystal casket, except as noted above.
spell-curse-of-phantom-putrescence: This cursed illusion causes the subject to believe their flesh is rotting and falling off their body, and that their internal organs are spilling out. If the target fails their saving throw, they are dazed with horror for 1 round. On the following round, if they fail a second saving throw, they fall unconscious for 1d10 minutes, during which time they cannot be roused normally. This illusion cannot be removed by dispel magic. It requires a remove curse or break enchantment. A true seeing spell can see the curse as merely an illusion.
spell-cursed-blade:
You coat a weapon in powerful necromantic energy causing it to leave truly grievous wounds.

The weapon gains the wounding magic weapon property and any damage dealt by the weapon cannot be healed by magical or natural means until the damaged creature has been subject to a remove curse spell or similar effect which would remove a curse. If a creature is slain by a weapon benefiting from this spell the body must likewise be purged of this effect before the creature can be raised or resurrected.
spell-damping: You cause the energies that suffuse the target to temporarily flee them. They lose all access to spells, spell-like abilities, and use-based supernatural abilities for 1 round.
spell-damping-mass: This spell functions as damping except it affects multiple creatures.
spell-damping-greater: This spell functions as damping except for a longer duration. The target gets a new saving throw each round to end the effect.
spell-damping-greater-mass: This spell functions as greater damping except it affects multiple creatures.
spell-dance-of-daggers:
As you cast this spell the daggers in your hands glow with faint blue light, shedding light equivalent to a torch, though you can choose to suppress this light as a free action. While under the effects of this spell, you gain a +2 competence bonus on attack and damage rolls as long as you hold a dagger or dagger-like weapon in each hand.

Additionally, if you fight defensively while wielding two such weapons you gain a +2 shield bonus to armor class.
spell-darkbolts:
You unleash bolts of pure darkness from your outstretched hand. You must succeed on a ranged touch to affect a target. Each bolt may be at a different target and the targets must be living creatures.

Each creature hit takes 2d8 negative energy damage and must make a Will save or be dazed for 1 round. The dazing does not stack from multiple hits.

The bolts may be fired all at once or one per round as a free action. If a bolt is not launched in a particular round, it is lost. If the bolts are launched all at once, the targets must all be within 30 feet of each other.
spell-dazzling-brilliance: You unleash a brilliant flash of light in the area that dazzles those within for 1 minute. A successful Fortitude save negates the dazzling, but if they fail the save by 5 or more they are blinded for 1 round then dazzled for 1 minute. Sightless creatures are not affected by this spell. This spell also counters and dispels a darkness spell of equal level or lower.
spell-deadly-proficiency:
With a touch, the knowledge of soldiers and generals flows through your target.

When you cast this spell you draw the focus with a flourish and lay a hand on your target. The target of the spell gains proficiency with the type of weapon or shield used as the focus for this spell. If the target is already proficient, they deal damage with the weapon as though it were one size larger.
spell-deadly-proficiency-communal: This spell functions as deadly proficiency, except you divide the duration among the creatures touched.
spell-deadly-quiet:
With a touch, the knowledge of scouts and assassins flows into your target.

When you cast this spell you impart the target with increased subtlety, allowing them to use your ranks in Stealth in place of their own. The target also ignores an amount of armor check penalty to Stealth checks equal to your caster level.
spell-deadly-quiet-communal: This spell functions as deadly quiet, except you divide the duration among the creatures touched.
spell-deafening-thunder: You create an explosion of deafening sound in the area. Each creature in the area takes 1d8 sonic damage per two caster levels (maximum 10d8) and are permanently deafened. A successful Fortitude save halves the damage and reduces the deafness to 1 round.
spell-death-mask:
You complete the spell and don the terrifying death mask. Your eyes glow with a pale deathly light and a look from you can kill. Any living enemy that meets your gaze, must make a Fortitude save or die. A creature can avert their eyes as with any other gaze attack but you can focus your gaze on a target as a standard action to force a saving throw on them. You can kill a number of HD worth of creatures equal to 1d4 HD per caster level, but cannot kill creatures of 18th or higher HD.

A creature that succeeds on its saving throw or has too many HD does not count against the HD the spell can kill.

If at the end of the spell you have remaining hit dice worth of killing remaining, you can unleash the remaining necromantic energy as a ray of negative energy. You make a ranged touch attack against one target and on a hit deal negative energy damage equal to 10 times the remaining hit dice of killing remaining.
spell-decoy: You create a visual illusion of yourself as per the spell silent image. This decoy does not move from its space, but it can move in natural ways otherwise. Creatures might be prone to attacking the decoy rather than you if you are hidden.
spell-defiant-cure: This spell functions as a combination of remove disease and neutralize poison. Except that if the disease or poison are not removed, you can continue to attempt to remove it each round. Once the poison or disease is removed, this spell ends.
spell-deflection-mass: This spell functions as deflection except it has a longer range and it affects multiple allies.
spell-delayed-blast-thunderball: This spell functions like thunderball, except that it is more powerful and can detonate up to 5 rounds after the spell is cast. The burst of sound deals 1d4 points of sonic damage per caster level (maximum 20d4). The resounding bead created by delayed blast thunderball can detonate immediately if you desire, or you can choose to delay the burst for as many as 5 rounds. You select the amount of delay upon completing the spell, and that time cannot change once it has been set unless someone touches the bead. If you choose a delay, the resounding bead sits at its destination until it detonates. A creature can pick up and hurl the bead as a thrown weapon (range increment 10 feet). If a creature handles and moves the bead within 1 round of its detonation, there is a 25% chance that the bead detonates while being handled.
spell-delusion-of-consciousness: You create flashing lights in the eyes of the target creature rendering them unconscious for 1d6 unless they make a Will save. While the target is unconscious, an image of the target is created which shows them as conscious and active as per the minor image spell. If you cease concentrating on the spell, the image disappears and the unconscious target is revealed.
spell-desecrate-battlefield:
You fill the battlefield with negative energy. This spell functions as desecrate, except as above.

This spell counters and dispels consecrate and consecrate battlefield.
spell-desperate-volley:
You can stoke the fury of your allies and concentrate their efforts on a single foe.

When you cast this spell you must choose targets from among creatures with ranged weapons in hand. Each targeted creature may make a ranged attack against a single enemy you designate within the first two range increments of their weapon. The attacks granted by this spell are treated as attacks of opportunity and count against each targeted creatures' number of available attacks of opportunity for the round.
spell-detritus-form:
Your form collapses to mirror your natural surroundings. The caster transforms into a pile of fallen leaves, branches, or other natural refuse and gains a bonus on Stealth checks in natural terrain equal to half their caster level. All objects worn and carried by the caster up to a medium load meld into this new form.

DESCRIPTION

The caster maintains their base land speed and any other movement they possess that does not rely on their physiology. This transformation prevents the caster from speaking or casting spells that require somatic components though they may provide any material component that was on their person at the time of transformation. While transformed they take half damage from all sources other than fire and may squeeze through spaces as though they were tiny sized.
spell-dimensional-leap: This spell functions as dimension door except it has a much shorter range.
spell-direction-and-distance:
The touched target knows the direction and distance they must travel to reach you. This does not reveal the best or quickest route to do so, only the most direct.

This does not work if you and the target are on separate planes or either creature enters an antimagic area, the effect is suppressed.
spell-discern-spirit-presence:
This spell allows you to discern the presence of spirits (fey, outsiders, and incorporeal undead) within the area of effect. You do not learn the location, type, power, or aura of any detected spirits, merely the fact that they do exist in the affected area. You can detect a spirit's presence even if they are polymorphed, possessing a creature or object, or manifesting in some way (such as a curse), but if they have an ability or feat that would allow them a chance to avoid detection, they can still do so.

Each round, you may turn to discern the presence of spirits in a new area. Because this spell is focused on spirits and not the material world, it is only blocked by barriers made of materials that are harmful to spirits or summoned by magic.
spell-distract-assailant:
You make a motion and the target becomes convinced there is an enemy near them they did not anticipate.

They are treated as if they flanked for 1 round. If the target has improved uncanny dodge, all attackers are treated as having your caster level as their rogue level for the purposes of being able to use their existing sneak attack against the target.
spell-divine-impediment: This spell functions as divine impediment, except as noted above.
spell-doomhound:
You tear a piece free from the plane of shadow and shape it into a doglike creature loyal to you for the duration of the spell. The doomhound has the statistics of a dire wolf with the following adjustments: It gains a deflection bonus to AC and CMD equal to your spellcasting ability modifier, it is created with hit points equal to your full hit point total and it uses your base attack bonus instead of its own.

You may direct the doomhound as a move action, and it follows your commands as though it were fully trained in all tricks listed under the Handle Animal skill without needing to make a skill check.

The doomhound is considered a magical beast for the purposes of spells and effects, you may only have one doomhound at a time, and it is destroyed when its hit points reach zero.
spell-dreaded-mystic-abyss:
You send a creature into a chaotic, liminal, demi-plane of arcane energy. At the beginning of their turn, the target must make a Will save or remain in the plane until their next turn and take 4d8 points of damage from a random energy type the caster picks one of the d8s rolled to determine the damage type using the table below. On a successful saving throw, the target is shunted back to the plane they left at the beginning of their turn taking 10d6 force damage.

Creatures can take actions and attempt to cast spells on their turn to attempt to escape but any actions taken that require concentration treat damage taken at the end of their turn to be constant throughout for the purpose of determining the concentration DC.

Like any plane, a spellcaster or creature with the ability can plane shift out, but they still take the 10d6 force damage for doing so. Dimensional anchor or other spells, abilities, or conditions do not prevent the target creature from returning from this spell, but can prevent them from being affected in the first place.
spell-drugged-stupor: You place the helpless creature in a clouded, confused state. The target cannot think clearly, take actions and is unaware of their surroundings. The target can be moved or forced to walk along, if guided by another creature.
spell-dueling-companions: You cast the spell and illusory copies of yourself protect you from the directions you are not facing. For the duration, you have a +2 dodge bonus to AC vs. attacks of opportunity and cannot be flanked by creatures with hit dice less than 4 + the caster level of this spell.
spell-earth-scar:
You let out a pulse of energy that resonates and breaks up or solidifies earthen terrain. This spell removes any natural earthen difficult terrain except for such terrain caused by slopes or inclines. This spell dispels or removes difficult terrain created by spells such as spike stones, stone call or earth tremor. Natural terrain is solidified and smoothed out. This spell has no effect on plants, vegetation, creatures using spells or abilities to traverse rock or stone like earth glide, burrowing creatures, larger structures like walls or pillars, holes except to prevent them from causing difficult terrain, or manufactured difficult terrain like caltrops or spikes.

Additionally, any earth subtype creature within the radius of the spell takes 2d8 points of sonic damage. A successful Fortitude save halves this damage.
spell-echopraxia:
You take control of the target's mind, forcing them to mimic the movements you make. On a failed Will save the target must be forced to make the same action in the same directions as you do on your turn. For example, if you attack an empty space or creature to your West, on their turn the target must attack whatever is to the West of them. Or if you move, the target must move in the same pattern but from their starting point. If these actions would put them in danger, like movement sending them off a cliff, causing them to provoke an attack of opportunity, or causing them to harm one of their allies, they gain a Will save to stop short of making that action with a +5 bonus to the roll. This does not end the effect, but it prevents the action while still expending it. If the creature is unable to make the action, like you casting a spell, they still mimic the movement and expend the action without creating any effect.

Any action that you do not take is available for the target to use on their turn. Like an unused swift action would allow a bard target to maintain their bardic performance. However, any freed action would take place after the mimicked actions.
spell-ectoplasmic-coating: When you cast this spell you tug a few drops of ectoplasm from the ethereal plane and smear it across a suit of armor. For the duration of this spell the armor gains the ghost touch property, the armor's bonus also increases by +4 against critical confirmation rolls against incorporeal creatures.
spell-elation-lesser:
This spell functions as lesser elation, except the morale bonus increases to +4, and their main mode of movement increases by 15 feet.

If you are using the optional hope and despair rules, all three iterations of elation are considered hope spells.
spell-electric-arc:
This spell causes an arc of lightning to leap from your fingers, shocking a number of enemies nearby. It deals 1d6 points of electricity damage per caster level (maximum 10d6). For every additional target the discharge arcs to, reduce the number of damage dice by half (rounded down). Therefore, at 9th level, your electric arc deals 9d6 points of electricity damage to the primary target, then 4d6 points of electricity damage to a secondary target, then 2d6 points of electricity damage to a third target, and 1d6 to a fourth.

Each target can attempt a Reflex saving throw for half damage. The Reflex DC to halve the damage of the secondary bolts is 2 lower than the DC to halve the damage of the primary bolt.
