You may choose secondary targets as you like, but they must all be within 15 feet of the primary target, and no target can be struck more than once. You can choose to affect fewer secondary targets than the maximum.
spell-electric-eruption: Electricity erupts from your space in all directions, causing 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 20d6) to creatures. On your turn in each of the next 2 rounds, creatures and objects that failed their saves against the initial burst take an additional 1d6 points of electricity damage per 2 caster levels (maximum 10d6). Creatures wearing metal armor or bearing metal weapons take a -4 penalty on this save.
spell-electric-gag: You jolt the target with electricity in their vocal cords rendering them temporarily incapable of speech. The target takes 1d6 electricity damage per caster level (maximum 10d6), and is unable to speak, make vocal sounds, use language-dependent abilities, or use spells with vocal components for 1 round per level. A successful Reflex save halves the electricity damage and negates the silencing effect.
spell-electric-slash: You unleash a wave of electricity in the arc you designate. Any creature in the area takes 1d4 points of electricity per caster level (maximum 10d4). A successful Reflex save halves this damage. Additionally, creatures who take damage must make a Fortitude save or be stunned for 1d4 rounds.
spell-embodiment-of-grief: You exude an aura of despair, causing those around you to feel immense grief. Each creature that enters or begins their turn in the aura must make a Will save or take a -1 penalty on attack rolls, saving throws, ability checks, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls for 1 minute. If the subject creature fails their Will saving throw while taking penalties from this ability, the condition worsens. On a failure while taking a -1 penalty, the penalty increases to -2 for 10 minutes. On a failure while taking the -2 penalty, the penalty increases to -4 for 1 hour. If the creature fails while taking the -4 penalty, it does not worsen but the 1 hour duration resets. If a creature succeeds on a saving throw, it is immune to gaining or increasing the penalty from this aura, but the already imposed penalty remains for its duration.
spell-empty-gesture: You complete the spell and hide your movements behind an unmoving image of yourself. Until the beginning of your next turn, any action taken, with the exception of movement, does not provoke attacks of opportunity or other reactions.
spell-endless-dark: This spell functions as darkness except as noted above and it is not cast upon an object, it is cast upon a point in space. From that point an area of 1 mile per level is plunged into darkness. This darkness is not contained within walls and cannot be covered or contained.
spell-endless-slumber: You complete the spell and cause the target to fall into a permanent magically-induced slumber. This operates as the sleep spell for the purposes of how the target may be awakened. Otherwise, the target may make a new save every 24 hours to awaken early. The subject does not need to eat or drink during this time, though they still age and need to breathe.
spell-enforced-destiny:
Upon completing this spell, roll a single d20 and record the result. At any point during the duration of this spell, you may force the target to use that roll for a single ability check, attack roll, initiative check, saving throw, or skill check, using the recorded result in place of a roll. This spell cannot be used to replace a roll that has already been made; the recorded result must be used instead of a roll. Once you have used this recorded result or the duration of the spell ends, the spell's effect ends. You can't have more than one instance of enforced destiny active on you at the same time.

The target may make a Will save to negate the effects of this spell when the result is forced. On a success, they can roll normally.
spell-enforced-mercy: You utter a powerful command, forcing the target creature to fight in a more merciful manner. If the creature fails their Will save, they will deal nonlethal damage with their attacks, avoid using lethal spells or other abilities, and will not attack a helpless target.
spell-entangling-shadows: When you utter the words for this spell, chains and locks made from shadow writhe into being at a point in range you designate. Creatures in the area that fail a Will save become entangled. They may attempt to free themselves with a Strength or Escape Artist check against the spell's DC. Either attempt to escape requires a full round action whether it is successful or not. In addition, the affected area is treated as difficult terrain until the beginning of your next turn.
spell-entranced-by-calamity: This spell functions as entranced by calamity, except as noted above.
spell-everything-bleeds:
You cause the creature, normally immune to bleed, to bleed like a living creature. Creatures immune to most Fortitude saves are not immune to this effect. On a failed Fortitude save, the target loses any immunity to bleed damage and blood seeps from their wounds.

Additionally, such creatures are able to be affected by blood drain-like abilities.
spell-eye-of-the-swarm: You summon a swarm of bats, rats, or spiders (your choice) that occupies your space(s) and 10 feet in all directions from you. The swarm affects any creature that enters the area of the swarm. The swarm stays with you and moves with you as you move.
spell-eyes-of-the-executioner: You enhance your vision, seeing under the skin of creatures before you, seeing their weaknesses and vital organs. You gain a +2 bonus on attack and damage rolls when making precision-based attacks, like sneak attack, or when confirming and dealing damage on a critical hit.
spell-eyes-sewn-shut:
You complete the spell and the target's eyes are fused shut. On a failed saving throw the target is blinded.

This blinding is permanent unless the target forces their eyes open with a DC 10 Strength check, a full-round DC 15 Heal check is performed on the target, or the target cuts their eyes open. The Strength check or cutting option deals 1d6 damage and 1 bleed damage.

Using the Heal check option still deals 1d6 damage but negates the bleed.

This spell is not affected by remove blindness but can be removed by heal, dispel magic, limited wish, wish, or miracle. This spell cannot target creatures without eyes or flesh with which to cover their eyes.
spell-fear-is-the-mindkiller: You fill the target's mind with such intense fear that it shuts down completely. This spell functions as feeblemind except as noted above, and if the target succeeds on their saving throw, they are shaken for 1 round.
spell-feasting-forest:
You instill a violent, bloodlust into the nature spirits and bring them to violence against your enemies.

Grasses, Undergrowth, Sand, Ice, Snow or Water. Any area within the affected area that is covered by such terrain becomes magical difficult terrain for your enemies and any creature passing through takes on 1d4 bleed. If a creature is currently bleeding from this terrain and moves through the area on another turn the bleed damage increases by 1.

Trees or other Large Plants: At the beginning of your turn, any enemy within 10 feet of a tree in the affected area takes 4d6 slashing or bludgeoning damage. A successful Reflex saving throw halves this damage. Any creature that fails their saving throw is also subject to an immediate grapple attempt by the trees. The trees have a CMB equal to your caster level + your spellcasting modifier + a size modifier for the tree's size. Its CMD for the purposes of escaping the grapple is 10 plus its CMD.

Roots, Vines and Kelp: Any area with such plant material in the area acts as though under an black tentacles spell using this spell's DCs.

Rocks, Ice or Crystals: As a free action on your turn, you can cause a loose chunk of such material to launch and strike an enemy within the area of the spell or 10 feet outside of its area. You make a ranged touch attack and on a hit, you deal 3d6 non-magical bludgeoning damage. Also on a hit, you can make a combat maneuver to trip the target using your spellcasting ability modifier instead of Strength.

If the spell deals damage, afterward, the affected area looks more verdant. When casting the spell you can designate a number of creatures that are not affected by the spell equal to your spellcasting ability modifier.
spell-fell-mist:
You fill an area with dark, roiling, illusory mist. It seems to move and shift as if composed with vile shadowy creatures. Any creature within the area when the spell is cast or at the beginning their turn, or a creature entering the area of the mist, must succeed on a Will save or be dazed for 1 round.

The shadowy mist obscures all sight, including darkvision, beyond 5 feet. A creature within 5 feet has concealment. Creatures further away have total concealment. When casting the spell, you can decide to make this mist stationary or have it move up to 10 feet per round. Wind does not affect this illusory shadow-mist.
spell-feral-crown: You complete the spell and don the crown and for the duration of the spell, any animal that comes within the radius of the spell must make a Will save or be affected by the charm animal spell until this spell's duration ends. Additionally, anytime during the spell, you can use a standard action to grant any charmed animal the effects of the rage spell until the beginning of your next turn.
spell-fireburst-greater: This spell functions as lesser fireburst except it has a wider burst radius and deals 1d10 fire damage per caster level (maximum 15d10).
spell-fireburst-lesser: You burst forth with a flash of flame dealing 1d4 fire damage per caster level (maximum 5d4) to all creatures within the burst, except for you or creatures occupying your square. A successful Reflex save halves this damage. Flammable materials burn if the flames touch them. A character can extinguish burning items as a full-round action.
spell-flashbang: You create a flash of bright fire in the area. Sighted creatures are blinded for 2d8 rounds. A successful Fortitude save reduces the effect to dazzled. Creatures outside the radius of the burst but within 120 feet of its center must make a Fortitude save or be blinded for 2d4 rounds, if they have line-of-sight on the flashbang. A successful save negates the effect for them altogether.
spell-flight-of-stars:
This special spell can only be learned and cast by divine spellcasters whose patron deity is [this god] and they possess the Evening Initiate feat. This spell enchants a non-magical shuriken to fly from your hand and unerringly strike its target (much like magic missile), though the damage does not change.

Specific parts of a creature cannot be singled out.

Inanimate objects (locks, etc.) cannot be damaged by the spell.

For every caster level above 1st, you can enchant an additional shuriken with this spell. If you shoot multiple shurikens, you can have them strike a single creature or several creatures. A single shuriken can only strike one creature. You may substitute non-magical caltrops in place of shurikens when casting this spell, with the caltrops dealing the same amount of damage as shurikens.
spell-flowers-of-sadism: You focus on the target and cause many painful bruises to form on the target. They take 1d6 points of nonlethal damage per caster level (maximum 10d6) and take a -2 penalty on attack rolls, skill checks, and ability checks until the creature no longer has nonlethal damage, from any source. A successful Fortitude save halves the nonlethal damage and negates the penalty.
spell-flowers-of-sadism-mass: This spell functions as flowers of sadism, except as noted above.
spell-forbidden-speech:
You cast the spell, making it impossible for the target to speak about a single topic. The topic needs to be narrow for the spell to work, though it is up to the GMs discretion. For example, you could forbid the target to reveal the names of their conspirators, reveal the location of a hidden treasure, or the secret password to a portal. You may not forbid the verbal components of spells, a whole life history, or topics that cover many areas of information, like the existence of an entire city.

If the target attempts to speak about the topic, they may be rendered mute, speak in gibberish or end up speaking about something else entirely. Similar effects impact their writing or otherwise communicating the topic, including pantomiming, telepathy, or pictures.

The target has not forgotten the information, and the inability to communicate can be maddening.
spell-force-of-will: This spell functions as greater force of will except as noted above.
spell-force-ray: A glowing ray of force springs from your hand. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack with the ray to deal damage to a target. The ray deals 1d4 points of force damage per caster level (maximum 25d4) and dazes the target for 1d6 rounds. A successful Fortitude save negates the dazing effect.
spell-force-sunder: You use arcane force to crush or shatter an object. The object takes 2d6 force damage per caster level, maximum 20d6. If the object is not destroyed by the damage, you may make a caster level check against the object's break DC. The object may make a Fortitude save to halve the damage, or if held by a creature, the holder can make a Reflex save to halve the damage instead.
spell-forced-isolation:
You overwhelm the target's mind, making them unable to perceive other sentient creatures.

Seemingly they are alone. For the duration of the spell other creatures are imperceptible to the target in any way, including true seeing. Creatures are not merely invisible to the target, their mind has been altered to block out other sentient beings as background noise in the same way creatures do not hear the sounds of their own bodies such as joints moving, blood pumping or even their own heartbeat outside normal circumstances and the same way many creatures (particularly humanoids) have blindspots in vision. If the target of this spell is damaged, or targeted by a hostile magical effect they receive a new save against this spell. Allies can try to end the effect by dealing damage to them, therefore triggering a new save. The target is considered flat-footed for the duration against all attacks.
spell-forever-rot: You inflict a creature with a terrible cursed version of zombie rot. The Fortitude save for disease is the spell's DC. No amount of saves or uses of remove disease can cure the target of this disease. A successful use of remove curse removes the curse and the disease simultaneously. If turned into a plague zombie by dying from the disease, it spreads its own disease as normal, not this cursed version.
spell-freezing-jet:
You spray a long stream of freezing mist from your fingertips to freeze your foe.

While the spell is a 30-foot line, only the closest target to you is affected in each round. The affected target must make a Reflex save or be dealt 1d6 + 1 per caster level (max +5) cold damage. You may elect to exclude the square adjacent to you from the area of effect if you so choose to avoid affecting allies. Any creature that fails their Reflex save against this spell two rounds in a row suffers a -1 penalty to attack rolls, damage rolls and skill or ability checks that use Strength or Dexterity. The penalty lasts for 1 round after they are no longer being targeted by this spell or until they succeed on the Reflex save for this spell two rounds in a row. Each round while concentrating on the spell, you may redirect the line of effect.
spell-freezing-snow: You cause sheets of freezing snow to spread over the ground in the area of effect. This layer of snow is 1 foot deep and constantly shifts and churns, transforming the ground in the area into difficult terrain. The snow deals 1d4 points of cold damage to any creature that ends its turn in contact with the ground within the area of effect. At the end of the duration, the snow vanishes, leaving no after-effects (other than damage dealt).
spell-freezing-spray: A spray of frost erupts from your outstretched hand, dealing 1d6 points of cold damage per caster level (maximum 15d6) to each creature within its area (Reflex half). This frost continues to affect the targets for 1 round, dealing 1d6 points of cold damage per two caster levels (maximum 7d6) to any creature that failed its saving throw against the spell (a second Reflex save on the creature's turn negates this additional damage).
spell-friendly-face:
Everyone you meet sees you as friendly and nonthreatening.

Those who fail a Will save improve their reaction toward you one step in the positive direction, thus improving your chances at making a successful Diplomacy check. Those who succeed on their save do not react toward you any more negatively than they normally would. Starting at 5th caster level, you improve their reaction two steps in the positive direction.
spell-friendly-face-3pp-orphaned-bookwor: You make small tweaks to your demeanor, voice, and appearance to seem more amenable and friendly to the viewer. You gain a +5 circumstance bonus on Diplomacy and Handle Animal checks as long as the viewers are not already hostile to you. This spell does not hide your true appearance or provide any bonus to Disguise checks.
spell-frigid-arrow: An arrow of ice springs from your hand and speeds to its target. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack to hit your target. The arrow deals 2d4 points of cold damage. For every three caster levels you possess, the cold, unless neutralized by taking fire damage, lasts for another round (to a maximum of 6 additional rounds at 18th level), dealing another 2d4 points of damage in each round.
spell-funereal-hallucinations: You complete the spell and fill the targets mind with the illusion that they have died and are on the path to their afterlife. If the target fail's their save, they stand and march in place, taking no other action, including purely mental actions. The target is effectively helpless and takes no measures to defend itself. However, if the target takes any damage, is subject to a spell that imposes a detrimental condition or effect, or they reach the end of their turn, they get another saving throw to end the spell early.
spell-funereal-malediction: You inflict a creature with a curse that makes them susceptible to dark magics of death. They take a -8 penalty on saves against death effects, energy drain, and any spell or effect that deals negative energy damage.
spell-germinate:
You touch a seed where it has been planted in the ground and it instantly germinates and sprouts where it is. This spell may be cast upon any seed so long as it is physically intact including if the seed has been cooked or damaged. This does not cause the plant to grow faster than it normally would outside of accelerating the initial phase of growth even in harsh or arid climbs where the plant would not normally take root.

Additionally this spell can be used to instantly adhere a tree graft, like for apples, or cause a transplanted plant to comfortably set down roots.
spell-ghost-light: This spell acts like the spell light except the light is only visible to you and a number of specifically designated characters equal to one per three caster levels you possess. These creatures must be within 10 feet of you when you initially cast the spell, but need not stay within that radius to be affected. No other creatures can see the light and you and the other spell targets are affected by other light conditions.
spell-glacial-plasma: You cause an explosion of polar ice followed by burning plasma to erupt from the ground in an area. Creatures and objects within the radius of the explosion take 1d6 damage per caster level (maximum 20d6). Half of the damage dealt is cold damage, the other half is fire damage. Additionally, any creature within 5 feet of the radius takes 1 damage per dice rolled within the radius, split between cold and fire damage. This spell must be cast on the ground and leaves a half-sphere crater where it originates.
spell-glassbone:
You make the creature's bones fragile. The target takes 5 additional bludgeoning damage from physical attacks.

Additionally, the target takes 1 additional damage per damage dice of spells that deal damage via bones, like boneshaker. If the target does not have bones or an exoskeleton, this spell is ineffective.
spell-glassbone-mass: This spell functions as glassbone except it affects multiple creatures within range.
spell-globe-of-invulnerability-greater: This spell functions like lesser globe of invulnerability, except that it also excludes 5th-level spells and spell-like effects.
spell-glue-seal-greater:
This spell functions as glue seal, except as noted here.

When you use this spell to cover a solid surface with sticky glue, the 5-foot squares must form a continuous area, each part of which must be within the spell's range. When you use this spell to create a sticky coating on items, no two of the targeted items can be more than 30 feet apart. You cannot target both items and surfaces with a single casting of this spell.
spell-gout-of-flame:
You spray a long gout of flame from your fingertips engulfing your foe.

While the spell is a 30-foot line, only the closest target to you is affected in each round.

The affected target must make a Reflex save or be dealt 1d6 + 1 per caster level (max +5) fire damage. You may elect to exclude the square adjacent to you from the area of effect if you so choose. These flames can ignite flammable materials and any creature that fails their Reflex save against this spell two rounds in a row catches fire as per the environmental rules in the Pathfinder Core Rulebook. If the target is already on fire, this spell only deals 1 damage per caster level (max 5) but the target is unable to roll the Reflex save to put out the fire on themselves during that round. Each round while concentrating on the spell, you may redirect the line of effect.
spell-gravity-bomb:
You forcibly twist a creature's gravity field inwards, causing on-going damage that disrupts the creature's body even on a cellular level and slightly increases the damage of certain attacks against the target.

Each round at the beginning of the target's turn, they take 1d4 points of damage. Additionally, this spell increases the bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing dealt to the target creature by any ranged attack or ranged spell by 2 points. This secondary effect only applies if the target creature does not have any effect or defense that reduces the damage dealt.

Finally, each round in which the target creature suffers the damage from gravity bomb, any fast healing or regeneration they possess does not work in the following round.
spell-gravity-bomb-greater: This functions as per gravity bomb, except that the damage it deals each round to the target is 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier. Additionally, it increases the bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage dealt to the target creature by any ranged attack or ranged spell by 5 points.
spell-gravity-bomb-mass: This functions as gravity bomb, except that it affects multiple creatures, the damage it deals each round is 1d6 + your spellcasting ability modifier, and it increases the bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage dealt to the target creature by any ranged attack or ranged spell by 4 points.
spell-gravity-bomb-mass-greater: This functions as greater gravity bomb, except that it affects multiple creatures, the damage it deals each round is 2d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier, and it increases the bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage dealt to the target creature by any ranged attack or ranged spell by 10 points.
spell-green-flame-fist: One of your hands, or a weapon you are holding bursts into a strange green flame which sheds light equal to that of a torch. With a successful melee touch attack you deal 3d6 fire damage plus 1 point of fire damage per caster level. The target must then make a Fortitude save or catch fire for 1 round per caster level and take 3d6+ 1 per caster level fire damage each round. A successful Fortitude save each round halves the damage. A creature can only be suffering from one instance of this effect at a time. You can also choose to add this effect to a natural or manufactured weapon you possess, triggering when the weapon deals damage to an opponent rather than as a melee touch attack.
spell-groom:
The touched creature is cleaned up as if they took a bath, cleaned with soap, their hair, both head and body, are trimmed or cleaned up to local fashion and their worn clothing is cleaned up and smoothed out.

This does not repair any damage to weapons, armor, or clothing, but at least they're cleaned and polished. The subject creature gains a +1 circumstance bonus on Charisma-based skill checks for 24 hours or until they take a bath or get dirty.
spell-guileful-gaze: You complete the spell, and your face shifts into a distracting form. The target takes a -1 penalty on saves against illusions. The target only takes the penalty while they can see you.
spell-halo-of-bones:
You create a floating disc of bones that hovers behind your head. You create one bone per caster level. As a standard action, you can deploy one of the bones to create a standard human skeleton under your control, or launch it as a projectile at a target within 60 feet.

If you create a skeleton, it persists until destroyed or until the spell ends at which time it crumbles to grave dust. This skeleton does not count against your HD limit for undead controlling but gains the benefits of any feats or abilities that bolster created undead.

If you fire it as a projectile, you must make a standard ranged attack against the target's AC but using your spellcasting ability modifier in place of your Dexterity modifier, if higher. If the bone-projectile hits, it deals 1d8 piercing damage plus your spellcasting ability modifier and is considered magic for the purposes of bypassing DR.
spell-hammer-of-desolation:
You create a massive blast of green energy in an area.

This spell acts as disintegrate except it affects an area and a successful Fortitude save halves the damage.
spell-head-of-the-medusa:
You complete the spell and don the medusa-head mask.

The eyes in the medusa's mask glow and its mouth opens in a violent snarl. Any enemy that meets your gaze, must make a Fortitude save or turn into a mindless, inert statue as per the spell flesh to stone. A creature can avert their eyes as with any other gaze attack but you can focus your gaze on a target as a standard action to force a saving throw on them.
spell-healing-touch: This spell functions as lesser healing touch except that the amount healed is 1d8 + 1 per caster level (max +15).
spell-healing-touch-3pp-orphaned-bookwor: This spell functions as lesser healing touch except that the amount healed is 1d6 + 1 per caster level (max +10).
spell-heavens-call: You overlay a realistic illusion of a heavenly realm upon an area. Structures, equipment, and creatures within the area are not hidden, though environmental features take on an angelic appearance. Evil-aligned creatures within the area must make a Will save or become shaken and also take a –2 penalty on saves versus fear effects; the fear and penalty persists as long as the creature remains in the area. Good-aligned creatures gain a +4 bonus on Will saves against fear effects while within the area.
spell-hellfire-greater: This spell functions as hellfire except as above and the maximum damage is increased to 20d6.
spell-hellfire-lesser:
Hellish fire bursts forth from the ground and fills the area. Each creature in the area takes 1d6 damage per caster level (maximum 10d6). Half the damage is fire, but the other half results directly from unholy power and is therefore not subject to being reduced by fire resistance. This spell must be centered on the ground.

A successful Reflex save halves this damage.
spell-hollow-prophet:
This spell functions as greater bestow curse except as noted above and instead of the curse options, the target is cut off from the ability to observe the flow of time and their third eye.

All divination spells cast by the target automatically fail.
spell-homicidal-repentance: You fill the target with sadness and guilt anytime they harm a target. On a failed Will save, if the target deals damage to another creature, they take a -1 penalty to attack rolls, saving throws, ability checks, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls for 1d6 rounds. If the target renders a creature unconscious, or kills/destroys them, the penalty is increased to -2 for 2d6 rounds. The conditions do not stack, only the highest penalty is applied and each subsequent penalty instead increases the duration of the highest penalty.
spell-horizon-of-spikes: You fill the area with a mass of caltrops that move and shift to injure your enemies. The area is considered difficult terrain for your enemies and any enemy passing through the area takes 1 damage per 5 feet moved, and/or if they spend an action attacking, they take 1 damage. You and your allies are unaffected. A creature that takes damage must make a Reflex save or injure their feet. Their speed is reduced by half for 24 hours or until they receive healing via a spell or a Heal check against the DC of the spell.
spell-horns-of-the-triceratops: The target grows three imposing horns as their hide thickens and grays. When you cast this spell the target grows three horns which can be used as a primary gore attack which deals 1d8 piercing damage plus 1-1/2 times their Strength modifier. If this gore attack is made at the end of a charge it deals double damage. In addition the target gains a bonus to natural armor equal to 1/3 your caster level.
spell-hymn-of-battle: With a wave of your hand a distant hum grows louder until an uplifting chorus urges your allies towards victory, all allies within range may make a new save against any effect currently affecting them. While this spell lasts allies continue to be allowed additional saving throws against ongoing effects at the start of your turn.
spell-hymn-of-dissonance: Each creature within the area who is not already taking an action to physically attack a creature during their turn must make a Will save. On a failure, they must physically attack the nearest creature, whether enemy or ally. This will include moving up to their normal movement to do so. If they are unable to attack during the turn due to no targets nearby, they are nauseated for 1 round. You are not affected by the song.
spell-icy-impalement:
Each target is surrounded and impaled by freezing ice crystals. Each target in the area takes 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 20d6). Half of the damage is cold, the other is magical piercing.

Additionally to the damage, the target is slowed as per the slow spell for 1 round per caster level. A successful Reflex save halves the damage and negates the slow effect.
spell-illusory-pit:
You create an illusory pit within the area. Any creature entering the area or beginning their turn within must make a Will save or believe they are falling into a bottomless pit. While the spell is active all creatures can 'see' the pit in the area. If a creature fails their saving throw, they fall prone and are unable to take any actions but flail around as they believe they are falling.

Each round at the end of their turn, a creature may attempt a Reflex save to try to stop their 'fall', on a success, they may then reattempt a Will save to disbelieve the illusion, otherwise they cling to the ground as if they have barely saved themselves. Each round thereafter they may make a Climb check against the spell save DC to 'climb out', failing by 5 or more means they think they are falling again. If they succeed or fail by less than 5, they may attempt the Will save to disbelieve the spell.

Flying creatures are not affected by this spell. If a non-flying creature succeeds on the Will save for this spell or the spell's duration ends, they are freed from the it's effects and are no longer affected by it but they are dazed until the beginning of their next turn.
spell-imaginary-form:
Channeling magic wrought from a planar realm such as the Plane of Dreams, the Astral, the Spirit World, or other similar location where illusion-based magic are abundant, you weave a deception of weakness so powerful that you fool the target creature into believing they have been partially transformed into a pale imitation of themselves.

On a failed initial Will save, the target creature is convinced that they have been affected by the shadow transformation spell instead and subsequently transformed into a weak shadowy version of themself.

The reality though is that the target creature is fooled into believing that all of their attacks and special abilities (including spells, if any) deal only one-fifth (20%) of the normal damage. Any of the target's attacks or special abilities that don't deal damage are only onefifth (20%) of their normal effects (if applicable) or 20% of working normally instead.

Because they believe that they are made into a creature of shadowstuff, if they take damage while under the effects of this spell, their mind attempts to reconcile with why they are taking full damage. Thus, the target creature gains a new saving throw once each round at the start of their turn to disbelieve the spell's effect if they have taken damage from any source in the previous round.

Attempts to identify imaginary form with a skill check incorrectly identify it as shadow transformation.
spell-incendiary-prayer: You utter a prayer of cleansing fires. All allies within the aura gain a fire resistance of 5. All enemies beginning their turn in or entering the aura take 1d6 fire damage. A successful Fortitude save reduced that damage taken that round to 1.
spell-incinerate: You cause the temperature around the target to raise quickly, setting them on fire. The target takes 1d6 points of fire damage + 1 point per caster level (maximum +10). The target must then make a Fortitude save or be set on fire 1 round per caster level. The DC to put out the fire is the spell's save DC. After the duration, the DC reverts to the normal DC for putting out a fire. If in an area of cold or winter weather, or if the creature has the cold or water subtype, they gain a +5 bonus on the saving throw.
spell-incinerate-greater: This functions as incinerate, except that it affects all creatures within the area.
spell-indifference:
You fill a target creature with feelings of indifference toward a secondary target creature. The target's attitude is shifted to indifferent and cannot be shifted by Diplomacy and they are immune to spells like 25 charm person or spite of the same spell level or lower.

Additionally, the target cannot be treated as an ally or enemy for the purposes of spell or ability targeting and cannot provide flanking, teamwork feat benefits, or similar benefits to any other creature.

If the affected creature was hostile to the secondary target, they gain a +5 bonus on its saving throw. They will no longer be hostile on a failure but if attacked, will defend themselves and attack their attacker, though still feeling indifference while doing so.
spell-indifference-mass: This spell functions as indifference, except that it affects a number of secondary targets whose Hit Dice don't exceed twice your level. If there are more potential targets than you can affect, you choose them one at a time until you reach the limit of HD you can affect. If you target only one creature, you ignore the spell's HD limit.
spell-infiltrators-welcome: Upon completing the spell you become invisible as per the invisibility spell and you gain a +5 insight bonus on Disable Device checks and Perception checks to find traps. If you perform an action that would end the invisibility effect, like performing an offensive action, you lose the bonuses to your skill checks as well.
spell-infinite-regression:
You finish the spell and change the target into a primordial, un-evolved version of their species. If the target fails a Fortitude save followed by a Will save, their Intelligence drops to 2, and they lose access to skills that use Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma skills that require training. Additionally, they gain a +.

Strength and Constitution as they become more animalistic and they gain a 1d6 natural attack of their choice. The target retains class levels, feats and abilities gained but they lose the ability to use any spells or any abilities that require verbal components as they lose any linguistic capacity.

Any polymorph effects on the target are automatically dispelled when the target fails their saving throws, and as long as this spell remains in effect, the target cannot use other polymorph spells or effects to assume a new form with the exception of baleful polymorph.
spell-infinite-terror: This spell functions as the spell fear, except on a failed save, the affected creature is panicked and cowering for 1 minute or shaken for 1 round. At the beginning of the next minute the affected creature must make another Will save or be affected. This continues until the spell's duration ends. A casting of remove fear or other spell or ability that removes a fear condition only removes the active condition, it does not remove the spell or the need to roll a Will save in the next minute.
spell-instant-turnkey: A flick of the wrist opens the door. You may make a Disable Device check this turn as a free action with a +2 insight bonus on the skill check.
spell-invocation-of-doom: This spell functions as doom except creatures normally immune to fear effects, whether by immunity to fear or to mind-affecting, are still affected by this spell. This does not cause the creature to be susceptible to further fear effect, nor can it be used to increase a fear condition above shaken.
spell-invocation-of-doom-mass: This spell functions as invocation of doom, except it affects multiple creatures.
spell-itchy-feet: You complete the spell and the target is filled with the irresistible urge to move. For the duration of the spell, the subject must begin their turn by moving at least 10 feet by their main movement mode. This movement provokes attacks of opportunity as normal. The target has control over where they move, so long as they move at least 10 feet from their starting point. If the target is unable to move 10 feet in a given turn due to any reason, they are dazed for the round instead.
spell-joyous-laugh:
You let out a laugh full of joy and happiness. You and your allies within the area gain a +2 morale bonus to attack rolls and saves against fear effects, plus temporary hit points equal to 1d8 + caster level (to a maximum of 1d8+20 at caster level 20th). Enemies in the area must make a Will save or take a -2 penalty on attack rolls and saves against fear effects for the duration of the spell.

Creatures must be able to hear the laugh to be affected.
spell-keen-fangs: You cause claws and fangs to deal more grievous wounds. You invest the targeted creatures with primal power increasing the threat range of all natural weapons they possess by one. For example if a creature possesses a claw attack with a critical threat range of 19-20/x2 this spell increases the range to 18-20/x2. This increase stacks with effects such as the Improved Critical feat but is applied last.
spell-life: You cause the target creature to float in the air at a point 5 feet above where they were previously. They are unable to move from the spot as if they are in an area of no gravity. They are still able to make attacks, cast spells, and use abilities. However, they are considered flat footed and any attack rolls, including spell attack rolls, take a -4 penalty. Additionally, the target is considered 10 pounds lighter per caster level for the purpose of the violent thrust function of the telekinesis spell and takes a penalty against bull rush attempts equal to the caster level of the spell.
spell-lift-mass: This spell functions as lift except it affects multiple creatures.
spell-lightless-star: You create a shifting orb of shadow that explodes in the target area. The spell deals 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 15d6). Half of the damage is cold, and the other half is negative energy. This negative energy does not harm undead, nor does it heal them.
spell-lightless-walk:
You may transform into a utter-dark shadow as a standard action and instantly travel in a straight line to a distance of up to 120 feet, re-materializing in the new location as a free action. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity. Creatures in this line take 10d6 points of cold damage and the area of the line is treated as deeper darkness for 1 round (a successfu Reflex save halves the damage, spell resistance applies).

Objects and liquids in the path are frozen creating sheets of ice if applicable. If your path is interrupted by a barrier or otherwise deflected, you materialize short of your final destination in the nearest open space; targets in the line to that point take damage as normal. You are immune to cold while this spell lasts.
spell-lightning-bolt-greater: This spell functions as lightning bolt except the maximum is 15d6 and you can fire an additional lightning bolt per 4 caster levels. These extra bolts of lightning may be fired in any direction except directions you have already fired lightning bolts through the casting of this spell. Multiple bolts that hit the same creature due to size do not increase the damage dealt.
spell-lightning-burst: You burst out with a sheet of lightning dealing 1d6 electricity damage per caster level (maximum 15d6) to all creatures in the burst. You are not affected by this spell and a Reflex save halves the damage.
spell-lost-in-aimless-chaos: This spell functions as hallucinatory terrain except the terrain created is chaotic and constantly shifting. Any creature within the area or entering it must make a Will save or be confused as per the spell confusion for 1 round. Only the confusion effect is considered mind-affecting and is subject to spell resistance.
spell-mage-armor-lesser: This spell functions as mage armor except as above and the armor bonus provided is only +2.
spell-mages-barracks: This spell functions as secure shelter, except it can house up to 40 medium-sized individuals. The building has doors at both ends and windows on either side of the doors. The doors and windows can be barred from the inside. The beds are basic bunk-beds, there are tables and stools enough for 20 at a time, two large fireplaces, and enough wood for one night. Additionally there is enough food for 40 medium individuals for one evening next to each fireplace.
spell-mages-persistent-blade:
A small blade of force blinks into existence that resembles the knife used as a focus for this spell. The blade can move up to 40 feet and attack a designated target within the spell's range. Directing the dagger to a target is a swift action except on the turn the spell is cast where it is a free action. The blade attacks once per round on your turn unless it has no target. The weapon uses your base attack bonus and your spellcasting ability modifier for the attack roll and has a critical threat range of 19-20. The dagger also gains any enhancement bonus to the attack possessed by the dagger used as a focus.

The dagger deals 1d4 damage plus your spellcasting ability modifier and any enhancement bonus on the dagger used as a focus. No other properties on the dagger are transferred to the mage's persistent blade.

This dagger will move to flank a target if it is able to on the directed target. The blade is made of force and can strike ethereal and incorporeal creatures. If the target has spell resistance, the spell resistance is checked before the first attack. If the caster level check fails, the dagger is unable to target that creature for the duration of the spell. The blade has an AC 14 (+2 size, +2 Dex) and has 1 hit point.
spell-magma-pit: This spell functions as acid pit except the pit is filled with molten lava and deals 4d6 fire damage instead of acid damage.
spell-maintained-by-force: You quickly speak the spell and forcibly keep a creature alive by holding their body and soul together using force energy. The target is kept from dying for as long as you concentrate on the spell, though they are still staggered. This spell cannot affect creatures whose body has been destroyed, soul eaten or destroyed, or if the target is reduced to 10 damage per caster level lower than their death threshold. Healing a creature while being kept alive by maintained by force can allow this character to live. If the spell ends while the target is still below their death threshold or was killed by an instant- death spell, they die as normal.
spell-malevolent-haze:
Malevolent haze creates a shifting and moving cloud of blood-red vapor that functions like the solid fog spell.

In addition to slowing down creatures and obscuring sight, the vile vapors sap the life out of living creatures.

Each round on your turn, and when the spell is first cast, the fog deals 2d6 negative energy damage to each living creature within it. This spell does not heal undead creatures.
spell-mantle-of-disorder:
You radiate an aura of power out to a radius of 30 feet, granting your allies additional power to combat chaos.

While in the aura's radius, whenever an ally (including yourself) misses on an attack roll against a chaotic-aligned enemy within the range of the aura, the next attack roll they make against that enemy gains a +2 sacred (or profane, if the ally is evil). While this spell lasts, against any given enemy, this bonus is cumulative with itself if the ally consecutively misses hitting that enemy. Once the ally has succeeded in hitting an enemy, the bonus from this spell is reset to 0 against that enemy.

If the enemy is a chaotic-aligned fey or outsider or if they have the chaos subtype, the bonus provided by mantle of order is increased to +4 instead.
spell-mantle-of-order:
You radiate an aura imbued with order and mechanical precision out to a radius of 30 feet, granting your allies additional computational ability to strike with greater accuracy against agents of chaos.

While in the aura's radius, whenever an ally (including yourself) misses on an attack roll against a chaotic-aligned enemy within the aura, the next attack roll they make against that enemy gains a +2 sacred (or profane, if the ally is evil). This bonus is cumulative if the ally continues misses hitting that enemy. Once the ally has succeeded in hitting an enemy, the bonus from this spell is reset to 0 against that enemy.

If an enemy is instead a chaotic-aligned fey or outsider or if they have the chaos subtype, the bonus provided by mantle of order is increased to +4 instead.
spell-marching-chant-greater: This spell functions as marching chant, except as above. You also do not need to concentrate (via singing or chanting) to maintain this spell. Instead, you need only spend 10 minutes daily singing or chanting before attempting to hustle or overland travel for the first time each day of this spell's duration to maintain the effects of greater marching chant for the affected creatures. Failure to do so ends the spell for all affected creatures. Additionally, greater marching chant makes a forced march easier to endure for the spell's targets. When a target creature attempts a forced march each day, the Constitution check to avoid suffering nonlethal damage from each hour of forced march is DC is 5 (+1 per extra hour). Affected creatures also ignore any fatigue, but not the nonlethal damage, caused by a forced march. Once greater marching chant ends, if an affected creature still has any remaining nonlethal damage caused by a forced march, they become fatigued (or exhausted if already fatigued by another effect).
spell-mark-of-the-blade: You touch the target creature and a mark of a bladed weapon appears on their skin. Anytime the target takes slashing or piercing damage they are dealt 1d4 extra damage. This damage is increased on a critical by 1d4 for each multiple. For example, a critical hit from a greataxe would deal 3d4 extra damage.
spell-martial-master:
This special spell can only be learned and cast by divine spellcasters whose patron deity is [this deity] and they possess the Equilibrium Initiate feat. This spell temporarily grants you sufficient knowledge and experience to expertly execute one type of martial maneuver.

For the duration of the spell, you gain the use of one combat feat of your choice. This selected combat feat must enables you to perform a combat maneuver without provoking an attack of opportunity, such as Improved Bull Rush, Improved Disarm, etc. If the selected combat feat has prerequisites, such as a minimum ability score or base attack bonus, you are not required to have them. If the prerequisites are other feats you do not have, you are considered to have them for the express purpose of being able to use the selected combat feat for the duration of this spell.

You may spend a full-round action at any time during this spell's duration to select a different combat feat, as described above, but the spell's remaining duration is reduced by 1 minute.

You cannot have more than one casting of martial master in effect on you and you cannot use martial master to meet the prerequisites of other feats (nor qualify for other effects).
spell-mask-of-night: The target is covered in a shadow that hides their full being. Their countenance is obscured, but their size remains identifiable. This does not provide them any protection from attacks, but they are not affected by light or sunlight if they are damaged by such or have weaknesses like sunlight powerlessness or light blindness. Additionally, they gain a resistance bonus on saving throws and deflection bonus to AC against spells or effects with the light descriptor or that are light-based equal to 1/2 your caster level.
spell-masked-performance:
Masked performance transforms the audible components required to produce either of your mundane performances with the Perform skill or bardic performances (including language-dependent effects) into one specific background noise that is natural and appropriate for the immediate environment. Those who hear your bardic performance masked in this way remain unaware of its true nature while the bardic performance's effects remain the same.

For example, you could use this spell to make a bardic performance for distraction, inspire courage, or even suggestion sounds like footsteps on gravel, the buzzing of a bee, the sounds of water from a creek, and so forth.

You choose what your mundane performance or your bardic performance altered by masked performance should sound like at the time of the casting, but it must be a noise that belongs in the immediate environment.

Anyone listening to the performance that makes a successful Will save realizes that the sound has been altered and can hear its true nature.

Material Component: A small bit of whatever naturally makes the sound you're trying to mimic. For example, a small handful of gravel, a bee's stinger, and a small flask with water taken from a creek are some of the possible material components that can be used to generate the specific background noise listed above.
spell-masochism-sadism:
This spell comes in one of two forms, chosen when cast. If sadism is chosen, you gain the bonus for each 10 points of damage you deal to another. If you instead choose masochism, you gain the bonuses for every 10 points damage you receive.

Regardless of the type chosen, the damage dealt counts only after DR, immunity or resistance is applied. Nonlethal damage counts toward the damage dealt for bonuses.

You gain a +1 luck bonus on attack rolls, saving throws, and skill checks for the round to a maximum of +1 per 2 caster levels you possess.
spell-masters-proficiency: With a touch, the knowledge of soldiers and generals flows through you. When you cast this spell you draw the focus with a flourish and gain proficiency with the specific item used as the focus of this spell. If you are already proficient with the item used as the focus for this spell it instead gains an enhancement bonus to attack rolls equal to 1/4 your caster level, rounded down (minimum +1).
spell-meltdown: Molten metal explodes from your space in all directions, causing 1d6 points of damage per caster level (maximum 20d6) to creatures and unattended objects in the area. On your turn in each of the next 2 rounds, creatures and objects that failed their saves against the initial burst take an additional 1d6 points of fire damage per 2 caster levels (maximum 10d6) unless the molten metal is cooled by taking cold damage or otherwise removed.
spell-minor-disguise: You use magic to make minor, cosmetic changes in your appearance as if using a disguise kit. The spell does not change the actual structure of your features or body. It can add color to hair, paint wrinkles upon your face, give you a scar, darken your teeth, etc. Using this spell does not speed up the disguising process but it can be used in conjunctions with spells that do. This spell gives you a +2 circumstance bonus on the Disguise check made during the casting of the spell. If using an actual disguise kit in conjunction with the spell, the circumstance bonus increases to +4.
spell-mire-deep:
You create a large patch of deep quicksand. Creatures in the area must make a Reflex save. On a failure the target falls into the quicksand right where they are and must immediately make a Swim check to keep from going under the surface. On a successful saving throw, the target moves 5 feet closer to the edge, or if they are already at the edge of the area, they get to move to just outside the area assuming it is safe to do so.

Creatures must make a Swim check DC 7 + the caster level of the spell to tread water and stay in place, or DC 12 + the caster level of the spell to move 5 feet in any direction. If a creature fails by 5 or more, they sink down 5 feet and must begin holding their breath or drown. Such creatures can attempt to swim back to the surface with a Swim check DC 12 + the caster level of the spell plus +1 per consecutive round being under the surface. In all cases the Swim checks are move actions, but any creature under the surface suffers a 50% spell failure due to the viscous nature of the quicksand and retrieving or stowing items requires a Strength check equal to DC 12 + the caster level of the spell.

A creature may attempt to save a creature stuck in the magical quicksand with a long branch or other long item. The rescuer must make a Strength check DC 12 + the caster level of the spell as a standard action to pull and the rescu-ee must make a Strength check DC 7 + the caster level of the spell to hold onto the item. If both checks, the trapped creature is pulled 5 feet closer to safety. If the trapped creature fails to hold on they must make a DC 12 + the caster level of the spell Swim check or go under the surface. The standard action to save the stuck creature does not include retrieving an item with which to save them.

Creatures that are large, with the exception of swarms, require more turns than smaller creatures to be affected.

Huge creatures treat the area as difficult terrain on their first turn, then on subsequent failures, they are stuck.

Creatures larger than huge treat the area as difficult terrain only and do not need to make a saving throw.

The suction and viscous nature of the quicksand prevents flight or levitation from helping a stuck creature from escaping, but such creatures that are flying or levitating do not initially get affected by the spell. Control water can be used to grant creatures in the affected area to gain a +5 bonus on their Swim checks.

Transmute mud to stone turns the affected area to stone, trapping creatures within, per that spell. Other spells and their interaction with the quicksand are at the discretion of the GM.

Otherwise this quicksand operates as normal and when the spell ends, any trapped creatures are left on the ground where the quicksand was.
spell-mire-deep-pit: This spell functions as mire deep except the area is smaller and the target falls down a pit first as per the spell create pit, the maximum depth of the pit is 100 feet, then the quicksand extends for 20 feet past the bottom of the pit.
spell-misguidance:
This spell imposes a divine curse of bad decision making on the subject with a touch.

The creature gets a -1 penalty on a single attack roll, saving throw, or skill check. You must choose to impose the penalty before they make the roll to which it applies.
spell-molten-chains:
The chain in your hand turns into a long length of red hot chains that shoot forth and wrap around the designated target. The target takes 2d6 fire damage and is pinned. A successful Reflex save negates the panned condition and reduces the damage to 1d6.

On subsequent rounds, a creature that failed their save may attempt to free themselves of the chains by either attempting an Escape Artist (DC 15 + your caster level) check or Strength check (DC 10 + your caster level).

Each round they attempt such a check, they take 2d6 fire damage. Any creature attempting to physically aid the target takes 1d6 fire damage in the round they aid.
spell-moonfire:
You unleash a blast of pale-white fire. All living creatures take 1d8 damage per 2 caster levels (maximum 10d8). Undead or shapechangers in the area instead take 1d8 damage per caster level (maximum 20d8). A successful Reflex save halves this damage. Any creature that is normally affected by moonlight must make a Will save or automatically undergo the effects of those abilities.

After the damage is dealt, the area continues to glow with the pale light, creating an area of bright illumination for 1 round per caster level. Additionally, shapechangers and undead are illuminated as per faerie fire for 1 round per caster level as the moonfire reveals their nature.
spell-moonlight-aura:
You are surrounded by an aura of pale moonlight. For the duration, you illuminate the area to a minimum of dim light. This penetrates any darkness effect of the aura's spell level or lower. It does not counter or dispel the effect, however.

Additionally, the aura triggers any effects set off by exposure to moonlight, like lycanthropy, unless the creature makes a Will save. Once a creature has made the Will save against the aura, they are immune to its effects for 24 hours.
spell-moral-bankruptcy: This spell functions as moral bankruptcy, except as noted above.
spell-mystic-disarmament:
Weapons held by creatures within the burst are wrenched from their grasp and dropped to the ground.

An affected creature can make a Reflex save to negate this effect.
spell-mystic-disarmament-greater: This spell functions as mystic disarmament except the greater burst radius and the target takes 1d4 nonlethal damage per 2 caster levels as the weapon is wrenched from them.
spell-natures-favor: You call upon the power of nature and grant the touched animal a luck bonus to attack and damage rolls equal to 1/2 your caster level.
spell-natures-favor-communal: This spell functions as nature's favor, except you divide the duration in 1-minute intervals among the creatures touched.
spell-nauseating-barrier: You are closely surrounded by a barely visible magical field. The field provides a +1 deflection bonus to AC and a +1 resistance bonus on saves. Any creature that strikes you with a melee attack is nauseated for 1 round (Fort negates). Once the field has nauseated an opponent, the spell is discharged.
spell-nauseating-barrier-greater: This spell functions as nauseating barrier, except as noted above, and it provides a +2 bonus to AC and on saving throws. It is not discharged until it has nauseated a number of creatures equal to your caster level.
spell-necromorphic-illumination: You cause all the undead in the burst to be limned with ghostly blue light. They glow light torches, and take a -20 penalty to Stealth checks. The undead cannot benefit from concealment from darkness, blur, displacement, invisibility, or similar effects.
spell-necrotoxic: You inflict the touched undead with a magical poison that only destroys undead. Undead are not immune to the Fortitude save from this spell. The poison deals 1d3 Charisma damage per round for 6 rounds. Undead are not immune to this ability score damage. Poisoned undead can make a Fortitude save each round to negate the damage and end the affliction.
spell-negative-rain:
This special spell can only be learned and cast by divine spellcasters whose patron deity is [this god] and they possess the Equilibrium Initiate feat.

Negative rain is both an offensive and defensive dual-school spell that sucks the life from your opponents and bestows that life force upon your allies.

When you cast this spell, you create a zone of negative energy. For the duration of this spell, whenever a creature starts their turn within the area of effect, they take 1 point of negative energy damage for every two caster levels you possess (maximum 5). You can then channel that energy as positive energy to target one other creature within the area of effect to heal it of an equal amount of damage. This channeling occurs instantly and it does not require any action on your part while you concentrate to maintain this spell.

Creatures immune to energy drain, such as constructs, are not harmed by the negative energy. Since undead are powered by negative energy, the normally harmful effects of this spell heal them instead. However, undead are harmed by the positive energy of this spell, though they may make a Will save to negate the damage from this positive energy each time they are targeted.
spell-negative-threads: This spell functions as the spell web except the webs are infused with negative energy. Any creature that enters or begins their turn within the webs takes 2d4 negative energy damage. Additionally, the caster can move the webs up to 10 feet as a swift action.
spell-neural-shock: You jolt the target's mind with electricity. The target takes 1d6 points of electricity damage + 1 point per caster level (maximum +10). The target must then make a Will save or be staggered for 1 round per caster level. The target gains another Will save to end the effect at the beginning of each of their rounds.
spell-neural-shock-greater: This functions as neural shock, except that it affects all creatures within the area.
spell-nights-ember:
You hold up the coal which alights in a soft orange light.

This light does not burn your hand, however any creature in the radius with the shadow subtype or currently in an area of dim light or darker is covered is a nimbus of orange flame, glowing like a candle as per the spell faerie fire. Additionally at the beginning of their turn, an affected creature must make a Fortitude save or take 1 fire damage. A successful saving throw negates damage but not the highlighting. This fire can target incorporeal creatures.
spell-nightstalker-form: Your form twists and splits into hideous shadow. When you cast this spell you inhale the bottled air and transform into a shadowy version of yourself. You gain darkvision 60 ft (or your existing darkvision increases by 60 ft), a +4 enhancement bonus to Dexterity, a +3 luck bonus on attack rolls, a +3 deflection bonus to armor class, and a +5 bonus to Perception and Stealth skill checks. In addition you deal an extra 2d6 damage to creatures you flank or are denied their Dexterity bonus to armor class, this stacks with sneak attack and similar abilities. You may end this spell early as a swift action, becoming incorporeal and gaining a 60 ft fly speed until the end of your turn. However you can only move until the beginning of your next turn.
spell-no-time-to-bleed: This spell functions as no time to bleed except it affects multiple creatures as noted above.
spell-nourishing-the-fire:
You cut your hand and take 1 point of damage, then cast your blood into the air while chanting the spell.

For the duration all fires and fire effects within the area are empowered. All fire-based lights increase their bright and dim light radii by 10 feet. All fire-based spells and effects increase their DC by 1 if the effect is within the aura. Additionally all fire damage dealt within the radius is increased by 1 per dice of fire damage dealt, or by 1 if no dice are used. Finally, any creature with the fire subtype gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage while within the aura.
spell-oblation-husk: You touch the target with a shell and they are granted divine protection from your deity. They gain a +1 deflection bonus to AC and against saves against divine spells or abilities (like channel energy). Additionally, the target gains temporary hit points equal to 1d8 + caster level (to a maximum of 1d8+10 temporary hit points at caster level 10th).
spell-oblation-husk-mass: This spell functions as oblation husk except as noted above and the bonus maximum for the temporary hit points increases to 15.
spell-offering-to-the-wild:
You complete the sacrifice and anoint each creature to be protected with some part of the sacrifice, typically blood or ash, leaving the rest to the spirits of nature.

For the duration the protected creatures gain a +2 bonus on initiative checks and Knowledge (geography), Perception, Stealth, and Survival skill checks while in the terrain that the spell was cast in.

The terrain is determined similarly to a ranger's favored terrain and stacks with the effects of that ability.

Additionally, any animal or magical beast native to the affected wilds begins with a neutral disposition and will not run from nor attack a protected creature, unless attacked first or impelled by some outside means. This spell cannot be used on urban terrain.
spell-optimism:
You bolster the target's confidence and instill a sense of bravery.

This confidence manifests as a +2 morale bonus on attack rolls, saving throws, ability checks, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls. Additionally, the target increases the bonus to +4 on saves vs. emotion and fear effects. No amount of failure counters the spell's effects—the target simply explains away negative events with a self-assured perspective.

Certain events can solidify the character's belief that they are the best. Whenever the target rolls a natural 20 on an attack roll or saving throw, or succeeds on an ability or skill check by more than 5, the bonuses to rolls imposed by optimism becomes +3 (or +6 vs. emotion or fear) for 1 round.

This increased penalty doesn't stack, even if multiple triumphs occur on the same round.
spell-ordeal-of-iron:
A rain of iron shards and bands rain down in the area dealing 2d6 bludgeoning damage and 1d6 slashing damage to every creature in the area. This damage only occurs once, when the spell is cast. Any creature that takes damage from the spell must make a Reflex save or be bound by the iron and entangled. A DC 18 Strength check or escape artist can free the creature from the iron.

For the remaining duration of the spell, the shards and other iron debris covers the ground, making the entire area difficult terrain and deals 1d4 slashing damage to any creature moving more than 5 feet through the area.

At the end of the duration, the iron debris disappears, leaving no further aftereffects.
spell-overload: You cause the target's magical defenses to malfunction. You make a targeted dispel attempt per the spell dispel magic at the highest CL of qualifying effects. On a success the spell- or magic-item-granted resistances and immunities to damage, AC bonuses, and saving throw bonuses are suppressed for the duration of this spell.
spell-painwrack: As you complete the final utterance, the target is wracked with such pain that it doubles over and collapses. The physical presentation of the immense pain is determined by the caster but it involves various blisters, sores, welts and bruises spontaneously, and painfully, causing the target to be incapacitated by the pain. For the duration of the spell, the subject falls prone and is blinded and helpless. Each round on its turn, the subject may attempt a new saving throw to end the effect. This is a full-round action that does not provoke attacks of opportunity. After the duration of the spell expires or if the creature successfully makes their Fortitude save, they are sickened for 3d10 minutes.
spell-paired-seals-of-private-communicat:
You lay down a pair of magically entangled seals (one each for you and the touched creature) that enable mental communication. The focus of this spell is the pair of permanently inscribed seals on you and the touched creature (effects like erase can remove the inscribed seals).

The bearer of any one of the paired seals can mentally transmit their thoughts to the bearer of the other paired seal as per the sending spell. Unlike a regular sending spell, the bearer of a paired seal can transmit up to 250 words (or a single page of images) per round and the range of this sending is 5 miles per caster level (it cannot cross planar boundaries). A user cannot have more than one ongoing instance of paired seals of private communication active on them.

Creatures under the effects of paired seals of private communication on them suffer a -2 penalty to Perception checks due to the mental strain imposed by the spell.
spell-passing-glance: When you cast this spell you seem slightly hazy and nondescript to enemies. Whenever you would be the target of an attack the originating creature must attempt a Will Save, failure means they overlook you as an option and must choose another target in range. If there is no other valid target in the attacker's range, this spell has no effect on the attacker.
spell-perpetual-dawn: This spell functions as continual flame, except that it is equivalent to the brightness created by the daylight spell.
spell-phantasmal-assailants:
You create a phantasmal image of nightmarish creatures surrounding the target. Only the spell's target can see the phantasmal assailants. You see shadowy shapes, while others see nothing. The target first gets a Will save to recognize the image as unreal, at which point, on a success the spell fails. If the target fails their saving throw, the phantasms strike, dealing 8 points of Wisdom and Dexterity damage. A successful Fortitude save at this point halves the ability damage.

If the target of the phantasmal assailants succeeds in disbelieving and possesses telepathy or is wearing a helm of telepathy, the spell can be turned upon you.

You must then disbelieve it or become subject to its effects.
spell-phantasmal-combat:
You create phantasmal sensations of a pitched battle in the area. Any who enter the area must make a Will save or be affected by the phantasm). You and any creatures that succeeded on their Will saves see shadowy shapes, all other creatures do not see anything.

Creatures that failed their Will saves move cautiously and try to avoid the dangers of the battle. They cannot make attacks of opportunity and are considered flanked by any creature attacking them. If the creature leaves the area, they are no longer affected and do not perceive the battle. If they re-enter the area, they are allowed another Will save to disbelieve the phantasm).

When casting the spell, you can designate a number of allies that are immune to the spell and can see its shadowy presence equal to your caster level.
spell-phantasmal-decoy:
You create a phantasmal image of the target's most hated enemy or favored prey. Only the spell's target can see the phantasmal decoy. You see a shadowy shape, while others see nothing. On a failed Will save, the target will chase after and primarily target the phantasmal decoy. Creatures with an Int of 3 or less will automatically chase after it, while more intelligent creatures will avoid taking foolish or dangerous actions, like provoking attacks of opportunity, to do so.

As a move action, you can move the phantasmal decoy up to 60 feet in any direction within the range of the spell. Because it is a phantasm), the phantasmal decoy is not subject to difficult terrain, though you can choose to make it seem as though it is affected to keep up the facade. The target of the spell gets another Will save to disbelieve the phantasmal decoy if it successfully attacks or moves adjacent to the phantasm).
spell-phantasmal-resonance: You create a painful, phantasmal ringing in the target's ears. They take a -10 penalty to Perception checks related to hearing and take 2d6 sonic damage at the beginning of each of their turns. A successful Will save reduces the duration to 1 round.
spell-phantasmal-strangler:
You create a phantasmal image of a nightmarish creature. Only the spell's target can see the phantasmal strangler. You see a shadowy shape, while others see nothing. The target first gets a Will save to recognize the image as unreal, at which point, on a success the spell fails. On a failure, the target is strangled by the phantasmal creature and is treated as if grappled for the duration of the spell.

Each round on your turn, the phantasmal strangler deals 2d6 points of damage to the target. If the target is reduced to -1 or fewer hit points by this damage, the spell ends.

Each round, on their turn, the target can attempt any actions a creature that is part of a grapple could do.

Treat the phantom strangler's CMB and CMD as equal to the target for this purpose. The phantasmal strangler cannot be damaged, or pinned. If the target escapes the grapple, the spell ends.
spell-phantasmal-success:
The next time the subject attempts an action that requires a die roll to determine success, they must make a Will save or the action fails. However, the subject sees a phantasmal image of their success. The subject then acts as though they succeeded for 1 round, over which time the subject realizes they were fooled. They must then make another Will save or take a -4 penalty on attack rolls, saves, ability checks and skill checks for 1d6+1 rounds thereafter.

If you are using the hope and despair rules from Good Hope – Crushing Despair by Orphaned Bookworm Productions, phantasmal success gains the despair descriptor and the subject is hopeless for 1d4 rounds, then despairing for 1 round and doubting for 1 round after that. These conditions are instead of the listed penalties.
spell-phantasmal-terrain:
You create a phantasm) of terrain that shifts and moves that confuses the target as they move. Each round when the target moves, they must make a Will save or confuse the landmarks by which they are navigating. Instead of moving in the direction they intend, they move 90 degrees in either direction, with an equal chance of left or right. The target does not realize they are headed in the wrong direction until it reaches a point where they would interact with something, or would be shifting direction. For the remainder of the round they may move as normal if they have movement remaining.

This spell also interrupts ranged attacks, the first ranged attack made in a round, the target must make a Will save or automatically miss. Any ranged attacks made for the rest of the round are made as normal.
spell-phantom-air: You create the phantasmal sensation that the creature is suffocating. The target must make a Will save or hold their breath and be staggered. At the end of their turn, the target can make a Will save to end the effect.
spell-phosphorescent-blight: This spell functions as faerie fire except that if an illuminated creature passes within 5 feet of a non-illuminated creature, they are also affected by the faerie fire effect for the spell's remaining duration.
spell-piercing-sound:
Each round, you can target a single living creature, striking it with a piercing sound. Depending on the target's HD, this attack has as many as three effects.

The effects are cumulative and concurrent.

You must spend a swift action each round after the first to target a foe.
spell-plague-mouth: You turn into a plague-bearing monster. You gain a 1d6 bite attack that can be used as a primary natural attack or as a secondary with other attacks. On a successful hit with the bite, the target must make a Fortitude save or be inflicted with bubonic plague. Alternatively, if you are currently afflicted, or carrying, a disease, you may instead transmit that disease using this spell's Fortitude save DC in place of the disease's DC.
spell-plasma-storm:
Plasma swarm is a very powerful and spectacular spell that is similar to fireball in many aspects. When you cast it, four 2-foot-diameter spheres spring from your outstretched hand and streak in straight lines to the spots you select. The plasma spheres leave a trail of electric sparks.

If you aim a sphere at a specific creature, you may make a ranged touch attack to strike the target with the plasma ball. Any creature struck by a sphere takes 2d6 points of electricity damage (no save) and takes a -4 penalty on the saving throw against the sphere's additional electricity damage (see below). If a targeted sphere misses its target, it simply explodes at the nearest corner of the target's space. You may aim more than one sphere at the same target.

Once a sphere reaches its destination, it explodes in a 40-foot-radius spread, dealing 6d6 points of electricity damage to each creature in the area. If a creature is within the area of more than one sphere, it must save separately against each. Despite stemming from separate spheres, all of the electricity damage is added together after the saves have been made, and electricity resistance is applied only once.

Targets wearing metal armor take a -4 penalty on their saving throws.
spell-power-through-decay: You sacrifice your own physical heath for more mental and magical power. You gain a +6 bonus to your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma. For the duration however, you take 1 damage to your Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution each round at the beginning of your turn. You cannot cast this spell if your are immune to ability damage.
spell-power-word-deafen:
You utter a single word of power that causes the target's hearing to ring, then is deafened. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The duration of the spell depends on the target's current hit point total.

Any creature that currently has 101 or more hit points is unaffected by power word deafen.
spell-power-word-disable: You utter a single word of power that brings a wavering creature to the brink of defeat. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The target of the spell is instantly reduced to 0 hit points. Any creature with 51 or more hit points is unaffected by power word disable.
spell-power-word-distract: You utter a single word of power that instantly causes the target to become briefly distracted. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The creature is treated as flat-footed until its next turn. Any creature that currently has 151 or more hit points is unaffected by power word distract.
spell-power-word-fatigue: You utter a single word of power that causes the target to become fatigued. A fatigued creature becomes exhausted, then reverts to fatigued when the spell ends, or the original fatigued condition ends. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The duration of the spell depends on the target's current hit point total. Any creature that currently has 101 or more hit points is unaffected by power word fatigue.
