spell-power-word-frighten: You utter a single word of power that causes the target to become frightened. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The duration of the spell depends on the target's current hit point total. Any creature that currently has 151 or more hit points is unaffected by power word frighten.
spell-power-word-graceless: You utter a single word of power that causes the target to become uncoordinated and graceless, taking 2 Dexterity damage. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The duration of the spell depends on the target's current hit point total. Any creature that currently has 76 or more hit points is unaffected by power word graceless.
spell-power-word-infirm: You utter a single word of power that causes the target to become sickly and weak, taking 2 Constitution damage. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The duration of the spell depends on the target's current hit point total. Any creature that currently has 76 or more hit points is unaffected by power word infirm.
spell-power-word-nauseate: You utter a single word of power that causes the target to become nauseated. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The duration of the spell depends on the target's current hit point total. Any creature that currently has 151 or more hit points is unaffected by power word nauseate.
spell-power-word-pain: You utter a single word of power that wracks the target with pain dealing 1d6 points of damage each round at the beginning of their turn. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The duration of the spell depends on the target's current hit point total. Any creature that currently has 101 or more hit points is unaffected by power word pain.
spell-power-word-petrify: You utter a single word of power that causes the target to instantly turn to stone, permanently becoming petrified. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. Any creature that currently has 101 or more hit points is unaffected by power word petrify.
spell-power-word-scare: You utter a single word of power that causes the target to become shaken. A shaken creature becomes frightened, then reverts to shaken when the spell ends, or the original shaken condition ends. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The duration of the spell depends on the target's current hit point total. Any creature that currently has 101 or more hit points is unaffected by power word scare.
spell-power-word-sicken: You utter a single word of power that causes the target to become sickened. A sickened creature becomes nauseated, then reverts to sickened when the spell ends, or the original sickened condition ends. The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The duration of the spell depends on the target's current hit point total. Any creature that currently has 101 or more hit points is unaffected by power word sicken.
spell-power-word-weaken:
You utter a single word of power that causes the target to become feeble and listless, taking 2 Strength damage.

The target does not need to hear or understand the word. The duration of the spell depends on the target's current hit point total. Any creature that currently has 76 or more hit points is unaffected by power word weaken.
spell-primordial-rage: This spell functions as rage except if the target does not have natural attacks, they gain a 1d6 bite attack in addition to the normal benefits of the rage. If the target has natural attacks, their damage dice are increased by 1 step while the spell is active in addition to the rage benefits.
spell-prismatic-aura:
You are surrounded by an aura of scintillating colors.

This shimmering aura grants you concealment and any creature that hits you with a non-reach melee weapon or a melee natural weapon is subject to a random prismatic effect. Roll on the prismatic spray table. The aura cannot generate two effects at once, so reroll any 8s rolled. Each time an effect is expended, that color dissipates from the aura and must be re-rolled if rolled on the table on future rounds. Once all the colors have been used, the spell ends. An attacker is entitled to the applicable saves, and spell resistance applies.
spell-prismatic-deluge: You call down a brilliant, colorful blast of energy in the area. Each creature in the area is affected as though by the prismatic spray spell and are blinded for 2d4 rounds if 8 HD or fewer.
spell-prismatic-orb:
You create a head-sized orb of scintillating colors. Once per round as a free action, the orb can fire a ray of prismatic energy with a range of 50 feet. The ray has a random effect using the table from prismatic spray. To affect a target with the effect, you must succeed at a ranged spell attack using your spellcasting ability modifier instead of Dexterity. The target must then make a save depending upon which color of ray they are affected by. After a particular color has been used by the orb, it is no longer available and must be re-rolled.

Once all the colors are expended, the orb dissipates and the spell ends.

You can move the prismatic orb up to your speed as a move action, but the orb must stay within the range of the spell from you. If you move further than the spell's range from it, it becomes inactive and cannot be moved until you move closer to it again.

The orb is not tangible and as such cannot be damaged or targeted except by targeted dispel effects and disintegration which instantly destroys the prismatic orb.
spell-prismatic-sword:
You summon a shimmering blade of scintillating colors. You are automatically proficient in this blade and it is treated as a +1 ghost touch longsword. When summoned and at the start of each round roll 1d8 to select one of the effects listed on the table below to the sword until the beginning of the next round.

Additionally, the sword's enhancement bonus increases by 1 for every 5 caster levels you possess to a maximum of +5.

Any creature struck by the sword must succeed at a will saving throw or be dazed for one round. Once a creature succeeds at this saving throw it is immune to the dazing for 24 hours or until a critical hit is confirmed against them using the prismatic sword.

* Chosen by wielder when result is rolled.

spell-programmed-amnesia:
You pry open the target's mind and memories, selectively destroying, adding, or modifying memories at your whim. If the target fails their saving throw, you have access to the target's memories and thoughts for 1 hour, you can record that information if you like, but you can also implement one or all of the following:

This spell, if not crafted perfectly, can leave contradictions or situations where the subject is confronted with the falsity of their implanted memories. For example, if the subject is implanted with a memory of being friends with a high profile noble and the noble dismisses them in turn as an unknown peasant. If faced with this new information, the subject may seek an explanation and possibly a magical fix to this gap in their memory that could negate the spell's effect.

The programmed amnesia cannot be dispelled and is permanent until a specified trigger or timed delay expires, if applicable, or the effects are removed by greater restoration, miracle, or wish.
spell-proper-retort: You shout a magically enhanced, vicious insult at an attacking creature. When you are damaged by a weapon or natural attack from a creature you can see, you may cast this spell as an immediate action. You reduce the damage taken by your caster level to a minimum of no damage. If the damage from the attack is entirely prevented the attacker takes 1d4 force damage for every 2 caster levels you possess, a successful Reflex save negates this damage.
spell-protection-from-arrows-greater:
This spell functions like protection from arrows except as noted above. Additionally, if damage from a ranged attack is completely negated by the damage reduction gained from this spell the projectile is sent flying back towards the attacker.

You make a ranged attack roll using your caster level in place of your base attack bonus and using the highest of your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifiers in place of your Dexterity modifier. If the attack hits it deals damage as appropriate for a weapon of its type plus an amount of damage equal to the ability score modifier you used on the attack roll.
spell-psychosilencer: This spell functions as psychosilencer, except as noted above.
spell-quick-march: All the affected allies gain a 30-foot enhancement bonus to their base speed.
spell-rainbow:
You create a longbow and a quiver of arrows in all the hues of the rainbow. The rainbow is treated as a +1 longbow and you gain proficiency with it, regardless of having the requisite feat. The quiver has an unending supply of arrows of various colors. Depending upon which arrow is drawn from the quiver it adds an extra effect to the attack from the longbow as follows: Red: The attack is considered adamantine and bane against outsider (elemental) creatures.

The bow only works for you and if dropped or given to another appears back on your person. However you may stow the bow to use other weapons or cast spells.

The bow and arrows have no weight and cannot be sundered or destroyed, but can be dispelled if any part is subject to a dispel effect. At the end of the spell's duration, the bow and arrows disappear.
spell-raining-blood:
You create a downpour of blood in the area that deals 1d6 points of negative energy damage per caster level (maximum 15d6) to every living creature in the area.

Any corporeal undead or creature with the blood drain ability in the area is healed by 4d6. A successful Fortitude save halves the damage. For the remaining duration, the area is filled with the smell of putrid offal.

Any living creature entering or beginning their turn in the area must also make a Fortitude save or be sickened until the beginning of their next turn.
spell-ravenwight:
You fill a target creature with dread, fearful that death is around every corner, and haunted by the image of menacing spectral raven. The target must make a Will save or become haunted by the vision of a large shadowy raven, gripping them with fear during their waking hours and denying them restful sleep. If they succeed at this initial Will save they are shaken for 1 round per caster level. Upon failing the initial Will save and at the beginning of each hour the target sees a vision of the raven nearby (somewhere visible within 30 ft. in a random direction). They must make an additional Will save or be shaken and unable to move in the direction of the spectral creature, for the remainder of the hour. They can circumvent the raven by walking around it in a wide arc, but they can get no closer than the distance at which it first appeared.

If they fail this save by 5 or more instead they are frightened for 5 rounds. Success means they may approach but if they end their turn adjacent to the ravenwight they take 3d6 damage as their life force is disrupted by negative energy. The creature must also make a Will save when it wakes each morning, failure means it is fatigued and does not gain the benefits of 8 hours of rest. The caster use a move action to cause the ravenwight to appear in a square of your choice within 30 ft. of the target. The spectral raven is insubstantial and can't be hurt.
spell-ray-of-bedevilment:
You shoot a ray of chaotic light and energy at a target that clouds the mind of the target with peals of insane laughter. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack against the target to affect them. If affected, the target then must make a Will save or be dazed for 1d3 rounds.

On a successful save, the target is dazzled for 1 round.
spell-ray-of-bedevilment-greater: This spell functions as ray of bedevilment except it allows you to shoot one ray per round. The dazed duration remains 1d3 rounds and the target that makes their save is still dazzled for 1 round. If you hit the same target, the duration of the effects do not stack, instead the condition is replaced by the condition with the longer duration or greater effect if both are 1 round.
spell-ray-of-rupturing:
You fire a beam of necrotic energy into a target causing their internal organs to burst one at a time.

When the ray strikes a target they take 3d6 damage and are nauseated for one round. Then, at the beginning of each of your turns the creature takes 3d6 damage and becomes nauseated for another round. A Fortitude save halves the damage and reduces the nauseated condition to sickened. If a creature makes two successive saves against this spell it ends.
spell-ray-of-sorrow: You shoot a ray of dark energy causing the target to be filled with doubt and sadness. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack against the target to affect them. If you hit, the target takes a -3 penalty on saving throws, attack rolls, ability checks and skill checks.
spell-ray-of-sunlight: You release a bright beam of light. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack with the ray to deal damage to a target. The target is blinded for 1 round and takes 2d6 points of damage. A successful Reflex save negates the blinding. Creatures harmed by sunlight and undead take 4d6 damage. Undead that are particularly adverse to sunlight, like vampires, take 6d6 damage.
spell-red-in-tooth-and-claw: This spell functions as red in tooth and claw except it affects multiple creatures.
spell-reign-in-hell:
You don the crown and it begins to glow with a hellish light. For the duration you gain a +4 deflection bonus to AC and a +4 resistance bonus to saving throws against attacks or spells from evil outsiders.

While under the effects of this spell you are immune to any charm or compulsion effects from evil outsiders.

Any such effects that are active on you prior to the casting of this spell are suppressed while this spell is active.

Finally, while the spell is active, all evil outsiders start with a disposition of indifferent toward you and you gain a bonus to Charisma-based skills and ability checks against evil outsiders equal to 1/2 your class level.
spell-release-the-clowder:
This spell summons a clowder of cats that respond to the spellcaster's commands and act in perfect unison, causing them to function like a swarm. The pack uses the statistics for a dire lion, except it gains the swarm subtype, a swarm attack that deals 4d6 points of damage, and the distraction special attack (DC 17).

The pack does not gain any damage reduction or immunity to damage and can be attacked by effects that target a specific number of creatures, though such attacks deal 1/4 the normal amount of damage (25%) and effects that don't deal hit point damage are only 25% likely to work.
spell-repeating-fireball:
This spell functions as the spell fireball except each round at the beginning of your turn after the initial explosion, the fireball explodes again in the same area.

Each explosion thereafter deals 2d6 less fire damage than the previous round. Each explosion has their own Reflex save to halve the damage.
spell-resounding-runes:
This spell functions as explosive runes, except it creates a small burst of sound rather than an explosion of force.

The runes automatically deal 1d4 points of sonic damage to any creatures and objects in adjacent squares, and those creatures are deafened for 1d6 rounds unless they succeed at Fortitude saves.
spell-resounding-voice:
The touched target's voice becomes magically enhanced. It is able to be heard clearly up to 100 feet away per caster level. This does not bypass areas of silence or deafness.

This spell counters and dispels silence on the target and is countered and dispelled by silence.
spell-robe-of-words: This spell functions as robe of words, except it automatically defends against qualifying spells of 5th level or lower and can attempt to counterspell spells from 6th to 9th level.
spell-rotting-curse: The vile curse causes the subject's flesh and bones to rot. On a failed saving throw, the subject takes 1d6 points of Constitution damage immediately, and a further 1d6 points of Constitution damage every hour until the subject dies or the curse is removed with a break enchantment, wish, miracle, or remove curse spell or any other spell capable of removing curses. The subsequent Con damage can be reduced to 1 by a successful Fortitude save. If the target succeeds on their initial saving throw they take 1 Con damage and the curse is thwarted.
spell-sabotage: This spell functions as dispel magic except it can only be a targeted dispel. Additionally, the target of the dispel takes damage equal to the caster level of the spell Dispelled. If the target is a summoned creature or a construct, instead of the dispel effect, they instead take 1d8 damage per caster level of the spell used to summon them. Constructs cannot be immune to this spell.
spell-saltspray: You fire a stream of saltwater at the target. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack to hit your target. The stream deals 1d3 points of damage. This spell deals 1d6 damage to slugs, plant creatures, and creatures primarily made of acid or weak to salt.
spell-scent-of-evil:
You gain a supernatural ability to scent evil. This spell grants the scent special ability but only to detect evil creatures. Any ability or spell that hides a creature's alignment like undetectable alignment thwarts this scent ability. Additionally, you gain a bonus to Perception and Survival checks using this scent ability depending on the strength of the creature's evil aura power. Refer to the spell detect evil. You gain a +2 competence bonus on the skill check for each aura power level over 'none'.

For example, you would gain a +4 competence bonus to your Perception and Survival checks against a 3rd-level evil cleric.
spell-sealing-glyph:
You recite a spell of protection and transfer the lock in your hand onto the object to be worded, leaving behind a quickly fading sigil. An object warded by this spell cannot be opened by any means other than by breaking the object, or using magic such as knock or dispel magic. When forced open the glyph explodes in a resounding blast dealing 1d4 force damage per caster level in a 10 ft. radius. A knock spell suppresses, but does not remove the glyph, for 10 minutes.

The DC for a knock spell is 11 + the caster level of the glyph's creator.

A sealing glyph can be bypassed as a magical trap with a disable device check DC 11 + the caster level of the glyph's creator.
spell-shadow-landscape:
You blend the landscape of the area with the same area on the shadow plane, making the terrain and features more dangerous. The spell effects depend upon the affected terrain as follows:

Finally, you can designate a number of animals, plants, or magical beasts native to the area normally as shadowy protectors. You can designate 1 HD/level, split up in any grouping you wish. For example, a 19th-level sorcerer could designate a giant flytrap (13 HD) and 3 wolves (2 HD) as shadowy guardians. As long as the creatures remain within the spell's area, they have a friendly disposition toward you and the creatures marked when casting the spell, and they gain the shadow creature template.
spell-shadow-spike-strike: You create a vile flurry of shadowy spikes, which blast from your hand in a line. The line deals 1d6 negative energy damage per caster level (maximum 15d6).
spell-shadowchains: A creature targeted by this spell is held immobile by dark chains composed of pure shadow. The creature is paralyzed and held in place, but may attempt a new saving throw each round to end the effect. While held by the shadowy chains, a creature cannot use any sort of extradimensional travel, such as astral projection, blink, dimension door, ethereal jaunt, etherealness, gate, maze, plane shift, shadow walk, teleport, and similar spells and spell-like abilities. The spell does not affect creatures that are already in ethereal or astral form when the spell is cast.
spell-shadowclaws: You grow wicked claws made from dark wisps of shadow by drawing in nearby light. When you cast this spell you gain two primary claw attacks as natural weapons which each deal 1d6 damage plus one cold damage per caster level. Enemies struck by both claws in a single round must make a Fortitude save or become fatigued for one round. If you are grappling a creature while you have these claws they must make a save each round they remain grappled to avoid becoming fatigued. This spell cannot cause a creature to become exhausted.
spell-shadowy-form: You envelop your form in shadow, becoming one with it. You gain a +4 bonus on CMD, Escape Artist checks, and Stealth checks. You also gain concealment. These benefits are not thwarted by see invisibility, but true seeing and being in a place of bright light can negate these benefits. Additionally, you gain the compression universal monster ability.
spell-shards-of-heaven:
You call upon the raw energy of the heavens and create 1 floating shard of heavenly energy per 2 caster levels.

Each shard glows golden light with the strength of a candle.

As a swift action, you may make a ranged touch attack with one of your shards. On a hit, the shard deals 1d6 damage per 3 caster levels and the shard is expended. If the target is evil-aligned, the damage increases to 1d8s, if the target is an undead or evil outsider, the damage increases to 1d12.

If the duration expires or all of the shards have been expended, the spell ends.
spell-shared-pain: You make a small cut on your body and the same small cut appears on the target. Both you and the subject take 1 point of damage. On a failed saving throw, the subject takes a –1 penalty on attack rolls, saving throws, skill checks, and ability checks for the duration due to the annoying pain.
spell-shared-strength: You call forth to your allies to lend you power for a crushing blow. When you cast this spell allies within 20 feet of you, up to a number of creatures equal to your caster level, may choose to take a -2 penalty to Strength for one minute and grant you a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls on the next attack you make before the end of the round. After you make an attack that has been enhanced by this spell you become fatigued for one minute and cannot benefit from this spell while fatigued.
spell-sickening-reality: You place a curse on the target that forces them to seek some kind of mind-altering state. Anytime the target is not subject to an enchantment or illusion (figment) spell of 2nd level or higher or if they are not under the influence of a drug, they are sickened. If the target creature is sickened and subject to an effect that also imposes the sickened condition, they are instead nauseated.
spell-sigil-of-the-tyrant:
As part of casting this spell, you use blood drawn from a lemming to paint on your forehead the personal sigil of a mysterious summoner known only as Tyrant. For the duration of this spell, you draw in fragments of the essence of your summoned creatures to collect and form a boon you can bestow upon target creatures.

During this spell's duration, whenever one of your summoned creatures within close range of you is killed, the sigil of the Tyrant absorbs a fragment of the summoning magic, generating 1 rune fragment. Each time the sigil of the Tyrant has collected 4 rune fragments, the 4 rune fragments fuse to form 1 tyrannical runemark (which is then stored into the sigil). For the purposes of this spell, only your summoned creatures from spells you have personally cast counts towards generating a rune fragment (summoned creatures via spell-like abilities, supernatural abilities, class features, magic items, and other sources do not count).

As a swift action, you can bestow 1 tyrannical runemark upon a target creature within close range. A tyrannical runemark confers the target creature a +1 dodge bonus to AC and a +1 luck bonus to attack and damage rolls with melee weapons (including thrown melee weapons, unarmed strike, and natural attacks).

The benefits of a tyrannical runemark, once bestowed upon a target creature, lasts for a number of rounds equal to 1 round/5 caster levels you possess. A creature can only gain the benefit of up to 5 tyrannical runemarks. You can only designate 1 target creature for any given tyrannical runemark.

Alternatively, you may spend a full-round action to bestow all of the tyrannical runemarks your sigil of the Tyrant currently holds upon target creatures within close range.
spell-silver-arc:
You create an arcing beam of moonlight between two targets. This moonlight deals 1d6 points of cold damage per caster level (maximum 15d6) to both targets and any creatures in the line connecting them.

Additionally, all affected creatures are affected by the effects of moonlight if they have abilities or conditions triggered by moonlight. Any creature that has their DR assed by silver instead takes 1d8 per caster level (maximum 15d8) points of untyped damage. A successful Fortitude save halves the damage.
spell-singularity: This spell functions as lift against all creatures that are within the area of the burst. However, at the center of the area is a dark sphere which pulls all affected creatures to the center of the area, as much as possible. Any creature that enters the area must make a save or be affected.
spell-siphon-resistance: This spell functions as overload except you gain the benefits of the suppressed protections for the duration.
spell-sleep-arrow: An arrow, glowing like a star at night, springs from your hand and speeds to its target. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack to affect the target. If hit, the target must make a Will save or fall asleep as per the sleep spell for 1 minute/level, with no HD limit. On a successful saving throw, the target is fatigued for 1 minute.
spell-snakepit: This spell functions as create pit, except that the bottom of the pit is filled with a mass of writhing snakes and the maximum depth is 50 feet. Creatures that fall in take damage as normal and there is a venomous snake swarm that takes up the entire bottom. The snake swarm will not attempt to crawl out of the pit but will attack any creature at the bottom of the pit or within 5 feet of the bottom. If the snake swarm is destroyed another swarm forms at the beginning of your next turn.
spell-sniper-shot: A quick word of luck and a sharp breath ensures a sure shot. The next ranged attack roll you make can add precision damage regardless of distance and gains a bonus on critical confirmation rolls equal to your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (whichever is higher).
spell-somniloquy:
You grant a form of consciousness to an unconscious creature, allowing it to answer questions. You may ask one question per two caster levels. The creature's knowledge is limited to what it could possibly know or understand while awake, including the languages it spoke. Answers are brief, cryptic, tinged with dream oddities, or repetitive, especially if the creature would have opposed you in life.

If the creature would be unwilling while conscious, they may make a Will save. If successful, the creature can refuse to answer your questions or attempt to deceive you, using Bluff.
spell-song-of-the-dead: You begin a mystical necromantic song that causes all undead to freeze in their place and listen. Roll 2d4 and add your caster level (maximum 10) to determine the total number of HD of undead affected. Creatures closest to you and with the fewest HD are affected first. HD that are no sufficient to affect a creature are wasted. Mindless undead do not get a saving throw to resist the effects, but intelligent undead do. All affected undead become fascinated by the song intoned. This spell affects incorporeal undead, but those incapable of hearing the son are not affected. If the target is attacked, they get a saving throw to resist the spell's effects, with the exception of mindless undead.
spell-sonic-wave-of-bees: You extend your hand and unleash a swarm of sonically infused bees. The bees use the statistics of a wasp swarm but they deal 1d6 additional sonic damage. The swarm begins adjacent to you, but if no living creature is within its area, it moves in one direction of your choosing at normal speed. You can move the swarm or change its direction by spending a standard action to concentrate on the swarm, otherwise it continues moving in its current direction.
spell-sonorous-steel: You hum in tune with the din of battle and impart that essence into your weapon. When you cast this spell you choose one weapon you are holding, it deals an additional 1d8 sonic damage on a successful attack until the end of the round. In addition, when a creature takes sonic damage from the weapon they must make a fortitude saving throw or be deafened for 1d6 rounds and stunned for one round. With a successful saving throw the creature instead suffers a 10 foot penalty to movement speed as its equilibrium is impacted. Against a creature that relies on hearing to see, such as a creature with echolocation and some creatures with blindsense or blindsight, increase the sonic damage to 2d8.
spell-sorrowful-void:
This spell functions as call the void, except in addition to the spell's normal effect, a creature that takes damage must also roll a Will save or take a -2 penalty on attack rolls, saving throws, ability checks, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls for 1 minute per caster level.

Once a target has had to roll a Will save against this spell, they are immune to the Will save portion of the spell for the remaining duration. The Will-save portion of the spell is an emotion, mind-affecting effect.
spell-soul-trap:
With a wave of your hand you attempt to bind a creature's soul to a gem or crystal. The target's soul is tied to the material component crystal or gem. If the target should die during the duration of the spell, their soul is pulled and absorbed into the crystal creating a soul stone. Such a creature cannot be raised from the dead except for by the spell wish. For uses and stats of these soul stones, see the sidebar to the right. The soul is bound to the crystal permanently until used, dispelled or destroyed.

If the creature is killed by a spell or effect that obliterates the soul, their soul is not trapped within the soul stone and the spell fails.

If the creature does not have a soul, like most constructs, automatons or mindless undead, this spell has no effect. Additionally, this spell has no effect on summoned creatures as their souls are already tethered to their original plane by the summoning magic.
spell-soulmending: This spell functions as soulmending except it also removes permanent effects, and it restores 2d4 Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma damage. Instead of healing ability score damage, this spell can also remove drain at the cost of 3 ability damage healing per 1 drain healing. The healing result may be divided up between the three ability scores. If using sanity rules, this spell can remove a lesser madness and heal 5 sanity damage/level.
spell-sound-of-broken-bells: You ring the broken bell and the affected area is filled with a painful clangor of bells. Each creature in the area is dealt 1d4 sonic damage per caster level (maximum 10d4) and the target is deafened for 2d6 rounds. A successful Fortitude save negates the deafness and halves the sonic damage.
spell-space-walk:
When casting this spell, your spatial awareness momentarily expands outwards to encompass all observable spaces within the fixed range listed for this spell, enabling you to briefly synchronize with the space-time of such spaces and establish coordinates for the ensuing teleportation.

When you successfully cast this spell, you immediately teleport to any unoccupied and observable space (line of sight) within the fixed range that can support your weight and space. To all other observers, you took a step forward (or similar action) in the direction of your teleportation's destination and suddenly reappeared in your new location.

If you cast this spell as a swift action, you suffer no adverse effects from the sudden teleportation. If you cast this spell as an immediate action (usually to avoid being targeted or attacked), you are sickened immediately after the teleportation is completed and until the end of your next turn.

Casting this spell does not provoke an attack of opportunity normally, whether you cast it as a swift or immediate action. You cannot successfully cast this spell if you are held, grappled, or otherwise prevented from being able to move forward normally under your natural means of locomotion (such as walking for creatures with legs, slithering for creatures with only a tail, like snakes, or even swimming, if underwater) into the direction of your teleportation's destination.
spell-sparking-arc: You spray bolts of electricity from your fingertips at your foe. While the spell is a 30-foot line, only the closest target to you is affected in each round. The affected target must make a Reflex save or be dealt 1d6 + 1 per caster level (max +5) electricity damage. You may elect to exclude the square adjacent to them from the area of effect if you so choose. Any creature wearing metal armor, wielding a metal weapon or is made of metal has a -3 penalty on their saving throw. If such a metal-exposed creature fails their Reflex save against this spell two rounds in a row, the damage that on any round they fail is multiplied by 1.5, once the target succeeds on the Reflex saving throw, the bonus damage ends. Each round while concentrating on the spell, you may redirect the line of effect.
spell-storm-of-arrows: With a primal word of strength you channel the might the might of the storm into your bow. After casting this spell you may use a full round action to make a single attack at your highest base attack bonus against each enemy within the first range increment of your bow.
spell-stow-in-darkness:
With a whisper and flick of the rist you open a small portal to the plane of shadow.

You can store an item inside this pocket of shadow for an indefinite period of time.

For the next 24 hours after casting this spell you can retrieve the item as a swift action. Otherwise the next time you cast this spell you cause the stored item to appear in an unoccupied square adjacent to you.
spell-strung-up-from-the-sky: This spell functions like strung up from the sky, except it affects multiple creatures.
spell-stunning-mist: Stunning mist creates a bank of fog like that created by fog cloud, except that the vapors resonate in a way that stuns those within. Living creatures in the cloud become stunned. This condition lasts as long as the creature is in the cloud and for 1d4+1 rounds after it leaves. (Roll separately for each stunned character.) A creature gets a new save at the beginning of each of their turns to become un-stunned. Any creature that succeeds on its save but remains in the cloud must continue to save each round on your turn. Stunning mist can be made permanent with a permanency spell. A permanent stunning mist dispersed by wind reforms in 10 minutes.
spell-submission-web: This spell functions as web, except all creatures within the web takes 1d6 electricity damage at the beginning of their turn. A successful Reflex save halves this damage. On a failed Reflex save, the affected creature must make a Fortitude save or be stunned for 1 round.
spell-sudden-etherealness: You speak a quiet word and you become ethereal for the duration of the spell. If at the end of the spell's duration, you re-materialize within a solid object or in an occupied space, you are shunted off to the nearest open space, taking 1d6 points of damage per 5 feet traveled.
spell-sudden-flight: You speak a forceful word of grace and speed and take flight. You gain a fly speed equal to your base land speed, with a good maneuverability, for one round plus one round per three caster levels you possess.
spell-sudden-mirroring: This spell functions as mirror image except as detailed above.
spell-sudden-speed:
With a practiced motion you complete this spell and gain a burst of speed that briefly aids you in combat.

You gain a 10 foot increase to your base movement speed as well as a +1 bonus to armor class and reflex saves for one round plus one round per three caster levels you possess.
spell-summon-clockwork-warriors: You speak a word of animation as the gear and spring call forth a strike-force of clockwork warriors. When you cast this spell you summon 2d4+2 clockwork soldiers that attack your foes. As a move action each round you may designate an enemy and all clockwork soldiers will use their actions to move towards or attack that enemy until given another command. If not given any orders, the soldiers will each target the nearest enemy to themselves.
spell-summon-heroic-spirits:
Dual School Spells: While extremely rare (and heavily restricted in most such cases), some spells are considered dual-school, meaning that they possess magical energies stemming from two separate schools of magic. For all intended purposes, other than described here, a dual-school spell always counts as being both schools of magic. If you are unable, for any reason, to access any of the two schools of that spell, that spell remains inaccessible to you. A dual-school spell can only benefit once from any effect that would normally apply to either, or both, schools, such as Spell Focus or a metamagic feat. If applying a metamagic feat (or similar effect) to a dualschool spell, both of its schools must be eligible for applying the metamagic feat to be successful.

This spell functions like summon monster IX, except it allows you to summon a single manu; its creature bond is always the same as your ancestry), an amarok with the resolute template, or 1d3 couatls.

If you are attempting to summon the couatls, you must have a focus (as described above) on hand for each of the three coualts, even if you only summoned one or two couatls.

If you cast this spell to summon a manu, it is also a spell with the good descriptor.
spell-sunbeam-lethargy: This spell functions as the spell sunbeam except each time a creature is dealt damage by a beam, they are fatigued. A second time, they are exhausted. The condition cannot be raised past exhausted. If the target is immune to fatigue, they are instead staggered for 1 round if they take damage from the beam. The staggered effect does not stack from multiple hits.
spell-symbol-of-idiocy:
This spell functions like symbol of death, except that every creature within 60 feet of a symbol of idiocy instead suffers crippling mental weakness that deals 3d6 points of Intelligence damage.

Unlike symbol of death, symbol of idiocy has no hit point limit; once triggered, a symbol of idiocy simply remains active for 10 minutes per caster level. A creature can only be affected by this symbol once.
spell-tag-team-tactics: With a word you become perfectly in sync with your comrade in arms. After you cast this spell, whenever you make an attack roll, the creature you targeted with this spell gains a +2 bonus to damage rolls against the target of your attack until the beginning of your next turn. If the targeted creature makes an attack roll, you gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls against the target of their attack until the beginning of their next turn.
spell-telekinetic-attacks: You instill the touched weapon with extra kinetic power. The weapon deals 2 additional damage of the same type the weapon normally deals. This additional damage increases by 1 for every six levels you possess (maximum 5 damage at 18th level). A ranged weapon affected by this spell applies these effects to its ammunition. This spell cannot be cast on a natural weapon.
spell-telekinetic-attacks-mass: This spell functions as telekinetic attacks except it affects multiple weapons.
spell-telekinetic-charge-greater: This spell functions as telekinetic charge except at the end of the charge, if the attack hits, all creatures, aside from yourself, within 10 feet of the target must make a Reflex save or take half the damage dealt to the initial target.
spell-telekinetic-lance: You must succeed on a ranged touch attack to affect the target with the telekinetic lance. If the attack hits, you deal 1d6 damage per level (maximum 10d6). The damage is considered magical piercing damage. Additionally, the target must make a Fortitude save or be launched back 5 feet per 4 caster levels you possess. After striking or missing its target, the telekinetic lance disappears.
spell-telekinetic-slam: You telekinetically lift the target and quickly slam them into the ground. The target takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage per caster level (maximum 10d6). A Fortitude save halves this damage.
spell-telekinetic-slam-greater: This spell functions as telekinetic slam except the bludgeoning damage dealt is considered magic for damage reduction purposes and the damage is 1d8 per caster level (maximum 15d8).
spell-telekinetic-slam-mass: This spell functions as telekinetic slam except it affects multiple creatures and the maximum is 15d6.
spell-telekinetic-slam-mass-greater: This spell functions as greater telekinetic slam except it affects multiple creatures and the maximum is 20d8.
spell-telepathy-block:
The area centered on the designated point in space, object, or creature blocks all telepathic communication. If the spell is cast upon an object or creature, the center point of the emanation moves.

Otherwise it is stationary.
spell-terror-storm:
You create an evil-looking black storm cloud in the air. Each creature under the cloud must succeed on a Will save or be shaken for 1d4 x 10 minutes.

Each round you continue to concentrate, the spell generates additional effects as noted below.

Each effect occurs on your turn.

2nd Round: Negative energy floods the area, dealing 1d6 points of negative energy damage to living creatures (no save), undead are not healed by this negative energy.

3rd Round: You call six bolts of lightning down from the cloud. You decide where the bolts strike. No two bolts may be directed at the same target. Each bolt deals 10d6 points of electricity damage. A creature struck can attempt a Reflex save for half damage.

4th Round: Hailstones rain down in the area, dealing 5d6 points of bludgeoning damage (no save).

5th through 10th Rounds: All living creatures take 1d6 negative energy damage (no save) and must make a Will save or be panicked for 1 round.

Positive energy spells deal half the amount of damage or heal half the amount of wounds in the area.
spell-tethers:
This spell causes a multitude of ropes burst forth from the ground and wrap up any creature in the area.

Every creature within the area of the spell is the target of a combat maneuver check made to grapple each round at the beginning of your turn, including the round that tethers is cast. Creatures that enter the area of effect are also automatically attacked. The ropes do not provoke attacks of opportunity. When determining the ropes' CMB, they use your caster level as their base attack bonus and add your spellcasting ability modifier. Roll only once for the entire spell effect each round and apply the result to all creatures in the area of effect.

The ropes do not deal damage to creatures they have grappled, but they will attempt to pin any creature currently grappled. The CMD of the tethers, for the purposes of escaping the grapple, is equal to 10 + its CMB.

The ropes created by this spell cannot be damaged as they are instantly replaced by more ropes, but they can be dispelled as normal. The entire area of effect is considered difficult terrain while the spell lasts.
spell-thunderball:
A thunderball spell generates a thunderous explosion of sound that detonates and deals 1d4 points of sonic damage per caster level (maximum 10d4) to every creature within the area. Unattended objects also take this damage. The explosion creates almost no pressure.

You point your finger and determine the range (distance and height) at which the thunderball is to burst. A glowing, pea-sized bead streaks from the pointing digit and, unless it impacts upon a material body or solid barrier prior to attaining the prescribed range, bursts into the thunderball at that point. An early impact results in an early detonation. If you attempt to send the bead through a narrow passage, such as through an arrow slit, you must "hit" the opening with a ranged touch attack, or else the bead strikes the barrier and detonates prematurely.

The thunderball damages objects in the area. If the damage caused to an interposing barrier shatters or breaks through it, the thunderball may continue beyond the barrier if the area permits; otherwise it stops at the barrier just as any other spell effect does.

A thunderball does not function in an area of silence. If the center of the burst is in the area, the spell fails.
spell-thunderbursts: When you cast this spell, deafening sound bursts forth from your body in all directions. The sound does not harm objects or creatures in the area you wish to exclude from damage. Any other creatures within the area take 1d8 points of sonic damage per caster level (maximum 20d8) and are stunned for 1 round. A successful save halves the damage and negates the stun effect.
spell-thunderous-trap:
Thunderous trap creates a resounding explosion when an intruder opens the item that the trap protects. A thunderous trap spell can ward any object that can be opened and closed.

When casting thunderous trap, you select a point on the object as the spell's center. When someone other than you opens the object, the resounding explosion fills the area within a 5-foot radius around the spell's center.

The sound deals 1d3 points of sonic damage + 1 point per caster level (maximum +20). The item protected by the trap is not harmed by this explosion.

A thunder-trapped item cannot have a second closure or warding spell placed on it. A knock spell does not bypass a thunderous trap. An unsuccessful dispel magic spell does not detonate the spell. This spell does not function in an area of silence.

You can use the thunder-trapped object without discharging it, as can any individual to whom the object was specifically attuned when cast. Attuning a thundertrapped object to an individual usually involves setting a password that you can share with friends.
spell-thunderous-voice:
Your voice is amplified greatly. Subtract 10 from Perception check DCs to hear you speaking or whispering, and you gain a +2 circumstance bonus on Intimidate checks.

While the spell is active you can shout as a swift action dealing 1d8 sonic damage in a 15-foot cone. Creatures that take damage must also make a Fortitude save or be stunned for 1 round. Using this action discharges the spell.

Creatures that cannot hear are not stunned but still take the sonic damage. This spell cannot pass through an area of silence.
spell-tide-of-bloodlust:
You create a terrible field of violence and bloodlust.

The area affected by this emanation looks as though it is slick with blood. Any creature entering or beginning their turn in the area must make a Will save. On a failure, they are overcome with an irresistible need to kill or destroy the nearest creature. They must use the most deadly attack they have on the nearest creature, whether it be friend or foe. If the most deadly attack is an area effect one, it must be centered on the target.

Each round on your turn, you can move the emanation in a straight line up to 20 feet.
spell-tide-of-glass:
You create a blast of tiny, dangerously-sharp shards of glass. Any creature within the cone take 1d6 magical slashing damage per caster level (maximum 10d6).

Additionally, any creature that takes damage takes 1 bleed damage on a successful saving throw and 1d4 bleed on a failed one.
spell-tides-of-oneiric-darkness: This spell functions as tides of oneiric darkness, except that its darkness is increased to the effect produced by deeper darkness and the spell effects creatures up to 8 HD.
spell-tongues-prison: This spell functions as tongue's prison except it affects multiple creatures as noted above.
spell-tooth-grinder: This spell functions as tooth grinder, except it affects multiple creatures as noted above and the damage on a failure increases to 5d6 and on a success 3d6.
spell-towering-presence: You adjust your posture and seem to suddenly overshadow all others around you. The subject gets a +10 enhancement bonus on Intimidation checks. The enhancement bonus increases to +20 at caster level 7th, and to +30 (the maximum) at caster level 13th.
spell-trackers-focus:
If you don't have the swift tracker class ability, this spell grants you that ability of a ranger.

If you have the swift tracker ability granted by class levels, however, this spell grants you a +5 competence bonus on all Survival checks made to follow tracks. While under the effects of this spell, whenever you lose a trail by rolling poorly on a Survival check, you may roll a second Survival check. This new roll uses the same modifiers as the first roll. If your second roll is high enough to avoid losing the trail, you must take an additional minute to find the trail. Each time you take advantage of this feature, the remaining duration of the spell is reduced by 1 that minute—if less than a minute's worth of duration remains, the spell ends as soon as you reroll your Survival check.
spell-trackers-gift: Your eyes grow glassy for a moment and then clear into a sharp focus. While this spell is active you may roll any Survival check made to follow a trail twice and take the better result.
spell-trampled-by-light:
You launch a beam of sunlight from your hand. Each creature in the beam is permanently blinded and takes 4d6 points of damage. Any creatures to which sunlight is harmful or unnatural take double damage. In addition, any creature in the line that fails their Reflex save is knocked prone. A successful Reflex save negates the blindness and prone, and reduces the damage by half.

Any undead in the line instead take 1d6 damage per caster level (maximum 15d6), or half as much on a successful saving throw. This is considered sunlight for such creatures destroyed by sunlight.
spell-transfix-monster: This functions as transfix person except it affects any living creature that fails its Will save.
spell-transfix-person: You cause the target to become paralyzed freeze in place. It is aware and breathes normally but cannot take any actions, even speech. You specify a condition that will end it like "Wait until my master returns.". This condition can be stated in a way that can never feasibly be met, like "Wait here until you see dawn's light" while underground. For every hour the target may make a Will save to end the spell early. A winged creature who is paralyzed cannot flap its wings and falls. A swimmer can't swim and may drown.
spell-transfixing-area: This spell functions as transfix person except it affects all humanoids within the spell's area. Additionally, any humanoid that enters the area must make a successful Will save or be affected by the spell with the same conditions.
spell-twilight-of-the-mind: You cause the area to fill with a shadowy twilight that shifts and moves confusing the observer and leaves them doubting their senses. The area becomes dim light and all creatures within the area of the spell take a -10 penalty on Perception and Sense Motive skill checks. A successful Will save negates the penalties of the spell but not the dim light effect.
spell-unassuming-guise: When you cast this spell you take on the appearance of a completely average member of whatever race is the majority of the current settlement. You gain a +10 bonus to disguise checks to impersonate a common member of this race. In addition, if someone attempts to recall information about you that creature must attempt a Will save to remember anything beyond a very simple physical description of the disguise.
spell-unnerving-gaze:
You complete the spell, and your face shifts into the form of the target's bitter enemy or departed loved one.

The target takes a -1 penalty on attack rolls and a -1 penalty on saving throws against fear effects. The target only takes the penalty while they can see you.
spell-valorous-brigade: You wave the banner high and shout words of victory as you embolden your allies towards certain victory. When you cast this spell each of the targets gains the challenge ability of a cavalier of your caster level, though with no additional bonus from an order. In addition each target gains the aura of courage ability as the paladin ability of the same name. If any of the targets is currently suffering from a fear effect it ends, if suffering from a compulsion effect, those effects immediately end unless the source has more hit dice than you. If you are slain or knocked unconscious, this spell immediately ends.
spell-vampiric-drain: You pull the life essence from the target. This can be blood leaving the body or a dark energy, it is up to the caster. The target must make a Fortitude save or be dealt 1d6 + 1 per caster level (max +5) negative energy damage. Additionally, you gain temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt. The temporary hit points granted by this spell stack each round but the total gained from this spell cannot exceed 6 + 1 per caster level (max +5). These temporary hit points disappear 1 hour later. A successful Fortitude save by the target halves the damage and negates the temporary hit point gain by you. Each round while concentrating on the spell, you may change the target of the spell.
spell-vespertine-decay: You create an aura that causes degradation to any creature lurking in the dark. At the beginning of your turn, creatures in dim light take 3d4 damage. Creatures in darkness or creatures with the shadow subtype instead take 3d6 damage. A successful Fortitude save halves this damage. You are also affected by the spell if in an area of dim light or darker.
spell-vicarious-trauma:
You create a vile connection between you and another creature that transfers some of your wounds to them.

You take a -1 penalty to AC and saving throws, but you take only half damage from all wounds and attacks that deal hit point damage. The amount of damage not taken by you is transferred to the targeted creature.

Other detrimental effects that do not cause hit point damage are not shared, including lowered total HP due to changes in their Constitution modifier.
spell-violent-dread: This spell functions as violent dread except it affects all creatures in an area as detailed above.
spell-violent-growth:
Focusing on the bit of plant matter and the intended living creature, you create a small kernel of primal energy in the target. One round after the completion of the spell, the spell deals 1d6 per caster level (maximum 20d6) physical damage as a violent plant growth bursts from the body of the target. This physical damage is considered bludgeoning, piercing and magic for the purposes of damage reduction additionally, it inflicts 1d4 bleed damage. The target that succeeds at a fortitude save takes half of the physical damage and negates the bleed damage.

Additionally the explosion of plant growth creates an entangle effect as the spell entangle in a 20 ft. radius around the target. Any living creature that stays in the entangle effect for more than 1 round has a kernel of the primal energy put into them. As with the original target, the kernel causes a violent explosion of plant growth and the cycle begins anew.

The entangle effect created by the explosion lasts for 1d4+2 rounds. Any creature that has taken damage from this spell is immune to an additional kernel from this spell but is still subject to the entangling condition above.
spell-vision-of-triumph: Crying out a single stirring word grants your ally sudden strength and resilience. When you cast this spell the targeted creature gains a bonus to its next saving throw or skill check equal to your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (whichever is highest) made before the end of the current round.
spell-vortex-of-shadow:
You create a violent whirlwind of shadowy material. It occupies the space of a huge creature and on the turn it is summoned, it can move 60 feet in a straight line. Any creature that is in the space of the whirlwind when it is summoned or anywhere along its movement must make two saving throws.

First, the target must make a Fortitude save or take 1d6 cold damage per caster level (maximum 15d6). A successful saving throw halves this damage.

Second, the target must make a Reflex save or be thrown 1d4 x 10 feet in a random direction, taking 1d6 damage per 10 feet traveled. If the save is failed by 10 or more, they are also prone. A successful Reflex save moves the creature 5 feet in a random direction and no damage is taken.
spell-wall-of-dispel-magic:
This spell creates a nearly invisible wall that does not block entry or hinder movement. The wall can be spotted with a perception check of DC 11 + your caster level. Any magical effect or summoned creature passing through the wall is subject to a targeted dispel magic as the spell using your caster level for the caster level check against each magical effect which passes through the wall. The wall can only be seen with the aforementioned perception check. See invisibility does not reveal the wall, though true seeing does. Detect magic reveals the presence of the wall and allows it to be identified.

The wall need not be vertical or supported by any existing structure when it is created, but each section of the wall does need to be contiguous.

Special: A wall of dispel magic can be made permanent with the permanency spell. To do so requires a minimum caster level of 11 and costs 12,500gp.
spell-wall-of-sorrowful-shadows:
When you cast this spell you summon a curtain of writhing shadow that quickly settles into a disquieting stillness. The wall is pitch black and blocks light passing through in either direction.

Creatures cannot see through the wall unless they possess some way of seeing through magical darkness. Any creature that passes through the wall must make a Will save or be shaken with images of their own failures and shortcomings for 1d6 rounds. Otherwise the wall does not hinder movement in any way.

The wall need not be vertical or supported by any existing structure when it is created, but each section of the wall does need to be contiguous.
spell-war-cry: You unleash a battlecry that causes all creatures within the cone to cower in fear for 1d4 rounds. Any creature that fails their Fortitude save loses their Dexterity bonus to AC and is dazed.
spell-war-song:
You play a song of war with the instrument used as a focus for the spell that fills your enemies with dread.

All enemies within range that can hear the song take a -2 penalty on attack rolls and saving throws.
spell-warp-defenses: You reach out and impact the defenses of the target. The target takes a penalty to their AC and regeneration equal to -2, with an additional -1 penalty for every six levels you have (maximum -5 penalty at 18th level). This spell cannot reduce their AC below 10 + their Dexterity or reduce their regeneration below 0.
spell-warp-defenses-greater: This spell functions as warp defenses except it also reduces damage reduction to a minimum of 0.
spell-warp-defenses-mass: This spell functions as warp defenses except it affects multiple creatures.
spell-warp-defenses-mass-greater: This spell functions as greater warp defenses except it affects multiple creatures.
spell-watcher-in-the-woods:
You have given eyes to the woods so that they may defend you. To cast this spell you carve a seal into the target tree and then grind the knife into bone meal and sprinkle it around the tree.

At the end of the ritual the tree awakens as a treant and will guard an area of 1 square mile centered on its original square. The tree will otherwise treat you as friendly and follow your commands. It will not attack creatures you consider allies or creatures of the animal and plant types except in self defense or directed by you as a standard action.

While the treant is animate you may focus to use its senses. You spend a standard action to begin doing so and may share senses with the treant until you wish for the effect to end or the spell ends. You cannot give commands to the treant while using its senses but you may cast the spells message and read magic through its sight.
spell-waves-of-sickness: You create a burst of horrid stench in front of you causing the creatures within eyes to water and insides to wretch. Subjects wracked by this stench must make a Fortitude save or be nauseated. On each of their turns they may attempt a new save against this effect as a move action. Success ends the effect but the target is sickened for 1 round.
spell-weakness: You inflict a minor curse on the target causing it to be more susceptible to harm, imposing a -1 penalty on saves.
spell-weakness-greater: This spell functions as weakness except as noted above and the resistance bonus to saves is increased to +3.
spell-weakness-greater-mass: This spell functions as greater weakness except as noted above.
spell-weakness-mass: This spell functions as weakness except as noted above.
spell-weakness-superior: This spell functions as weakness except as noted above and the resistance bonus to saves is increased to +6.
spell-weakness-superior-mass: This spell functions as superior weakness except as noted above.
spell-weaponized-loss:
You instill the target creature with an underlying dread that is enhanced when their allies fall around them. The target takes a -1 penalty to Will saves against emotion effects for the duration whether or not they succeed on their saving throw. On a failed saving throw, if an ally of an affected creature is killed, destroyed, or otherwise incapacitated, the affected creature must make another Will save or take a -1 penalty on attack rolls, saving throws, ability checks, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls. This penalty lasts until the end of the spell's duration. On a success the penalty is not imposed, however they will be subject to the Will saving throw the next time an ally is killed, destroyed, or otherwise incapacitated.

If the target witnesses an illusion of a triggering event, they must make a Will save or believe their ally is lost and take a heightened penalty.

If a target creature is affected by the -1 penalty to all their rolls and another falls, the penalty increases to -2 unless they make another saving throw. The next time, the penalty increases to -4. Once the penalty has reached -4, it does not increase any further.

If their ally is revived, awakened, brought back into the fight, or shown to be not lost in the case of an illusion, the penalty is reduced by one step.
spell-where-the-light-dies:
This spell functions as deeper darkness but any light source, magical or otherwise, is snuffed out. All non-magical light sources are extinguished, and all magical light sources are automatically subject to a targeted dispel check as per the spell dispel magic. This includes any such light source brought into the area of darkness.

Additionally, the darkness is so deep even creatures with the see in darkness ability can only see 10 feet around them and anything more than 5 feet away has concealment.

This spell does not stack with itself or other darkness spells. Where the light dies can be used to counter or dispel any light spell of equal or lower spell level.
spell-whirlwind-smite: This spell allows you to strike multiple foes with a single smite attack. When you cast this spell you also expend a use of your smite class ability and make an attack roll against each enemy in your threatened area. Each attack gains any bonuses from your smite.
spell-whirlwind-strike: With a flourish you channel the swiftness of the wind into your blade. After casting this spell you make a single attack at your highest base attack bonus against each enemy within reach. If you move after casting this spell you do not provoke attacks of opportunity from any creature hit by one of these attacks.
spell-wind-bind:
Calling out to the elemental forces of air you grasp at and bind a foe. When you cast this spell your target must make a Reflex saving throw or be entangled by air and suspended up to 10 feet above the ground.

While entangled in this way the target must make concentration checks to cast spells with a DC equal to this spells save DC + the level of the spell being cast, in addition any sounds the creature makes are drowned out by the binding winds and cannot be heard by others.
spell-wolfs-aspect: You invest the ferocity of the wolf into your target, granting them a bestial aspect. While under the effects of this spell your target becomes more bestial in appearance. Growing a large jaw, thick fur and gnashing teeth, your type changes to animal and you gain a primary bite attack which deals 1d6 damage. In addition when the affected creature deals damage with the bite attack they may make a free trip attempt without provoking an attack of opportunity.
spell-wooden-hands:
You transform the target's hands into wooden carvings.

While this spell is in effect the target is unable to manipulate, grasp, or release items. If they have no weapon equipped they can use, they gain a 1d6 slam attack. The target's Cmd against disarm increases by 5. However, their hands are susceptible to spells that affect wood, like warp wood. At the end of the spell, the target's hands return to normal, including any changes to the wood caused by other effects.
spell-words-of-the-forest:
The casters taps into the nature around them, connecting to the fauna allowing them to see flashes of the memories of the forest. By focusing on specific areas or topics, the target can see the past in that area or learn secrets that the forest has learned.

Each round for the duration of the spell, the target can attempt a Perception or Handle Animal check to learn about people or events within or in the forest or view glimpses of other locations within the forest. The check is treated as if using Diplomacy to gather information from local people for 1d4 hours, but instead learns information from the animals and plants of the location. While concentrating on this spell, the user is blind and deaf.
spell-wracking-sobs: You cause the target to be wracked with debilitating sobs and torrents of tears. For the duration of the spell, the target is sickened and blinded. A successful Will save negates the effect entirely.
spell-aberrant-form: The caster transforms a willing creature into an aberration. Its form shifts into a hideous mockery of its natural state. The creature's type changes to aberration, and it gains a +1 natural armor bonus to AC for every four levels the caster has, up to a maximum of +5. While the spell persists the target also takes a penalty to Diplomacy checks a bonus on Intimidate checks equal to the bonus granted to natural armor.
spell-absorb-mind:
When casting this spell the caster consumes a portion of another creature's corpse, usually the brain. When they do, they gain a limited view of the creature's memories and knowledge gaining a 50% chance of recalling any important fact known to that creature such as it's family history, recent events, the general layout of its hometown or home, how the creature died, and other important pieces of information like passwords or hidden items of importance. Skills, feats, spells, and other such knowledge cannot be obtained in this fashion.

Once the caster rolls to determine whether they recall a fact, they cannot attempt to recall that same fact again. Once per minute while the spell persists the caster can roll to recall a different piece of information. After the duration expires, the caster no longer has the ability to recall new facts. The flesh must be from a creature that died no more than one week prior to the casting of the spell.
spell-absorb-strength:
The caster consumes a portion of another creature's flesh as they finish this spell, gaining one quarter of the creature's Strength score as an enhancement bonus to their Strength score, and one-quarter of the creature's Constitution score as an enhancement bonus to their Constitution score.

The flesh must be from a creature that died no more than one week prior to the casting of the spell. The caster can gain a bonus to either score of no more than 1/2 their caster level from this spell.
spell-amanuensis:
You cause writing to be copied from one source to another. For example you could copy a book into a blank book. The spell copies one page per minute and creates a perfect duplicate though it is written in your handwriting. This spell copies only non-magical text. So any magical writing (such as spellbooks or scrolls), sigils (such as a sepia snake sigil) or illustrations are left as blank spaces on the page. This spell will trigger rune, sigil and symbol spells (if applicable) even if it does not copy them.

A blank medium (paper, parchment or book) must be provided for the spell to write upon. The spell will automatically turn pages of the source material and the destination medium for copying, if applicable. If there are insufficient blank pages for copying, you are alerted by a light pinging in your head and the spell stops copying until more blank material is provided. At any time, you may change sources or destinations of the copying.

This spell will not translate the text being copied. If you do not understand the original, you cannot understand the copied text.
spell-analyze-portal:
You can detect whether there is a magic portal or a gate spell within the area. If you study the area for 1 round you know the size and locations of the portals in the area. Once you find a portal, you can then study it to find more information. You can only study one portal at a time if there are more than one in the area.

With each round of study you gain one piece of information in this order:

This perspective uses your own unaided vision as if you were standing on the other end of the portal. This does not allow you to use other divination spells through this vision. This glimpse lasts only 1 round.

For each property, you must make a caster level check equal to the caster level of the portal or gate effect. If you fail you may attempt the check again the next round.

This spell has only a minor ability to determine other portal effects as follows:
spell-antagonize: You call out an insult charged with infuriating power. The target takes 1d4 damage per caster level (maximum 10d4). Additionally, the target must make an attack against a target of your choosing, using their attack of opportunity in the process. On a successful saving throw the target takes half damage and does not make the attack.
spell-arcane-scourge:
You tap into the latent arcane energies in an area and enhance them to your benefit. You cause an area within range to become animated with arcane energies. Each effect has an amount of space within the area that can be affected and a space can only have one effect. SR is checked per effect.

Arcane Vortex: At the beginning of your turn, any creature within 5 feet of the vortex area takes 3d6 force damage. A successful Fortitude save halves this damage. You may place up to 2, 5-foot cubes of this effect within the area.

Air of Slumber: Any creature beginning their turn in or passing through an area with this effect must make a Will save or be affected as per the sleep spell except there is no HD limit. You may place up to 4, 5-foot cubes of this effect within the area.

Dilated Time: Any area within the affected area that is affected by this time dilation is treated as difficult terrain for enemies, or increase the speed of yourself or allies by 5 feet while passing through the area. You may place up to 8, 5-foot cubes of this effect within the area.

Storm Front: Any creature beginning their turn in or passing through an area with this effect takes 3d4 electricity damage. A successful Reflex save halves this damage. Additionally, as a swift action, you may launch a bolt of lighting at a target within 10 feet of one of these areas. If you succeed on a ranged touch attack, the target takes 3d4 electricity damage. You may place up to 2 5-foot cubes of this effect.
spell-arrow-salvo: You conjure an massive version of the ranged weapon used as a focus that launches a salvo of attacks into an area. All creatures within the area must make a Reflex save or take 1d10 damage per 2 levels to a maximum of 10d10 at 20th caster level. The damage dealt by this spell matches the base damage type of the weapon used but is considered magic for the purposes of damage reduction. A successful Reflex save halves this damage. If the target fails their Reflex save by 10 or more, they are knocked prone in addition to the damage.
spell-arrow-trap: You place up to 1 piece of ammunition per caster level on the ground and charge them with magic energy to ward an area. You are not affected by this spell and when casting the spell you may designate any number of individuals that are also exempted from the spell. When any other creature enters within 30 feet of the pile of ammunition or begins their turn in the area, a piece of the ammunition shoots up and toward the target and you make a ranged attack. If the attack hits it deals 1d6 plus your spellcasting modifier in damage. The damage type is the same normally dealt by the ammunition but is also considered magic for damage reduction purposes. If the attack is triggered, the ammunition is lost. The spell ends when all the ammunition places is expended. This spell does not function with magical ammunition like slaying arrows.
spell-ash-cloud:
You summon a roiling cloud of ash and smoke in the area. The cloud is difficult terrain for flying creatures due to the shifting temperatures but it does not cause concealment. However, it is impossible to use scent within the area.

When a creature ends their turn within the area of the smoke, they must make a Fortitude save or be nauseated for 1 round from smoke inhalation and take 1d4 fire damage from the burning ash in the lungs. On a success, the creature is only sickened for 1 round. If a creature does not need to breathe or if they are immune to fire damage, they are immune to these effects.
spell-aspect-of-the-hope-devourer:
Your presence saps the hope and joy from your enemies. A creature that fails a save against this spell paralyzed by unbearable despair and hopelessness. A flying creature may continue to hover while paralyzed by this effect and if they cannot hover, they immediately land but are otherwise paralyzed. These creatures are paralyzed for the duration of the spell.

Each round on its turn, a target of this spell may attempt a new saving throw to end the effect; this is a full-round action that does not provoke attacks of opportunity. A creature that recovers from this spell early after being affected by it for at least 1 round takes 1d6 points of Wisdom drain and is hopeless for 1d4 rounds. A creature that makes the initial save to resist this spell is merely hopeless for 1 round.
spell-aura-of-consumption:
When you cast the spell and each round at the beginning of your turn, you consume the ebbing life force from surrounding creatures within 30 feet, and use it to fuel your own power. Any creature in the area of the emanation that has -1 or fewer hit points must make its saving throw or die, and you gain 1d8 temporary hit points and a +2 bonus to Strength for each death caused by this spell until the spell's duration expires.

Additionally your effective caster level increases by one per death caused up to a maximum of half your unmodified caster level. This bonus improves the effects of spells cast and does not grant you access to more spells.

No creature can be affected by this spell more than once per casting, regardless of the number of rounds they are exposed to the aura.
spell-aura-of-impurity:
You create a foul aura out to 30 feet that moves with you. Any enemy in or entering the aura, must make a Will save. On a failed save the creature takes a -4 penalty on saves vs. diseases and poisons, and effects that cause the blinded, deafened, despairing, doubting, hopeless, shaken, frightened, panicked, paralyzed and stunned conditions while within the aura. If the creature is normally immune to one or more of the effects, the immunity is suppressed while in the aura though they do not suffer the -4 penalty on a save vs. that condition. On a successful save, the creature is immune to the aura for the duration of the spell.

Note: The despairing, doubting and hopeless conditions are detailed here.
spell-aura-of-purity: You create a soothing aura out to 30 feet that moves with you. Any ally in the aura, including yourself, is immune to non-magical disease and poison and gains a +4 sacred bonus on saves vs. magical diseases and poisons, and spells or effects that cause the blinded, deafened, despairing, doubting, hopeless, shaken, frightened, panicked, paralyzed and stunned conditions. This does not remove or suppress conditions, poisons or diseases already present on an ally upon entering the aura.
spell-awaken-entropy:
You draw upon the awesome power of entropy and vastly accelerate the decay and death in a burst of dark energy. Creatures and objects within begin to age, degrade and rot rapidly. Any creature that begins their turn within the area of the spell takes 4d6 damage + 1 point per caster level even if their bodies, souls or forms are normally immune to the ravages of time. A successful Fortitude save halves this damage.

Each round you concentrate on this spell you may either move the area of the spell by up to 20 feet, or increase its potency. When increasing the potency of the effect, the radius it affects increases by 10 feet (to a maximum of 40 feet), and the damage dice it deals increases by one step (from d6 to d8, then d10, and finally to d12).
spell-awaken-undead:
This spell grants intelligence to mindless undead such as skeletons and zombies. Undead creatures with Intelligence scores are unaffected. A mindless undead gains an Intelligence score of 1d6+4, subject to the limitation that it cannot become more intelligent than a typical living creature of the same kind. For example, an animal skeleton would simply have an Intelligence of 2 (no roll needed), while an orc may make a die roll but not exceed 8.

The newly awakened undead regains any proficiencies and abilities they had in life.

Additionally the awakened undead gains an additional +2 channel resistance. This bonus stacks with their normal channel resistance.
spell-beacon-of-life: You conjure a great beacon of light in a 5 foot square anywhere in the area, even up off the ground. The beacon maintains its position for the duration of the spell. It exudes sunlight in a 60 foot sphere dispelling any darkness effect in its area, it creates normal light out 30 additional feet and dim light for 30 feet further. Any ally that enters the sphere of daylight or begins their turn in the light heals 3d8 points of damage. Any undead creature not destroyed or already damaged by the sunlight is dealt 3d8 points of damage. The light affects a creature only once per round even if they leave and reenter the daylight area. Additionally, the beacon grants immunity to despair effects to allies in the 60 foot sphere. Any ally currently affected by a despair effect has its effects suppressed while in the 60 foot sphere.
spell-binding-ice:
A frigid cone bursts forth freezing those within.
